author: mrtitaniumj
body:
💡 **What:** 
Reordered the conditions used to filter DOM nodes inside Puppeteer's `page.evaluate` context in both `index.js` and `linkedinClient.js`. Added fast geometric checks (`scrollHeight > clientHeight + 80` and `offsetWidth > 0`) *before* calling the expensive `window.getComputedStyle(element)` method.

🎯 **Why:** 
Calling `window.getComputedStyle` forces the browser to calculate the final styles for an element, which is computationally expensive, especially when iterating over a large `NodeList` generated by `document.querySelectorAll('*')`. By short-circuiting these checks with fast, built-in properties, we significantly reduce the CPU overhead and memory allocation required during DOM traversal.

📊 **Impact:** 
Drastically reduces the number of times `window.getComputedStyle` is called. For example, during scrolling, only elements large enough to scroll will have their styles computed, bypassing 99% of nodes on a typical page. This makes the script execute faster and consume less CPU in the Puppeteer environment.

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Run `npm test` to ensure existing utilities haven't broken. The optimization is isolated to the `page.evaluate` blocks and avoids any side effects by maintaining identical selection logic. Also logged in `.jules/bolt.md` to avoid similar regressions in the future.

author: voces
body:
Gives `.vl` files syntax highlighting on GitHub. VL isn't a Linguist-recognized language and can't easily become one, so we map `.vl` to the closest existing grammar via a `.gitattributes` override.

## Mechanism
GitHub Linguist's [`.gitattributes` overrides](https://github.com/github-linguist/linguist/blob/main/docs/overrides.md): `linguist-language=<Name>` reclassifies an extension for both highlighting **and** the repo language-stats bar (they can't be separated by that one attribute). Pairing `linguist-detectable=false` keeps the highlighting but excludes `.vl` from the stats bar, so it won't inflate the TypeScript percentage.

```gitattributes
*.vl linguist-language=TypeScript
*.vl linguist-detectable=false
```

## Why TypeScript
Catalogued VL's real syntax from the self-host sources (`lexer.vl`/`parser.vl`/`typecheck.vl`) + the test corpus, then compared TypeScript/Swift/Kotlin/Rust/Go for grammar token-coverage. TypeScript matches on the highest-impact tokens: `function`, `let`/`const`, `type` aliases, `<T>` generics, `A | B` unions, `?.`/`??`, `//`+`///` comments, double-quoted strings, `0x`/`0b`/`0o` + `_` numeric literals, `is`-narrowing, and `{}` object literals. Minor mismatches: VL's char literals `'x'` highlight as strings (TS has no char type), and `elseif`/`to`/`step` fall through as identifiers — cosmetic only. Runner-up **Kotlin** (`fun` vs `function`, divergent object/generics/doc conventions); Swift/Rust/Go ruled out by `func`/`fn`/no-angle-generics and no union syntax.

## Changes
- `.gitattributes` (new) — the override + a comment explaining the choice and how to drop the stats-suppression line if you'd rather `.vl` show in the bar.
- `README.md` — short "GitHub Syntax Highlighting" note recording the decision, runner-up, the stats side-effect, and the Linguist docs link.

Only `.gitattributes` + `README.md` touched; `deno check`/`lint`/`test` unaffected.

author: francescorosciano
body:
## Summary

Implements the five features described in `PROJECT.md` that were specified but missing. All changes are additive — the existing audio → STT → Moss → summary → dashboard pipeline is untouched. **No new dependencies.**

1. **Floor-plan config** — `POST /sessions` accepts an optional `floorplan_url` (validated to http(s), ≤2048 chars); the dashboard renders it behind the node markers.
2. **Recent transcript entries** — the agent keeps a per-node bounded buffer (`backend/transcripts.py`) and attaches recent lines to each published `NodeSummary`; the dashboard detail view shows them (speaker-labeled, XSS-safe via `textContent`).
3. **On-device STT browser node** — `node_client/index.html` gains a *Stream audio* / *On-device STT* mode toggle; STT mode uses the Web Speech API and sends `TranscriptChunk` JSON over the `phontology.transcript` LiveKit text stream. The backend receiver was hardened to read the full stream (`reader.read_all()`) instead of parsing partial chunks.
4. **Linux headless node** — `node_client/headless.py` self-registers via the API for a publish token (no LiveKit secrets on-device), captures the mic with `sounddevice`, and publishes audio to LiveKit (STT deferred to the backend — suitable for Raspberry Pi). Registration has a timeout + fail-fast.
5. **Mobile-responsive dashboard** — `@media (max-width: 768px)` turns the side panel into a bottom sheet and stacks the layout.

Process artifacts: design spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/`) and implementation plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/`) are included. LiveKit JS/Python APIs were verified against live SDK source before coding. An adversarial multi-dimension review pass produced 5 confirmed findings, all fixed (input validation, registration timeout, JWT-grant + 404 test coverage).

## Test plan

Automated (all green locally):
- [x] `uv run pytest` — **36 passed** (models, API endpoints incl. floorplan validation + publish/subscribe token grants + 404s, transcript helpers, headless registration)
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` — clean

- [x] Inline dashboard / node-client module JS passes `node --check`

Needs a real browser + microphone (manual):

**Load Testing Harness Implementation and Documentation:**

author: fuzyll
body:
A user last week complained that we had broken the ability to build the API and some examples with a change we made. It wasn't broken for _us_, since we build in-tree, but customers don't have the rest of our source code.

As it turns out, @CouleeApps wrote a nice little script that lets us test this out-of-tree build process in February 2022 so we wouldn't have this problem. Unfortunately, it appears to have been taken out of our build process pretty quickly because it added a lot of overall time to builds.

I've gone ahead and set up a new nightly process for ensuring we are made aware when we break builds for customers. To do this, I've split the original script @CouleeApps wrote into two–one for us to test in-tree builds with, and one to test out-of-tree builds with. (They were previously both in the same script, so the former would fail with my setup that approximates a customer's environment.)

In the process of doing this, I discovered that the Triage example would no longer build on Windows and the API itself would not build with clang 14 on Ubuntu 22.04. This PR fixes those issues in the quickest and most straight-forward way I could figure out how.

I have separately run a full build with these API changes through CI as well, which has succeeded. Just want someone else to look these over and ensure they look reasonable before I merge them.

author: cboettig
body:
**NCP turned out not to be a seam-bug case** — its hex uses point-based `h3_latlng_to_cell` indexing and never crosses ±180°, and it was already ~1 row/cell (not the assumed "~300 rows/h8"). So this is a **quality re-hex**, not a seam fix.

### The real issue
The legacy build point-binned **2 km World Eckert IV** pixels at **res 8** (finer than the pixels) → coverage gaps + ~1 row per pixel, and the COGs were left in a projected CRS.

### What changed
- **Reproject** both projected 2 km COGs → WGS84 (`NCP_{biod_nathab,only}_4326_cog.tif`); `ncp-reproject.yaml`.
- **Re-hex each at res 7** (matching 2 km) via `cng-datasets raster`, `--hex-resampling mean` (exact_extract) → **gap-free, one row per h7 cell, area-weighted**.

### Live on canonical + STAC + README
- `public-ncp/hex/ncp_biod_nathab/` — 26.1M cells [0,20], 95 h0; `public-ncp/hex/ncp_only/` — 18.6M cells [0,19], 76 h0. One row per h7 (was multi-row/gappy).
- Validation truths (reproject job): biod_nathab mean 5.11 (47.5M px), ncp_only mean 4.52 (28.0M px); hex values within COG bounds.
- STAC: COG assets repointed to WGS84 + `raster:bands`; hex assets res-7 + `h3:*` + `table:columns`; **fixed the wrong "~300 rows per h8 … GROUP BY AVG" note** (it's one row per cell); new README.

Closes the ncp box in #186 (as a quality upgrade — not seam-affected).

author: xrl
body:
Two defects found by the post-merge end-to-end test of #8.

## 1. `fetch-models.sh` skipped 2 of 4 models (closes #17)
`fetch_file()` referenced `$url` without binding `$1` (the `fetch_tar()` helper does). Under `set -euo pipefail` the first call aborted the script *after* the two `.tar.bz2` downloads, silently skipping `silero_vad.onnx` + the 3D-Speaker embedding — so the backend then failed with "models are missing". One-line fix (`local url="$1"`), verified by re-running the helper.

## 2. Far-end diarization over-clustered → now opt-in, off by default (addresses #18)
On a ~13 min webinar the diarizer invented **50+ phantom `Them N`** speakers (the default clustering threshold + the zh-cn 3D-Speaker embedding aren't discriminative on English). The ASR text was fine, but the labels were noise — worse than a single label.

- New `LocalConfig.diarize_far_end` / `CORTI_LOCAL_DIARIZE` (**default off**). Off ⇒ ch1 → single `Speaker::Other("Them")`, exactly like the AWS backend.
- When off, the segmentation + embedding models are **no longer required** (`models::discover` is conditional) — the default local backend needs only Parakeet + VAD.
- Tuning the diarizer (threshold / English embedding) to make it usable remains tracked in #18 (with #14/#15).

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check` + `clippy -D warnings` clean (`--features aws,local` and `local`-only); `cargo test --workspace` green.
- E2e on the same 13-min webinar now yields **one `Them`** (was 50+) and runs ~3× faster (no segmentation/embedding load).
- `fetch-models.sh` re-run downloads all 4 model sets.

author: defactorongse
body:
This PR makes two additions to the payer-well-known-json-example folder:

**1. New endpoint keys in example.json**

Adds `tic_table_of_contents` entries to the endpoints block, following the
existing `{endpoint_type}#{disambiguator}` convention:

    "tic_table_of_contents#issuer-11111": "https://...issuer-a_index.json",
    "tic_table_of_contents#issuer-22222": "https://...issuer-b_index.json"

The disambiguator is the issuer ID rather than a spec version, because a
carrier typically has multiple licensed issuers each publishing a separate
ToC file under the CMS TiC schema.

**2. New README.md**

Documents the structure of the well-known JSON file, explains the dual
use of the # disambiguator convention (spec version for Da Vinci endpoints,
issuer ID for TiC), and describes the discovery problem that TiC entries
solve.

**Why TiC belongs here**

The TiC rule (CMS-1715-F) requires payers to publish machine-readable files
but specifies no standardized discovery path. The .well-known file solves
the same last-mile discovery problem for TiC that it solves for FHIR
endpoints. Raised during the CMS weekly provider directory call, June 2026.

author: kevinzhao658
body:
## Fix: exiting registration signs you out

**Bug:** Phone-OTP verify creates a live Supabase session, and the DB trigger auto-creates an empty `public.users` row — so a half-registered user reads as `isAuthenticated`/`needsRegistration`. Exiting the registration screen only cleared local state and left the Supabase session alive → the user "stayed signed in" with an un-activated account.

**Fix (frontend, `App.tsx`):**
- `SignUpPage onCancel` now `await logout()` (`supabase.auth.signOut`) before clearing pending state + going home → app returns to **signed out**. The empty account stays un-activated, so the user must OTP in again and complete registration to activate.
- Reload-hardening (option a): when `needsRegistration` is true, the redirect effect backfills `pendingSignupToken` from the live session `token` and forces the signup screen — so an incomplete-profile session can't browse as authenticated after a reload. Complete-user sign-in path is untouched.

QA: APPROVED — typecheck+build clean, cancel→session-kill confirmed, no render loop between the two interacting effects, complete-user path unaffected, scope = App.tsx only, no `any`.

author: 2-a-m
body:
## Problem

`domains/buy` charged a user's credits for a domain that was **never registered**. On a live run the buy returned `success: true` and debited **$14.95**, but no domain was registered: the returned zone was `stub-zone-<domain>`, the name resolves to a third-party registrar, and `domains/check` still reports it available afterward.

Root cause: `cloudflare-registrar.ts` (and `cloudflare-dns.ts`) have a dev stub gated only by `ELIZA_CF_REGISTRAR_DEV_STUB=1`, documented as "local dev + integration tests ... without spending money on real registrations." When that flag is set in **production**, the stub returns fake successes. The buy route (`v1/apps/[id]/domains/buy/route.ts`) debits credits **before** registering and only refunds when the registrar **throws** (catch -> `refundCredits` -> 502). A stub success never throws, so the refund never fires and the caller is charged for nothing. (`ensureConfigured` already fails correctly when the stub is *off* and creds are missing — the whole failure mode is the stub running in prod.)

## Fix

Make the dev stub **fail closed in production**, matching the existing footgun guards in `deployment-environment.ts` (`shouldBlockDevnetBypass`, `shouldBlockUnsafeWebhookSkip`):

- add `shouldBlockRegistrarStub(env)` = `ELIZA_CF_REGISTRAR_DEV_STUB === "1" && isProductionDeployment(env)`
- `cloudflare-registrar.ts` and `cloudflare-dns.ts` `config()` throw when it returns true

The throw happens per request inside `config()`, which the buy flow hits in `checkAvailability()` **before** any credit debit — so a misconfigured production fails loudly with **no charge** instead of silently faking registrations. Dev/test/staging (`NODE_ENV=test`, `ENVIRONMENT != production`) keep using the stub unchanged, so the cloud-e2e `monetized-app-loop` suite is unaffected.

## Tests

- `deployment-environment.test.ts` — `shouldBlockRegistrarStub` blocks only when the flag is on **and** in production (via `ENVIRONMENT` or `NODE_ENV`), allows dev/test/staging, and is off when the flag is unset.
- `cloudflare-registrar.test.ts` — the registrar **throws** when the stub flag is set with `ENVIRONMENT=production`, and still serves stub data outside production.

`bun test` (cloud-shared): 7/7 pass. Diff is additive only (no reformatting).

## Note for operators

Production should also **unset `ELIZA_CF_REGISTRAR_DEV_STUB`** and configure real `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` / `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`; until real creds exist, domain buys should fail rather than fake-succeed. A latent follow-up (out of scope here): the buy route keeps the debit on an async "pending" registration that later fails — it only refunds on a synchronous throw.

author: simonw
body:
<details><summary>PR description by Claude Code for Web (Opus 4.8)</summary>

This PR introduces `datasette-agent-edit`, a new package providing storage-agnostic file-editing tools for Datasette Agent plugins. The package is organized into three architectural layers:

## Summary

The package extracts and generalizes file-editing functionality to work with any storage backend (SQLite, filesystem, S3, GitHub, etc.) while maintaining a consistent JSON API for Datasette Agent integration.

## Key Changes

**Layer 1: Pure Operations** (`operations.py`)
- Pure, synchronous string-editing primitives: `view_lines`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `apply_edits`
- No I/O, no async, no Datasette dependencies
- Custom `EditError` and `EditApplyError` exceptions for edit validation

**Layer 2: Storage Abstraction** (`store.py`)
- `EditStore` protocol defining the backend interface with atomic `edit(ref, transform)` method
- `Editable` dataclass representing content snapshots with metadata and versioning
- `IdCodec` and `PrefixCodec` for mapping between internal refs and external IDs
- `NotFound` and `Conflict` exceptions for error handling

**Layer 3: Agent Tools** (`toolset.py`)
- `EditToolset` class wrapping any `EditStore` as Datasette Agent tools
- Five tools: `view`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `edit` (batch), and optional `render`
- Consistent JSON envelope with configurable field names and descriptions
- Two extension points: `id_codec` for ID translation and `render` hook for presentation

**Storage Backends**
- `SqliteVersionedStore`: Versioned storage with full history, atomic writes via `execute_write_fn`
- `DiskStore`: Filesystem-backed storage with per-file metadata sidecars, atomic `os.replace` writes

**Tests** (`test_operations.py`, `test_stores.py`, `test_toolset.py`)
- Comprehensive test coverage for all three layers
- Parameterized tests validating both SQLite and disk backends against the `EditStore` contract
- End-to-end toolset tests with ID codecs and render hooks

## Notable Implementation Details

- The `transform` parameter in `EditStore.edit()` is intentionally synchronous and pure, allowing it to run safely inside any backend's critical section (SQLite write thread, file lock, S3 compare-and-set loop)
- Batch edits are all-or-nothing: if any edit fails, nothing is persisted
- The render hook is optional; omitting it disables the `*_render` tool and simplifies edit responses
- Version tokens are opaque and backend-defined (incrementing integers for SQLite, mtime for disk)

</details>

author: atimothee
body:
Rescues the product against the core complaints: it now reads ~500 emails and emits a short, color-coded list of **decisions**, with **all** intelligence in the Node sidecar.

## What changed
- **All AI in the sidecar, via `@openai/agents` only.** No direct OpenAI REST calls from the extension, no client-side heuristics. Sidecar returns `{clutter, decisions}` over SSE. The OpenAI key from Settings is forwarded to the sidecar (or `server/.env`).
- **Sidecar is required.** If unreachable / no key, the extension throws `SidecarError` and the UI shows a clear error state (Today + Cleanup) and a red pulse — no silent fallback.
- **Synthesis, not selection.** New `Decision` unit folds N emails into one. The sidecar collapses related mail, omits newsletters/promos/notifications, and returns a short ranked list; Today renders `DecisionCard`s (capped, theme-clustered, "Nothing pressing today" when empty).
- **No more dumb labels.** A bank statement is no longer a "payment reminder"; a marketing "Hi {city}" no longer "needs a reply"; senders resolve to real names (never "noreply"). Verified end-to-end against the live sidecar.
- **Cleanup** aggregates by theme with real unsubscribe/mute CTAs.
- **Honest scan lifecycle.** Deep scroll-scan to ~500 emails (position restored); real reading→thinking→done/error states replace the fake spinner; the pulse no longer says "All done" mid-run.
- **Color** used meaningfully (per-theme tints), confidence shown as a soft fill not a %.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` (src + evals + server) clean
- `npm run evals` green (safety, memory, handoffs, sender resolution)
- `npm run build` succeeds
- Sidecar boots; live `/orchestrate/classify` smoke test returns correct decisions + clutter (statement→clutter not payment; personal note→reply decision; promo→unsubscribe)

author: chriscrosstalk
body:
## Problem

Kiwix runs in library mode reading `kiwix-library.xml` (via `--monitorLibrary`). A missing or corrupt library XML is currently only repaired on the **download path** (`rebuildFromDisk` after a completed download). If the file is lost or truncated *outside* that flow — storage relocation (#938), an interrupted write, manual deletion — Kiwix comes up serving an **empty library with no path to recovery** until the next download happens to trigger a rebuild.

## Fix

Add `KiwixLibraryService.ensureLibraryXmlHealthy()`:
- Reads the library XML. If missing (`ENOENT`) or it fails to parse / lacks a `<library>` root, rebuilds it from the ZIM files on disk.
- A well-formed but empty library is treated as valid (no spurious rebuild).
- Filesystem errors other than `ENOENT` are re-thrown rather than masked by a rebuild.

The Kiwix migration boot provider calls it on the already-in-library-mode path, so a broken library is recovered at startup.

## Notes

Reuses the service's existing parser config and `rebuildFromDisk()`. Builds on the idea raised in #733, reimplemented in-house (separates missing vs. invalid, avoids rebuilding a valid-but-empty library, and surfaces real fs errors).

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- Logic-only; the rebuild path itself is the same `rebuildFromDisk()` already exercised by the download flow.

## What this does
Validates **every** operator path end-to-end through real generation, fixes what was broken, adds the missing **composition (combine outputs)** capability, and closes the **self-improvement** loop. All findings were surfaced by actually running Liminal (dogfooding), and each generation now feeds learning.

### Routing & providers
- **Domain routing** — `detectPromptDomain` + `run()` now forwards `collabDomain` to `RalphLoop`, so all 13 domains route generation **and** validation correctly (was: every `--prompt` defaulted to p5).
- **Easy MiniMax-M3 key** — `liminal provider set-key minimax <KEY> --use` writes the international endpoint + model MiniMax-M3 and activates it.

### Per-domain fixes (found by all-domains testing)
- **revideo** — allowlist rejected standard `@revideo` exports (easings, `LinearGradient`, flow helpers); crash → 0.75.
- **tone / strudel (audio)** — scored 0.00 because the loop scored them via headless **visual** render (silence). Route audio domains to code-based scoring → tone 0.93, strudel 1.00. Also: the final validation gate now validates by known domain (a short Strudel pattern was misdetected as ASCII → crash).
- **p5** — `P5_GLOBALS` was partial and rejected valid sketches using `clear()`, `arc()`, 3D, input events, etc. Expanded to the common p5 surface.

- `compose` records a generation episode; `consolidate` now `initialize()`s before reading, so it loads **1383 generation episodes** (this session's domain tests + compositions) and compresses them into **23 learned patterns**. (Idempotent with PR #591.)

author: kmay89
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the optional-feature gating (#735). Two more off-by-default features had **no CI compile gate**, and probing them confirmed the risk was real:

- **`ingest-v4l2` was structurally broken** — 32 compile errors from un-migrated `v4l` 0.14 / `ouroboros` 0.18 bumps (same "bump without source migration" pattern as the tract and ureq breakages).
- **`rtsp-gstreamer`** compiled but carried never-linted clippy violations.

## Fixes

**`ingest-v4l2` (`src/ingest/v4l2.rs`)**
- `v4l` 0.14: `MmapStream` dropped its device type param → `MmapStream<'this>`.
- `with_buffers(dev: &Device, …)` takes a shared ref, so the `#[self_referencing]` field now borrows the device immutably (`#[borrows(device)]`).
- `ouroboros` 0.18: fallible self-referencing builds use the generated **`…TryBuilder`** struct (`DeviceV4l2StateTryBuilder`), not `Builder::try_build`.
- clippy 1.95 in the now-compiled code: `checked_div`, `is_multiple_of`, `is_some()`, `inspect_err`, and removal of an orphaned dead helper (`should_skip_connect`, never called).
- The synthetic `stub://` unit tests pass (4/4). The real device path can't be exercised without V4L2 hardware, but it now compiles and is clippy-clean.

**`rtsp-gstreamer` (`src/ingest/rtsp.rs`)**
- Removed two `unnecessary_cast` (`u32 -> u32`) casts in `sample_to_pixels` (gstreamer-only fn; `rtsp-ffmpeg` unaffected).

## CI (`rust.yml`)
- Added `ingest-v4l2` to the existing **optional-features** job — the `v4l` crate builds and links with no system library.
- Added an **ingest-gstreamer** job that installs the GStreamer dev libraries and clippy-gates `rtsp-gstreamer`.

## Verification
Installed the exact CI toolchain (1.95.0) and the GStreamer dev libs; `cargo +1.95.0 clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean for **both** `ingest-v4l2` and `rtsp-gstreamer`. Default build and `rtsp-ffmpeg` (shares `rtsp.rs`) both still compile clean; fmt clean.

---

⚠️ **Separate heads-up:** **#734** (the Detect Eval YAML startup-failure fix) appears **not merged** — `detect-eval.yml` on `main` still has the unquoted `run: cargo test --lib eval::`, so that workflow is still startup-failing. Worth merging #734 to get Detect Eval green.

author: risky-scout
body: ## Root Cause Every `Train & Calibrate Model` job in the workflow has been failing with `halted_reason: training_failed`. The failure chain is: 1. `run_nightly_training_and_calibration.py` calls `train_daily_challenger_model.py` 2. `train_daily_challenger_model.py` calls `calibrate_pmf.py --aggregate-mode` 3. `calibrate_pmf.py` completes calibration, then hits `_fit_final_calibrators_and_emit_report()` which references `_fold_dirs` 4. **`NameError: name '_fold_dirs' is not defined`** — `_fold_dirs` is a local variable in `main()` but `_fit_final_calibrators_and_emit_report()` is a separate module-level function and cannot see `main()`'s local scope 5. `calibrate_pmf.py` exits with non-zero code 6. `train_daily_challenger_model.py` raises `RuntimeError` 7. `run_nightly_training_and_calibration.py` sets `halted_reason: training_failed` This is a Python scoping bug. The `_fit_final_calibrators_and_emit_report()` function was added as a standalone module-level function but still referenced `_fold_dirs` as if it were a closure over `main()`. ## Fix - Added `fold_dirs: list[Path] | None = None` parameter to `_fit_final_calibrators_and_emit_report()` - Aggregate-mode call site passes `fold_dirs=[]` (no per-fold temp dirs) - Non-aggregate call site passes `fold_dirs=_fold_dirs` (actual fold directories) - Inside the function, uses `fold_dirs or []` to handle None safely ## Impact This fix unblocks every nightly training run. Without it, the model retrains via Phase 13 (contextual) only — which works separately — but the base calibration job always shows red in GitHub Actions. This bug was present before the PR #66 calibration changes. The `per_stat_weights` additions from yesterday do not introduce any new scoping issues (verified via AST analysis). ## Verification ```bash python3 -m py_compile scripts/calibrate_pmf.py # passes # AST confirms _fold_dirs is no longer referenced bare in _fit_final_calibrators_and_emit_report() ```

body: ## Summary Critical bug investigation on PR #40 found two high-severity issues in recent commits and fixes them with minimal changes. ## Bug 1 — Orphan recovery races active cross-tab registration **Impact:** Profile corruption, wrong username assignment, and potential field loss when a second tab runs orphan recovery while signup is still in progress. **Root cause:** `waitForCrossTabRegistration` broke after a fixed 120s wall-clock deadline even when `register()` heartbeats kept the cross-tab registration flag fresh. Tab B then cleared the flag and provisioned a default profile while Tab A was still completing signup. **Fix:** - Wait until the heartbeat flag goes stale naturally (no wall-clock cap that fights refreshed `startedAt`). - Skip orphan recovery when `isRegistrationInProgress(uid)` is still true after waiting. ## Bug 2 — Import duplicate detection silently truncated at 100 places **Impact:** Lists with 101+ places could re-import existing entries because PR #35 paginated `getListPlaces` but Google Maps import still used it for dedup. **Root cause:** `useGoogleMapsImport` called `getListPlaces`, which returns only the first page (100 docs). **Fix:** Add `PlaceService.getAllListPlaces()` (paginated) and use it for import duplicate checks. ## Validation - `npm test` — 22 tests passed - `npm run check:types` — passed ## PR #40 review note PR #40’s AI search and bulk-import batch limit fixes look correct; no additional critical issues found in that diff.

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary
Adds the Session 10 end-to-end **integration tests (pytest)** and **load tests (k6)** for the multi-tenant SaaS platform, entirely under a new `saas/tests/` directory. Tests target the platform's documented HTTP contracts (services owned by Sessions 1–9) through the API gateway.

Three hard design constraints drove the structure:
1. **Collect cleanly on a bare checkout** — `pytest --collect-only` succeeds with no stack, no docker, no model assets.
2. **Skip, never error, when the stack is down** — every stack-dependent test is guarded; an absent gateway yields *skipped*, and individual steps a partial deployment `404`s are skipped too, so the suite stays green as Sessions 1–9 land incrementally.
3. **Still run meaningful logic locally** — privacy enforcement, pack-signature verification, key-rotation grace logic, and corpus/verdict normalization are exercised against synthetic data with no stack.

Current local result: **21 passed, 12 skipped** (stack not running); `ruff check` clean; `--collect-only` clean.

## What's here
- `saas_testkit.py` — shared helpers: env-driven `ServiceConfig`, reachability probes (skip guards), sample-corpus loader, `PrivacyScanner`, and a bridge onto the repo's existing manifest verifier.
- `conftest.py` — fixtures: optional `docker compose up --wait`/`down -v` lifecycle (`SAAS_MANAGE_STACK=1`), health waits, isolated `test_tenant` with teardown.
- 7 pytest modules + 3 k6 scripts + `README.md` + `requirements.txt` + `ruff.toml`.

Most modules are split into a **self-test layer** (synthetic data, always runs) and a **live layer** (skips without the stack):

| Concern | Self-test layer (always runs) | Live layer (skips when stack down) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Privacy contract | `PrivacyScanner` flags raw text, >8-token verbatim echoes, message-id/sender/group keys, hash/embedding blobs; allows ≤8-token quotes + opaque tenant ids | scans real classifier/telemetry/appeal payloads |
| Pack distribution | sign→verify round-trip + tamper/unpinned-key rejection via the repo's `manifest_verifier` | upload→SHA-256→download→signature→ETag 304→rollback |
| Key rotation | grace-period **trust store** modelled on the single-key verifier (old accepted during grace, rejected after) | `/v1/keys/rotate` + trust-store status assertions |
| Classification parity | corpus loads/in-taxonomy + `ux_action` precedence normalizer | server API vs. on-device sidecar verdict triples |
| Tenant lifecycle / isolation / rate-limit | — | full lifecycle; jurisdiction divergence; per-tenant 429 + cross-tenant isolation |

## Privacy enforcement (automated, not aspirational)
`PrivacyScanner` recursively walks any JSON payload and reports violations of the 8 immutable rules. Key nuance — opaque id fields are allow-listed so a 32-char hex *tenant id* isn't mistaken for a message hash:
```python
ALLOWED_OPAQUE_ID_KEYS = {"tenant_id", "event_id", "appeal_id", "request_id", ...}
# rule 4: forbid any (MAX_VERBATIM_TOKENS+1)=9-gram copied from a source message
# rule 5: forbid hash/embedding key names, hex>=32 / base64>=24 blobs, float vectors>=8
```

## Signatures use the repo's existing scheme
Pack manifests are verified through the existing `build-tools/cv_guard_shared/manifest/manifest_verifier.py` (canonical-JSON-preimage → ed25519 with declared-key pin), so the suite can't drift from production verification.

## k6 load targets (encoded as `thresholds`)
- `classify.js`: 5,000 tenants × 10 req/s = 50k req/s, **p95 < 250 ms** (matches `build-tools/compiler/benchmark.py::P95_LATENCY_TARGET_MS`).
- `ingest.js`: 5,000 tenants × 100-event batches, sustained **≥ 50k events/s** (gate = `count >= TARGET_EPS * duration_seconds`).
- `pack-download.js`: 5,000 simultaneous downloads complete **< 30 s**; repeat GETs return **304** via ETag (`cached_304` rate > 99 %).

## How to run/test locally
```bash
pip install -r saas/tests/requirements.txt
cd saas/tests
pytest                 # 21 pass, 12 skip when stack is down
pytest --collect-only  # clean on a bare checkout
ruff check .           # clean (inherits root ruleset via ruff.toml `extend`)
# load tests (needs k6); scale down for a smoke run:
TENANTS=50 RPS_PER_TENANT=2 DURATION=15s k6 run saas/tests/load/classify.js
```
Point at a live stack via `SAAS_GATEWAY_URL` / `SAAS_DEVICE_URL` (or `SAAS_MANAGE_STACK=1` to drive docker-compose). All endpoint/jurisdiction assumptions are env-overridable — see `saas/tests/README.md`.

## Devin Review fixes (commit `acb9c9f`)
Confirmed each flagged item before changing code; fixed the genuine bugs with root-cause fixes and documented the non-issues:
- **Privacy scanner base64 detection (real bug):** used `re.fullmatch`, which missed *padded* (`...==`) and *embedded* base64 — the base64 leak check was effectively dead. Switched to `re.search`; added `test_scanner_flags_base64_blob_standalone_and_embedded` as a regression guard.
- **Tenant cleanup leaks (real bug, ×2):** in `test_multi_tenant_isolation` and `test_rate_limiting`, a failure in the *second* `_create_tenant` leaked the first. Now each id is registered for teardown immediately after creation.
- **Ingest SLO gate too lenient (real bug):** threshold required only `TARGET_EPS` total events regardless of duration (~60× too lenient for a 1m run). Now `count >= TARGET_EPS * duration_seconds` via a k6 duration parser; counts only 2xx-accepted events so a backed-up path fails.
- **Tautological pack-signature pin:** split **integrity** (always verify the signature over the canonical preimage vs the declared key) from the **supply-chain pin** (only enforced against a *trusted* key from `SAAS_PINNED_PUBKEY` or `/v1/keys/trust-store`), skipping the pin assertion rather than self-verifying. Pin-rejection remains covered by the always-on `test_reference_verifier_rejects_unpinned_key`.
- **Parity device client:** now uses `make_client` (fast-connect / generous-request timeout split) for consistency with the gateway client.
- **Reachability probes:** `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` (no-arg probes); confirmed the cache only resolves after `saas_stack` waits for health, so no stale `False`.
- **Top-level-string scan asymmetry:** confirmed intentional (no key context ⇒ no opaque-id exemption ⇒ conservative scan); no change.

## Scope / constraints
Additive only: every file is new and under `saas/tests/`. No existing files modified. The suite is standalone — excluded from the root `pyproject.toml` `testpaths`, with its own `ruff.toml` that `extend`s the root config — so it doesn't collide with the repo's existing test trees.

Link to Devin session: https://uney.devinenterprise.com/sessions/40a6602f977b47d0bb2d7d203bb37cb4
Requested by: @kennguy3n

author: relevant47
body:
## Summary
The v1.2.0 mac self-heal spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-05-mac-daemon-self-heal-design.md`) says the UI should call `status()` before deciding which `SetupRequired` screen to show — so a user who previously approved FocusLock in Login Items and then disabled it lands on the `disabled` screen with the System Settings deep-link, not on the first-run "macOS will ask for your password once" copy. `detectInitialState()` never wired that call up; `daemon_status_macos` was registered in `invoke_handler!` but invoked nowhere.

## Files changed
- `ui/src-tauri/src/macos_daemon.rs` — add `#[serde(tag = "kind")]` to `ServiceStatus` so the JSON shape is `{"kind":"requires_approval"}` etc., matching `RegisterOutcome` which is already tagged. Without this the existing command returned a plain string (`"requires_approval"`) and the suggested-fix `status.kind` check would never match.
- `ui/src/pages/SetupRequired.tsx` — declare a `DaemonStatus` discriminated union, then in `detectInitialState` (after the legacy check) call `daemon_status_macos`, parse, and route `requires_approval` → `disabled`, `not_found` → `tampered`; everything else falls through to `first_run`.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `ui/` passes locally with the added type.
- Diff against the spec edge-case table in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-05-mac-daemon-self-heal-design.md` lines 199 + 142–143 — both rows now have a code path that reaches the documented destination screen.
- Did **not** add Windows-side changes — Windows uses a different install/self-heal path (`try_install_daemon_sync`) and has no equivalent `requires_approval` state.

Fixes #81

## Risk tier
**SECURITY-SENSITIVE / behavioural** — this changes the macOS setup-flow routing and the JSON shape of an existing Tauri command, even though the command was previously dead code. Opening as draft + `needs-review`.

## What a human should verify
1. **No existing callers of `daemon_status_macos`** depended on the un-tagged string shape. Grep confirmed it's invoked nowhere in `ui/src/` before this PR, but please re-confirm before merging.
2. **The four state paths work end-to-end on a real Mac** under SMAppService:
   - Fresh install (no prior register) → still lands on `first_run` (status is `not_registered`).
   - Previously approved, then user disabled in System Settings → Login Items → now lands directly on `disabled` (not `first_run` then `disabled` on the second hop).
   - Bundled plist missing/renamed → lands on `tampered`.
   - `Enabled` but socket not yet up → falls through to `first_run`, which is the most useful fallback (the user can click Enable → register() returns running). This is acceptable because the SetupRequired screen only renders when the socket is unreachable; `Enabled` here is a transient/rare inconsistent state.
3. **Serde tagging on a unit-only enum** — `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]` on `ServiceStatus` produces `{"kind":"not_registered"}` etc. This is the documented serde behaviour for unit variants in internally-tagged enums; no Rust toolchain to compile-test on this runner, so the Tauri/Rust CI gate is the real check.

author: williamthorsen
body:
## What

Consolidates all YAML parsing on a single library, removing a redundant YAML dependency that overlapped with it.

## Why

The repository carried two YAML libraries — `js-yaml` and `yaml` — for the same parsing job. Newer modules had already standardized on `yaml`, but older code and some tests still reached for `js-yaml`, so contributors had to know which one applied where, and the project paid for a redundant dependency.

## Details

### ♻️ Refactoring

- Every YAML-parsing call site in `agents` and `run-core` now goes through `yaml`'s `parse` instead of `js-yaml`'s `load`, spanning three source modules (`frontmatter-merger.ts`, `tool-name-rewriter.ts`, `resolve-base-dir.ts`) and two test files.
- Each call site keeps its existing `isRecord` guard and surrounding error handling, which already absorb the two differences between the libraries: `yaml` returns `null` (not `undefined`) for empty input, and throws a `YAMLParseError` (not a `YAMLException`) on malformed input.
- Comments and a test fixture that named `js-yaml` are refreshed to describe the `yaml` API.

### 📦 Dependencies

- `js-yaml` and its `@types/js-yaml` typings are dropped from both `agents` and `run-core`.
- `run-core` now declares `yaml@2.9.0` (it previously declared only `js-yaml`); `agents` already declared `yaml` at the same version.
- A transitive `js-yaml` remains in the lockfile via unrelated dev tooling, outside the scope of this change.

Closes #734

author: keanji-x
body:
## Summary

Followup to #488 PR2a (PR #511) round-6 finding. The terminal/codex/claude INSERTs in `0030_runtimes_backfill.sql` join `terminals t ON t.card_id = c.id` without checking the inverse stamp. In the legacy multi-step create-crash window this lets the backfill materialize an active runtime for an orphan-shape card; the orphan-terminal sweeper (`db/sqlite.rs:2611-2614`) later deletes the terminal row, and `runtimes.terminal_run_id ON DELETE SET NULL` leaves the runtime permanently active with no backing terminal.

Add `AND json_extract(c.payload, '$.terminal_id') = t.id` to the three terminal-joined INSERTs (shared-spec block has no terminal join — unaffected). Guard SQL is intentionally byte-for-byte the inverse of the sweeper predicate so the sweeper can never delete a terminal the backfill keyed off of.

Per PR3 plan in #488, this migration body becomes vestigial once payload stamps are deleted — the guard is a one-time legacy invariant.

Closes #518.

## Migration checksum impact

This edits an existing migration (`0030_runtimes_backfill.sql`) rather than adding a new one. **Any DB that already applied the previous (buggy) 0030 will fail sqlx checksum validation on next boot** with `MigrateError::VersionMismatch`. Per project state confirmed pre-PR: production neige-app has **not** upgraded through PR #511 yet, so prod is unaffected. Local dev DBs that ran the buggy 0030 need manual repair — either delete the row from `_sqlx_migrations` (sqlx will re-apply the corrected 0030 on next boot) or re-init the dev DB.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p calm-server --test migration_0029_runtimes_backfill` — 3/3 pass (orig + idempotency + new orphan-guard test).
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean.
- [x] Two-channel review: subagent PASS no findings; codex review P1 on checksum impact, explicitly accepted (see "Migration checksum impact" above).
- [ ] CI green (rust + web + openapi-drift + chromium-e2e).

## Notes

- Two existing shared-codex fixtures (`card-codex-shared-worker`, `card-codex-shared-plain`) get a matching `terminal_id` stamp in `seed_legacy_live_cards`. They were themselves an instance of the orphan-payload shape pre-fix — the bug was silently passing in the existing test suite. Stamping keeps the existing 12-card assertion valid.
- New test `migration_0030_skips_orphan_terminal_backfill` seeds two orphan shapes per kind (missing stamp / wrong-pointing stamp) and asserts no runtime materialized.

Every prisma-enabled typecheck CI job (workgraph-api, prompt-composer, agent-runtime) failed at `prisma validate` with:

Error code: P1012 — Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL

Prisma reads `env("DATABASE_URL")` (and `DATABASE_URL_RUNTIME_READ`) just to **parse** the datasource block — `validate`/`generate` make no DB connection — so the whole `typecheck-ts` matrix went red (and cascaded to `mergeStateStatus: UNSTABLE`).

Set dummy `DATABASE_URL` + `DATABASE_URL_RUNTIME_READ` at the `typecheck-ts` job level. Offline-only placeholders; never connected to.

author: sundar1207
body:
💡 **What:** 
Optimized the heuristic calculation in `8 puzzle problem.py`. Replaced the O(N^2) inner search loop with an O(1) dictionary lookup by pre-calculating `goal_positions`. Also initialized the A* starting priority queue correctly with its calculated heuristic cost `f = g + h`.

🎯 **Why:** 
The heuristic calculates the Manhattan distance by matching current state values with their goal state counterparts. Originally, it iteratively scanned the entire goal board (O(N^2)) for each non-zero cell in the *current* board, inside the heuristic function. Since the heuristic is called recursively for every state expansion, this inner loop created an immense performance bottleneck.

📊 **Impact:** 
Reduces the heuristic execution time significantly. A baseline benchmark test against the original script demonstrated the runtime dropping from ~8.9s down to ~5.1s, yielding a ~40%+ performance improvement for moderately complex pathing. 

🔬 **Measurement:**
Running `python3 "8 puzzle problem.py"` successfully returns the shortest path. Code styling passes Flake8.

author: pcmhacker-piro
body:
## What

Adds `_remove_string_literals` — a state-machine parser that strips string literal contents from SQL for structural safety validation. Semicolons and forbidden keywords inside quoted strings no longer cause false positives.

## Why (the two blockers from the previous review)

**1. Backslash escape bug** — The old `_remove_string_literals` treated `\` as an escape inside string literals, but PostgreSQL's default `standard_conforming_strings=on` gives backslash no special meaning. This made `SELECT '\'; DROP TABLE users` bypass validation. Fixed by removing backslash escape handling entirely — only doubled quotes (`''`) are recognized as escapes, matching PostgreSQL behavior.

**2. Narrow diff** — Previous PR had 16 commits / 37 unrelated files. This branch is a single commit on latest `main` with **only** the 2 relevant files changed: `agent_code/db_config.py` (+29/-2) and `tests/test_db_config.py` (+23/-0).

## Changes

- `db_config.py`: Added `_remove_string_literals()` that correctly handles PostgreSQL string escaping (doubled quotes, no backslash). Updated `_assert_read_only_select` to run checks on the structural skeleton.
- `test_db_config.py`: Added 10 new test cases covering safe queries with semicolons/keywords in strings, multi-statement injection attempts, UNION-based injection, and the backslash regression case.

Closes #548

author: boshen
body:
## Problem

The `Update Vite Stats` workflow ([failing run](https://github.com/voidzero-dev/vibe-dashboard/actions/runs/27080764637/job/79926065294)) runs `vp run generate` → `vp check --fix`. Since commit bf33f4a, `tools/override-vite.mjs` targets **stable Vite 8 releases** (`/^8\.\d+\.\d+$/`). No stable Vite 8 exists on npm yet, so `generate` writes an empty `[]` to `data/vite-version-stats.json`. With an empty array, TypeScript infers the JSON import as `never[]`, so every `stat.version` / `stat.buildTime` access fails (`Property 'X' does not exist on type 'never'`) and `vp check` errors out.

## Fix

- Add typed wrapper `apps/dashboard/src/data/viteStats.ts` that casts the JSON to `ViteStat[]`, so empty data type-checks instead of collapsing to `never[]`.
- Repoint all four importers (`BuildTimeChart`, `BundleSizeChart`, `StatsCards`, `ViteStatsPage`) at the typed module.
- Skip writing the stats file when no versions are collected, so existing tracked data isn't clobbered until Vite 8 ships. Picks up Vite 8 automatically once released.

Verified `vp check` and `vp run build` pass, including a simulated empty-data (`[]`) run.

author: badmade
body:
## What

Adds `.github/workflows/claude.yml` so that mentioning `@claude` on an issue or pull request triggers a Claude Code run. Comment something like `@claude review this PR` and Claude runs with the surrounding issue/PR context — reviews, answers questions, or pushes fixes when asked.

## Triggers

- `issue_comment` (created)
- `pull_request_review_comment` (created)
- `pull_request_review` (submitted)
- `issues` (opened, assigned)

The job only runs when `@claude` actually appears in the comment/review/issue body or issue title, so non-mention activity doesn't spend a run.

## Conventions followed

- Actions are SHA-pinned with version comments, matching the other workflows in this repo:
  - `actions/checkout@08c6903…` (`# v5`, the same SHA already used in `tests.yml`)
  - `anthropics/claude-code-action@fbda2eb…` (`# v1`, the commit the `v1` tag currently resolves to)
- Workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`; the job widens to the scopes the action needs (`contents`/`pull-requests`/`issues: write`, `id-token: write`, `actions: read`).
- `timeout-minutes` set, consistent with the rest of `.github/workflows`.

## Required setup

The workflow reads `${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}`. Add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` repository secret (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions) for it to run. The easiest path is `claude /install-github-app` from the Claude Code CLI, which also installs the GitHub App and wires up the secret.

body:
## Resumo

Adiciona uma camada **configurável de metadados de confiança e comerciais** ao motor de reservas direto (Roomix Direct), armazenada como sub-seções **aditivas** do JSONB `booking_engine_settings.settings_json` — **sem migration**, retrocompatível.

- Selos/badges + classificação por estrelas dinâmica (inclui selo genérico "Melhor preço direto")
- Formas de pagamento aceitas (somente exibição, com aviso de pré-autorização)
- Regras da casa estruturadas com ícones (check-in/out destacados)
- Faixa de comodidades-destaque (scroll horizontal no mobile)
- Galeria com contagem de fotos + "Ver todas as fotos" (lightbox, Esc/scroll-lock)
- Painel lateral de confiança: localização + link externo de mapa, resumo de pagamento e política; **avaliações ocultas** até existir dado real (nunca inventadas)

Backend é a fonte da verdade: `normalizeBookingEngineSettings` faz clamp de estrelas, whitelist de enums, limite de tamanho/quantidade, coerção de booleanos e remoção de campos de escopo em **toda escrita** (SQLite + Postgres). Adiciona `toPublicPreviewSettings()` para **remover segredos** (`linkIntegration`, `pixKey`/`bankDetails`/contatos de comprovante) do payload de preview injetado. Console ganha aba "Selos e Confiança" + editores nas abas de comodidades/pagamentos/políticas.

Publicação permanece **preview-gated**. Identidade visual própria, **sem** marcas/selos de terceiros (ícones genéricos + texto).

## Arquivos alterados (9)
- `server/db/bookingEngineRepository.ts` — tipos, defaults, normalização, `toPublicPreviewSettings`
- `src/services/bookingEngineService.ts` — tipos espelhados (cliente)
- `server.ts` — **somente por hunk**: import/uso de `toPublicPreviewSettings` + `validSections` (+4 seções)
- `motor 1 classico/src/App.tsx` — renderização no template público
- `src/components/BookingEngineAdminView.tsx` — aba/editores no Console
- `package.json` — **somente por hunk**: script `booking:trust:test` + cadeia `test`
- `scripts/booking-trust-metadata-smoke.ts` — novo smoke (10 cenários + normalização + isolamento + projeção)
- `docs/ROOMIX_DIRECT_TRUST_METADATA_SPEC.md`, `docs/ROOMIX_DIRECT_TRUST_METADATA_PLAN.md` — spec/plano

## Testes rodados
- ✅ `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit)
- ✅ `npm run build` (app + template Direct)
- ✅ `npm run booking:trust:test`
- ✅ `git diff --check` / `git diff --cached --check`
- ✅ secret scan do conteúdo staged (vazio)
- ⚠️ `npm run security:test`: `security-smoke` **passou**; a cadeia para na falha **pré-existente** `navigation-isolation-smoke` (ver aviso abaixo)
- Validação visual no navegador (desktop + mobile) do template com dados de exemplo: badges/estrelas, galeria+lightbox, regras, pagamentos+pré-auth, mapa, mobile responsivo — sem erros de console.

## ⚠️ Falhas pré-existentes (fora deste PR)
`navigation-isolation-smoke` (código de overbooking `ROOMIX_DIRECT_ROOM_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE` vs esperado `ROOMIX_DIRECT_ROOM_UNAVAILABLE`) e `agent-booking-engine-smoke`/`rate_coverage` **já falhavam** no working tree por WIP pré-existente em `server.ts` (fluxo de disponibilidade/tarifas), **não relacionado** a esta feature. **Não foram corrigidas** e **não estão neste PR**. O diff staged comprova que o commit não toca esses caminhos.

## Staging por hunk
`server.ts` e `package.json` tinham WIP pré-existente no working tree. Foram stageados **somente por hunk** (via `git apply --cached` de patches construídos a partir do HEAD + minhas edições), sem incluir WIP. O WIP segue **não-commitado** no working tree.

## Confirmações
- ✅ **Zero deploy** — nada deployado; sem alterações em Railway/banco/domínio.
- ✅ **Zero secrets** — scan staged vazio; a mudança nova **remove** segredos do payload de preview.
- ✅ **Gateway / OTA / FNRH / canal real intocados** — pagamentos são apenas exibição; publicação preview-gated.
- ✅ Sem `git add .` / stage geral; `server.ts` e `package.json` por hunk.

author: tspugh
body:
New spec + first buildable slice: the **authoritative-source allowlist**.

## Why
Surfaced by the SPEC-0007 R12 live tests: the LLM Parse Website scrape returns a single short
snippet (for bupropion×ADHD always the "used off-label" background line, never the efficacy
conclusion), and **any URL is currently accepted** as evidence. SPEC-0010 introduces a layer
that (a) **normalizes** an authoritative source into compact, support-forward content the
scraper reliably extracts, and (b) **gates** evidence on **source reputability** so the agent
can't be steered by a self-hosted/SEO page.

## What's in this PR (the allowlist slice)
- `docs/specs/0010-…md` — the full spec (normalize + allowlist + DOI/PMID anchoring + source
  tiers + provenance + governance R13 + tests + pass/fail + open questions).
- `src/evidence/allowlist.ts` (lib, pure) — `SourceTier`, `ApprovedSource`/`SourceMatch`,
  curated `DEFAULT_APPROVED_SOURCES` (openFDA, DailyMed, PubMed/PMID, PMC, Crossref/DOI, NICE,
  USPSTF), `matchSource()` (identifier→host→urlPrefix; no enabled match → reject),
  `mergeAllowlist()` (defaults ⊕ override; built-ins disable-not-delete, can't be shadowed).
- `web/src/approvedSourcesStore.ts` + Settings **"Approved evidence sources"** panel — list of
  defaults + custom, add / remove (custom) / enable-disable / reset, and an **R13 trust banner**
  (demo = local operator convenience; production = payer/governance-controlled; a claim
  submitter cannot self-approve a source).

## Not in this PR (SPEC-0010 §4 future)
The normalizer + resolvers (efetch/Crossref/openFDA → support passage → scraper-friendly doc),
the provenance record, and the create/appeal wiring — i.e. what actually makes the off-label
appeal *flip*. This PR is the allowlist gate + Settings surface only.

## Tests
+7 allowlist unit tests (T9–T12: defaults→tiers; identifier/host/prefix matching;
non-allowlisted reject; disable/custom merge; built-in non-shadow/non-drop; parse helpers).
Lib + web build clean; web tsc clean (only the 2 pre-existing client.ts/livenessDebounce errors).

> Companion: `docs/research/evidence-source-provenance.md` (the R12 diagnosis + full mechanism
> brainstorm) lands via the SPEC-0007 PR (#23), where the R12 verification lives.

## Summary
- Adds `.claude/commands/promote-to-main.md` — a `/promote-to-main` command that promotes the cumulative `staging` → `main` delta (production), modeled on `/pr-merge`'s rigor.

author: lilseancoc-png
body:
## What & why

A trader's-eye review of the Top Picks scoring system flagged one structural
problem above all (rubric/improvements call it the **horizon mismatch**):

> The grade is a stock-picker's 4-pillar score, but the product **trades ~14-day
> long premium** on 30–60 DTE contracts. The **fundamental** pillar (EPS/revenue
> growth, P/E, FCF, net-margin) pays off over *quarters* and is ~fully priced over
> the hold — near-zero information at the option's horizon — yet equal-weighted it
> was the **largest-magnitude pillar** and dominated the grade with signal a 2-week
> option can't monetize.

This PR fixes that by **scaling each asset-quality pillar by a horizon weight**
before summing, tilting the grade toward signals that actually move price before
the option decays.

## The change

| Pillar | Weight | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Fundamentals | **0.6** (`PICKS_HW_FUND`) | slowest; quarterly/annual, mostly priced over a fortnight (discounted, not gutted — still holds the faster *event* signals: analyst revisions, guidance, contracts) |
| Technicals | **1.0** (`PICKS_HW_TECH`) | RSI/MACD/S&R/momentum — natively the days-to-weeks horizon; the reference |
| Mechanicals | **1.15** (`PICKS_HW_MECH`) | options flow / OI / unusual volume / put-call — order flow leads price (modest boost) |
| Narrative | **0.9** (`PICKS_HW_NARR`) | catalysts move fast but are one noisy AI sentiment read; sector-narrative is slow |

`timing` and `ivCost` ride at **×1** (they're bounded conviction terms folded in
parallel, not asset-quality reads).

This is a **principled microstructure prior** (flow ≳ technicals ≫ slow
fundamentals at a 1–3 week horizon), **not** a fit to the 19-pick sample — the
per-signal IC bridge (§9.6) stays the path to replacing it with measured weights
once forward, gate-era outcomes accumulate.

## Implementation notes

- New `horizonWeight` / `applyHorizonWeight` in `scripts/build.mjs`, applied in
  **both** scoring paths: `scorePillared` (legacy/pre-standardization) and
  `computeCrossSectionalScores` (the cross-sectional recompute).
- The weight is **baked into each signal's `contribution`** so the card's
  per-signal chips stay consistent with the weighted pillar total **and** the
  pillars keep summing to `total` — both display invariants hold.
- The raw integer `score` on each signal is **untouched** (so `buildPickForecast`'s
  by-key reads are unchanged), and the IC-bridge standardized `z` is never scaled.

body: ## Summary Adds a fully public, read-only dashboard accessible at `/` without authentication. Unauthenticated visitors can view live speed test metrics, 24-hour trends, recent results, and alert history — all sourced from real data with no static placeholders. ## Changes ### Backend - **`PublicDashboardController`** — single `__invoke` controller with no auth middleware. Queries stats, 24-hour hourly trend (aggregated across all providers), 20 most recent speed results, and 10 most recent alert rules. Uses `DB::table()` for raw-select queries to satisfy PHPStan's strict type resolution. - **`routes/web.php`** — registers `GET /` to `PublicDashboardController` above the auth group. ### Frontend - **`layouts/PublicLayout.vue`** — slim sticky nav with `AppLogoIcon`, Zepeed wordmark, "Read-only · Public view" badge, and a `UserLock` Sign in link. No sidebar, no user menu. - **`pages/Public/Dashboard.vue`** — page shell composing all public components under `PublicLayout`. - **`components/public/PublicStatCard.vue`** — stat card with Lucide icon slot, value, and optional unit. - **`components/public/PublicTrendChart.vue`** — 24-bucket bar chart padded to always render 24 hourly bars regardless of data density. Empty buckets render as muted placeholder bars. - **`components/public/PublicResultsTable.vue`** — Shadcn/Vue `Table` showing last 10 results: Provider, Download, Upload, Ping, Jitter, Measured at. - **`components/public/PublicAlertHistory.vue`** — alert rule feed with name, Active/Disabled badge, and last updated timestamp stacked vertically per row. - **`types/public.ts`** — shared TypeScript interfaces: `PublicStats`, `TrendPoint`, `PublicSpeedResult`, `PublicAlertItem`. ## Sections (top to bottom) | Section | Data source | |---|---| | Overview stat cards | Aggregated last 24 h across all providers | | 24-hour trend charts | Hourly `AVG` bucketed by `DATE_FORMAT` across all providers | | Recent results table | Last 10 `speed_results` with provider name join | | Alert history feed | Last 10 `alert_rules` ordered by `updated_at` | ## Design decisions - No marketing copy — full public dashboard, same data density as the authenticated view - Sign in is accessible via the persistent nav button only (no FAB) - Trend charts pad to 24 buckets so sparse data never collapses to a single fat bar - All queries use `DB::table()` for PHPStan compliance on raw select columns - `RetrieveWebUserSession` PHPDoc return type widened to `Collection>` to resolve pre-existing PHPStan error ## Screenshots

author: codetalcott
body:
Completes the **`when` reactive block** track from `docs-internal/MULTILINGUAL_ROADMAP.md` — the last and hardest Track 1 item. Clears **12 failing pattern-instances** (`when-value-changes` + `when-multiple-changes` across ar/he/ja/pl/qu/tr). Priority-bundle average **96.8% → 97.1%**, **zero regressions** across all 24 languages.

## Mechanism
`when <cond> changes <body> end` parses as an event-handler whose leading `when` conjunction (the dictionary form, emitted as a prefix by the transformer) must be recognized. Each failing language had a distinct root cause:

| Lang | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **pl** | event-handler pattern keyed on `gdy`; transformer emits `kiedy` | add `kiedy` to the pattern's literal alternatives |
| **qu** | only postfix `{event} pi/kaqtin {body}`; transformer emits prefix `maykama` | add `maykama {event} {body}` pattern (mirrors es `cuando {event} {body}`) |
| **ar/he/tr** | no hand-crafted event-handler patterns (dispatch returned `[]`) | add narrowly-scoped prefix `{when} {event} {body}` patterns (`عندما` / `כאשר` / `iken`) + dispatch cases |
| **ja** | same as above **plus** `とき` starts with the particle `と`, which the character-based tokenizer's particle extractor greedily ate (`と`+`き`) | add the ja `when` pattern **and** switch the i18n dict `とき` → `時` (single kanji, already a ja temporal marker — tokenizes cleanly) |

New `when` patterns are scoped to the `when` literal, so they never shadow `on <event>` handlers (which start with the event word, not the conjunction).

## Verification (roadmap playbook)
- Probed each pattern via `MultilingualHyperscript.parse()` after rebuilding semantic + i18n + core.
- Repopulated the DB, regenerated the `browser-priority` baseline.
- Baseline diff: **exactly 12 fail→pass flips, 0 pass→fail** across all 24 languages.
- Keyword-collision guard green (25/25). i18n suite green (623/623). Semantic suite green except the known-environmental `build-artifacts.test.ts` `.d.ts` checks (5260 passing, unchanged from baseline).
- Binary `patterns.db` restored (not committed); regenerated baseline committed.

## Track 1 complete 🎉
With #269 (stragglers + socket), #270 (live blocks), and this PR (when blocks), **all 35 reactive instances are cleared**. Remaining roadmap work: Bucket C per-language (83, tl/ar/he-heavy) and Bucket B behaviors (24, runtime track).

author: jascal
body:
## What

The cross-model test of the positional-broadcast finding from #25. `validate_new_edges.py` showed (causally, on GPT-2) that the prev-token head reads a positional signal piped in from early **sink** heads. This asks whether that's an **absolute-positional-embedding artifact** across architectures.

A *key-only* causal path-patch that respects each model's RoPE is non-trivial to do faithfully cross-arch, so `scripts/gemma/cross_model_positional.py` goes to the **representational** question the hypothesis turns on: **is the prev-token head's position carried in the key *content* (absolute, must be written into the residual) or in the QK *rotation* (RoPE, applied at attention time)?** For each model it finds the top prev-token head, captures its **pre-rotation** keys over the corpus, and decomposes the key variance into position-explained vs token-explained.

## Result (Shakespeare, ~33s, 4 models) — a clean 1-vs-3 split (~10×)

| model | pos. encoding | prev-token head | key var: **position** | key var: token | pos/tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GPT-2** | absolute (`wpe`) | 4.11 | **59%** | 18% | **3.3** |
| Gemma-2-2B | RoPE | 21.7 | 7% | 23% | 0.30 |
| Llama-3.2-1B | RoPE | 0.2 | 2% | 64% | 0.04 |
| Qwen-2.5-1.5B | RoPE | 13.4 | 9% | 25% | 0.35 |

**Only GPT-2's prev-token key is position-dominated; every RoPE model's is token-dominated.** This is the cross-model *explanation* that ties the whole positional thread together:

- GPT-2 encodes absolute position as **key content** → its prev-token head must *read that content* → it depends on the early sink heads that **broadcast** it (the `validate_new_edges` collapse) → and GPT-2 is the only family member that **depends on its sink** (the sink-ablation result, position-independently = the absolute-positions signature).
- RoPE models need none of this — position rides in the rotation — so they have **no sink dependence and no positional-broadcast circuit**.

## Scope (honest)
- This is the **representational** confirmation (the key *is* position-encoded only in GPT-2), corroborating the *causal* GPT-2 result (#25). A faithful **key-only causal path-patch** across RoPE models is the heavier next step (forward-pointer (a) in the validation section).
- Arch-generic: the model applies its own RoPE/GQA; keys captured pre-rotation via a `k_proj` / `c_attn` hook.

## Verification
```
.venv/bin/python scripts/gemma/cross_model_positional.py   # ~33s, downloads/uses cached HF models
```
`ruff --select F` clean; tracked `cross_model_positional_summary.json`.

body:
## Summary
- New `RemoteStandardsUrlValidator` allow-lists the configured standards-pack git URL: only `https://`, `ssh://`, and `user@host:path` are accepted; `ext::`, `file://`, plain `http://`, shell metacharacters, whitespace, and URLs over 2048 chars are rejected.
- Validation runs at `LaunchpadSettings.update()` time so bad values never reach disk, with the error surfaced inline on the settings screen.
- `RemoteStandardsFetcher` re-validates defensively before invoking `git clone` (covers hand-edited `config.properties`) and adds `--` to the clone argv so a URL beginning with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag.

## Why
`RemoteStandardsFetcher.runGit()` previously passed the configured URL straight into `git clone` with no scheme check, no length cap, and no metacharacter rejection. Git accepts forms like `ext::sh -c ...` (a known RCE vector) and `file:///` (lets a pasted URL exfiltrate local paths). A user who pastes - or is socially engineered into pasting - an attacker-controlled URL gets arbitrary code execution. The five-line allow-list closes the easiest supply-chain ingress.

## Test plan

author: proggeramlug
body:
Follow-up to #4730, closing the deferred items it listed. Three independent fixes; no version/changelog bump.

## 1. Static accessors (`static get`/`static set`)

`static get/set` was never registered into `CLASS_STATIC_ACCESSORS` — codegen registered *all* getters/setters into the instance vtable, so `C.x` read `undefined` and `C.x = v` no-op'd (while `new C().x` wrongly saw them). Now:
- HIR `Class` tracks per-accessor static-ness via `static_accessor_names`; the accessor functions stay in `getters`/`setters` so every IR pass (async lowering, finally-inline, generator id-scan, inlining) still processes their bodies uniformly.
- Codegen emits static accessors via `compile_static_method` (no-`this` ABI, `this` from the implicit-this slot) under a `perry_static_…` symbol, and registers them with new `js_register_class_static_getter`/`js_register_class_static_setter` into `CLASS_STATIC_ACCESSORS` (whose read/write dispatch already existed).
- `js_object_get/set_property_key` now route class refs through the by-name dispatch instead of null'ing them via `extract_obj_ptr`, so `C['x']`/`C['x'] = v` reach static-accessor (and prototype instance-setter) dispatch.

`accessor-name-static` 0 → ~67%.

## 2. JS-canonical numeric member keys + empty-string keys

- `number_to_js_key` implements ECMA-262 `Number::toString`, so a numeric-literal member/object-literal key matches the runtime's key coercion (`0.0000001` → `"1e-7"`, `1e21` → `"1e+21"`) instead of Rust's non-exponential `Display`. A key registered under the Rust spelling was unreachable via `obj[0.0000001]`. Fixes class accessors/methods and object literals.
- Empty-string member keys (`get ''()`) now pass the `name_len <= 0` registration guard.

`accessor-name-inst`/`-static` → ~81%.

## 3. Default-aware method `.length`

The vtable only stores the total param count (needed for call dispatch), so `C.prototype.m.length` over-reported for methods with default-valued params. Codegen now computes the spec length (leading params before the first default/rest/synthesized-`arguments`) and records it via `js_register_class_method_bind_length` into `CLASS_METHOD_BIND_LENGTHS`, which `class_method_bind_length` consults first. Closes the `dflt-params-trailing-comma` `.length` cases.

## Verification
Test262 at the pinned SHA, `PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1`: `m(a,b=1).length===1`, `g(a=1,b=2).length===0`, `h(a,b,...r).length===2`, static `C.x`/`C['x']` read+write match Node; instance accessors unchanged (71%), object-literal numeric keys match Node. No instance-accessor regression.

## Still deferred (general semantics, not class-specific)
The `computed-err-*` accessor tests need ReferenceError-on-undeclared-variable and ToPropertyKey-invoking-a-throwing-`toString` — broad expression-evaluation gaps outside the class-element scope.

author: rickytan
body:
## Problem
Every PR — even pure README/LICENSE edits — runs the 4-5 minute macOS Xcode build + unit tests. Slow, and uses paid macOS runner minutes.

## Solution
Three-job CI pipeline:

| Job | Runner | Cost | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changes` | ubuntu | ~10s | Always |
| `build-test` | macos-15 | ~5min | Only if code paths changed |
| `ci` (name: **Build & Test**) | ubuntu | ~5s | Always |

The umbrella `ci` job mirrors `build-test`'s outcome — required by branch protection, but free for docs-only PRs since it just inspects the upstream conclusion.

## Why an umbrella job
Branch protection requires a check named exactly `Build & Test` on every PR. If we used `paths-ignore` on the workflow trigger, the required check would never appear for docs PRs → unmergeable. The umbrella always reports.

## Path classification (positive list)
Treated as **code** (triggers build-test):
- `Sources/**`, `Tests/**`, `Resources/**`, `Pods/**`
- `project.yml`, `Podfile{,.lock}`, `Gemfile{,.lock}`, `swiftgen.yml`
- `.github/workflows/**` (workflow changes must be self-tested)
- `**/*.swift`, `**/*.entitlements`, `**/*.xcassets/**`

Everything else (README, LICENSE, *.md, .gitignore, docs/**, etc.) → docs-only → `build-test` skipped → `ci` passes immediately.

## Self-test
This PR itself modifies `.github/workflows/release.yml` → `build-test` will run → validates the new structure works end-to-end.

author: proggeramlug
body:
## Problem
Headless/CI clients (e.g. `perry publish` in a non-TTY GitHub Actions shell) can't reliably retrieve their build artifact. The only path is a long-lived WebSocket that delivers the download token via a `Complete` message — if the WS drops or the job sits in the queue, the artifact is unreachable, and it's lost entirely if the hub restarts (the queue is in-memory).

## Fix
Two Bearer-authed (the same `api_token` used by `perry publish`) endpoints to enqueue-then-poll-then-fetch by Job ID, no socket required:
- `GET /api/v1/jobs/:jobId/status` → `queued|running|completed|failed` (+ `artifact_url`, size, sha256 when ready)
- `GET /api/v1/jobs/:jobId/artifact` → the final artifact as base64 text (same encoding as `/api/v1/dl`)

On artifact upload the hub also writes a **job-id-keyed record to disk**, so a completed artifact is retrievable by Job ID and **survives a hub restart**. Intermediate `*-precompiled` sign bundles are skipped (only the CLI-facing final is recorded).

Deployed + verified live: endpoints return 401 without a valid token, 404 for unknown jobs; existing routes/WS unaffected.

Follow-up (not in this PR): persist the *queue* itself so queued (not-yet-built) jobs survive a restart + get re-dispatched. Pairs with PerryTS/perry#4732 (CLI no longer exits 0 without a result).

author: beingzy
body:
## What changed

Operators running `ck kickass`, `ck run`, or `ck watch` now see a classified failure category and a one-line fix suggestion on every failure.

**Before:**
```
✗ failed humanbased-ai/monorepo#313
Execution summary: 3 executed, 0 skipped, 2 failed
```

**After:**
```
✗ failed humanbased-ai/monorepo#313 [network]
    → transient macOS/LibreSSL SSL error — retry in a moment; or set clone_protocol: ssh in crosscheck.config.yml
✗ failed humanbased-ai/monorepo#314 [auth]
    → run: codex login

Execution summary: 3 executed, 0 skipped, 2 failed
  ✗ humanbased-ai/monorepo#313 [network]
  ✗ humanbased-ai/monorepo#314 [auth]
    → run: claude auth login  (or codex login, or check GITHUB_TOKEN)
```

PR failure comments for reviewer auth errors now post the specific login command instead of the generic "subprocess failed".

## Why

Investigation of `~/.crosscheck/logs/2026-06-08.ndjson` found three recurring failure modes that were opaque at the terminal:

- **9 × LibreSSL SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL** — classified as `subprocess`/`unknown` instead of `network`; no hint shown
- **6 × codex/claude auth failure** — classified as `unknown` instead of `auth`; no login command shown
- **8 × git clone failures** — network errors with no category

All three now surface the category and the exact remediation command.

## Changes

- `src/lib/logger.ts` — add `auth failure` to auth regex; add `ssl_error_syscall|libressl` to network regex
- `src/lib/remediation.ts` *(new)* — `hintForError(category, message)` with vendor-aware auth hints and SSL-specific network hint
- `src/commands/kickass.ts` — inline `[category] → hint` per failure; `printExecutionSummary` lists each failed PR with deduplicated hints
- `src/commands/run.ts` — append `[category] → hint` to the terminal error line
- `src/lib/reviewer-error.ts` — explicit auth path before the subprocess catch-all
- Tests: 2 new test files, existing tests updated (36 tests, all passing)

Also includes: `fix(board): evict prior-round slot when a new round starts for same PR`

author: av-asu
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 painted the neighbor's *floor* into the host flat where the host didn't reach. That made the strip read as "another colored band bleeds in" — recognizable as a transition but not as a recognizable place. This adds the upright pieces (walls, doors, windows, counters, tree/headstone standees) via a satellite camera, so the strip starts to read as the actual neighbor scene.

* `draw_terrain_tilted` now also returns `neighbor_solids` — a list of `(neighbor_scene, ntx, nty, host_world_x, host_world_y, sat_camera)` for each wall-class tile in the out-of-bounds region.
* The satellite camera mirrors the host (same pitch/yaw/scale) but shifted by the neighbor's world-coord offset, so projecting neighbor world points lands at the same screen pixel a host point at the seam would.
* `render_mixin` emits each neighbor solid into the unified depth-sort list using the **host** camera's depth on **host-frame** world coords, so a neighbor tree in front of an actor sorts correctly against the host's cast.
* The draw callback dispatches through the existing `_tilt_tile_box` but with the satellite camera + neighbor scene, so all the wall/door/window/standee logic reuses unchanged.

## Scope (intentional)

Three threads were on the table; this PR is just the one I was confident shipping:

- **Thread 1 (this PR): walls + standees in the strip** for non-wrap hosts. Done.
- **Thread 2: wrap-scene strips.** Deliberately skipped. Brimley and cornfield_maze tile their content edge to edge — there's no out-of-bounds area for a strip to fill. A localized overlay around each exit tile would put 5 different neighbor patches at random spots of Brimley, which reads as fragmentation rather than continuity. Wrap hosts already get seamless transitions on crossing; this seems like the right answer for their topology.
- **Thread 3: Move 4 (standee LOD).** Deliberately skipped. The cheap levers don't help (`_ground_shadow` is already cached at ~6 µs); the expensive lever (per-distance card scale) would shrink trees toward the horizon — that's more *correct* perspectively, but a visible style shift that needs a call before landing.

Both punts are recorded so we can revisit on purpose.

## Test plan

- [x] `python tests/run_all.py` (smoke + flow + fold_pursuit + king_roam + render_smoke) all green
- [x] Strip visually inspected for `gravel_road_north`, `river_crossing`, `lodge_arrival` — neighbor walls now stand up in the strip area instead of the floor-only patch from #53
- [ ] Walk a non-wrap host edge in-game and confirm depth-sorting between host actors and neighbor walls reads correctly

author: boxbuilder1993
body:
## Problem

The proxy reads `WORKPLANNER_API_URL` + `INTERNAL_API_KEY` straight from its own environment (no `.env` loader) and **exits if they're missing**. But `start-all.sh` never set them and there's no `claude-proxy/.env` — they only existed because they happened to be exported in the dev's shell (pointed at prod).

So on a **fresh checkout** (e.g. a company laptop): `make dev` would create `.env`, bring up the Docker stack, then the **proxy would crash on startup** — and the archivist / `@ai` would be silently dead, with no obvious reason why.

## Fix

When `start-all.sh` starts the proxy, it now:
- points it at the **host-published local backend** `http://localhost:8080` (docker maps `8080:8080`),
- reuses **`INTERNAL_API_KEY` from the repo-root `.env`** (the one `make dev` generates),
- **respects anything already exported** (`:=` default) — so a prod-pointed proxy on a personal Mac isn't clobbered (and `start-all.sh` already leaves an already-running proxy alone),
- **fails fast** with a clear message if no key can be found, instead of a silent proxy crash.

Net: `make dev` is now genuinely turnkey on a fresh machine — `.env` is generated *and* the proxy is correctly wired to talk to the local backend.

Also documents local-vs-prod backend wiring in `claude-proxy/README.md`.

## Verified

- `bash -n` clean.
- Key extraction against a real `.env` → 64-hex, non-empty.
- `WORKPLANNER_API_URL` defaults to `localhost:8080` when unset, and an existing export is preserved.
