body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @Utemita :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## Resumen

Esta PR resuelve los tres puntos que pediste:

### 1. Postes hsp del mecanismo original (incluidos)
- Se agrega el **poste hsp = 17 mm** sobre la falange medial Fm (anclado a la mitad de Fm, perpendicular dorsal).
- Se agrega el **eslabon L9** que conecta P3 (extremo de c2) con el extremo del poste hsp de Fm. Esto materializa el offset `THETAauxfm = 51.39 deg` que en el codigo aparecia como una formula sin contraparte fisica.
- Se agrega el **poste hsp sobre Fd** marcado como **vestigial** (en el mecanismo original llevaba L10; en el nuevo diseno la falange distal recibe movimiento por el 4B#3).

### 2. Correccion de BETA2 (~200 deg)
Tenias razon: el BETA2 = 110 deg que aparecia en el diagrama no coincidia con el angulo que se mide con transportador. La causa era que el codigo usa internamente los parametros analiticos del lado palmar (40 y 110), pero el dibujo se muestra reflejado al lado dorsal. El angulo geometrico real es:

- `BETA1_geom = -11.4 deg` (antes mostraba 40)
- `BETA2_geom = 185.8 deg` (antes mostraba 110, tu lo medias como ~200)

Las **trayectorias DIP siguen identicas**: 32.12 -> 62.03 deg, monotonas, excursion 29.91 deg. Solo se corrigio la etiqueta para que coincida con la medida fisica del dibujo.

### 3. Archivos STEP de los eslabones del 4B#3
En `step_4B3/`:
- `acoplador_Lac.step` / `.stl` - barra plana 8.86 mm entre agujeros, espesor 1.5 mm
- `poste_Lpc.step` / `.stl` - oreja para Fp con base de montaje (longitud efectiva 8 mm)
- `poste_Lpd.step` / `.stl` - oreja para Fd con base de montaje (longitud efectiva 18 mm)
- `pasador.step` / `.stl` - pin de articulacion D = 1.5 mm

Cada poste incluye una base de montaje 6x4x1 mm con un agujero M1.5 para atornillarlo a la falange.

### 4. Plano tecnico cotado
- `plano_4B3_general.png` - vista lateral del 4B#3 montado sobre el dedo, con cotas Lpc, Lac, Lpd, Fm, BETA1_geom y BETA2_geom.
- `plano_4B3_piezas.png` - planos de fabricacion individuales del acoplador y los postes con dimensiones, lista de materiales (BOM) y parametros de fabricacion.

## Archivos modificados/creados

- `diagrama_mecanismo.py` - actualizado con postes hsp, L9 y angulos geometricos.
- `diagrama_mecanismo_completo.png` - regenerado.
- `generar_step_4b3.py` - **nuevo** (cadquery).
- `plano_4B3.py` - **nuevo**.
- `plano_4B3_general.png`, `plano_4B3_piezas.png` - **nuevos**.
- `step_4B3/` - **carpeta nueva** con 4 STEP + 4 STL.
- `verificar_angulos.py` - **nuevo** (utilidad para confirmar los angulos geometricos).
- `Guia_Ensamble_CAD.md` - actualizada con el procedimiento dorsal completo y referencia a los nuevos archivos.

## Verificaciones

- [x] Todas las longitudes coinciden con el modelo MATLAB (verificacion en consola).
- [x] DIP relativo de 32.12 a 62.03 deg, monotono creciente.
- [x] CRK3 y ROK3 en el lado dorsal (verificado por producto punto con la normal dorsal de Fm).
- [x] Postes hsp = 17 mm verificados.

## Como usar

1. Importa los archivos STEP de `step_4B3/` en tu CAD favorito.
2. Monta el acoplador Lac entre los extremos de los postes Lpc y Lpd.
3. Atornilla el poste Lpc a la falange proximal con `BETA1_geom = -11.4 deg` respecto al eje Fp (eje MCF -> IFP).
4. Atornilla el poste Lpd a la falange distal con `BETA2_geom = 185.8 deg` respecto al eje Fd (eje IFD -> TIP).
5. Sigue la guia `Guia_Ensamble_CAD.md` para el resto del ensamble.

author: nathanfraske
body:
## What

Lands the **agentic dispatch** layer and wires it to the self-hosted runner so the
budgeted tier-escalation loop can dispatch route-candidate compute to the box and pull
the metrics back to the cloud orchestrator to judge.

Two commits:

### 1. `cec_dispatch.py` — compute-as-tools + the budgeted loop (prototype)
Tightens the coupling the two-plane router left detached (compute ran a blind batch,
judgement happened after). Compute becomes discrete **tools** a tier agent calls on demand:
- `request_candidates(board, params, seeds, where)` → structured `CandidateMetrics`
  (kelvin_ok/diffpair_ok/gates_pass/drc/unconnected/drc_types/loci) — the agent reasons on
  metrics, never raw boards.
- `agent_route(board, tiers, budget)` — the loop: request → a TIER judges →
  `accept | request_more(params)` (budget--) | `escalate` (defer up, reset budget);
  budget exhausted → forced escalate; ladder exhausted → human.
- `tiers` = ordered `decide(JudgeContext)→Verdict` callables (Haiku swarm → Sonnet → Opus
  → human). Deterministic defaults run headless (loop unit-tested).

Demonstrated live earlier: a real Haiku judge distinguished the cosmetic logo DRC from the
real diffpair gate-fail, returned `request_more`, and the re-dispatch converged → accept.

### 2. `synth.yml` — a `candidates` mode (the `where='runner'` path)
The loop can now dispatch the FR candidate batch to the runner:
- `cec_dispatch request-candidates` wraps its metrics JSON in
  `===CEC_CANDIDATES_JSON_BEGIN===/END===` markers so the orchestrator can pull it cleanly
  out of the GitHub Actions job log (where stdout+stderr interleave), and writes
  `candidates.json` for the artifact.
- `synth.ps1`: `ValidateSet` gains `candidates`; `+Passes/+OptTime`; a candidates branch; java
  ensured for the FR run.
- `synth.yml`: `candidates` choice + `passes`/`opt_time` inputs + Windows/Linux invocations +
  `build/candidates/` in the upload path.

## Why on main
`workflow_dispatch` only sees a workflow file that is on the **default branch**, so the
`candidates` mode is only dispatchable once this is on `main`.

body:
## Summary

Adds real YouTube video search to the DSA Mentor agent using the Serper API. Before generating a lecture, the script now searches for a problem-specific YouTube solution video and injects the results directly into the Claude prompt. Also fixes HTML parsing bug in problem metadata extraction and adds retry logic for OpenRouter 504 errors.


## Changes

### `dsaMentor.js`

- **New `httpsPost()`** — shared HTTP utility reused by both Serper and OpenRouter calls, removes duplicated request logic
- **New `searchYoutube()`** — queries Serper `/videos` endpoint with 3 progressive fallback queries, filters results by title relevance to avoid generic playlist links
- **Fixed `extractProblemMeta()`** — strips HTML tags before regex matching, was previously extracting `<code>` tag content as the problem name
- **Updated `askOpenRouter()`** — retries up to 3 times with 5s/10s/15s exponential backoff on 504 or unexpected responses, refactored to use `httpsPost()`
- **Updated `runMentor()`** — calls `searchYoutube()` before `askOpenRouter()` and injects results as context into the user prompt

### `.github/workflows/code-mentor.yml`

- Added `SERPER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SERPER_API_KEY }}` to the Run step env block

### `skills/dsa-mentor.md`

- Updated Step 3 — agent now reads YouTube results from injected prompt context instead of being instructed to call a web search tool that was never available via OpenRouter
- Added rule — never fabricate a URL, omit Video Solution section entirely if no results were provided


## How It Works

```
dsaMentor.js extracts problem number + name from README (HTML stripped)
        ↓
Serper /videos searched with 3 progressive queries
        ↓
Results filtered by title — must mention problem number or name
        ↓
YouTube URLs injected into Claude prompt as context
        ↓
Claude picks most relevant watch URL for Video Solution section
```


## Before / After

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Problem parsing | Extracted HTML tags as problem name | Strips HTML, extracts correct number + name |
| YouTube search | None — agent guessed or fabricated | Serper `/videos` with relevance filter |
| Search results | Generic NeetCode 150 playlist | Problem-specific video |
| 504 errors | Script fails immediately | Retries 3x with backoff |
| HTTP logic | Duplicated in each function | Shared `httpsPost()` utility |


## Secret to Add

`SERPER_API_KEY` → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

Free key at [serper.dev](https://serper.dev) — 2500 searches/month included.

author: ipoe
body:
💡 What:
Created `ContactosListSerializer` to override the `create` logic for mass insertions, utilizing Django's native `bulk_create` along with `update_conflicts=True` to serve as a fast upsert. Integrated this custom `ListSerializer` into `ContactosSerializer` by mapping `list_serializer_class = ContactosListSerializer` under the `Meta` options.

🎯 Why:
The previous DRF implementation used an `update_or_create` logic directly in the child serializer, meaning when called with `many=True`, it would execute roughly N+1 queries. Each incoming contact required checking existence and applying inserts/updates, dramatically slowing down system performance and dragging backend responsiveness over heavy payloads.

📊 Impact:
Turns N+1 database querying operations into roughly ~3 static database queries regardless of the bulk size payload during a single request. Reduces memory and speeds up database transactions significantly. 

🔬 Measurement:
A standalone performance test with `DEBUG=True` passing 100 bulk objects demonstrated the total baseline ORM query count plunged from 600 queries initially down to a mere 3 queries total during `bulk_create`.

body:
## Problem
Fixes #16428

When a user applies a custom absolute date range (`startDate`/`endDate`) 
and then clicks a quick range filter button (15m/1h/24h), both params 
are sent to the API simultaneously, causing:
> HTTP 422: "Illegal argument: Parameters 'startDate'/'endDate' and 'timeRange' are mutually exclusive"

## Root Cause
In `loadQuery()` in `Executions.vue`, all URL query params are passed 
directly to the API without checking for this conflict.

## Fix
Before building the API query, check if a relative `timeRange` filter 
is present. If yes, remove `startDate`/`endDate`. This handles both:
- Legacy `DateFilter` format: `timeRange`  
- New filter-chip format: `filters[timeRange][EQUALS]`

## Testing
1. Go to Executions page
2. Set a custom absolute date range
3. Click any quick filter (15m / 1h / 24h)
4. ✅ Executions load correctly — no HTTP 422 error

author: nbx-liz
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #29 (H-0021): a **locally runnable** performance-benchmark harness
for the hot paths, plus a recorded baseline. No CI changes — benchmarks never
run in `make ci`/`make test`.

This is a Change-Gate change (new dev dependency + build tooling), so it ships
with proposal **H-0021** in `HISTORY.md`.

## What's included

- **`benchmarks/`** — `pytest-benchmark` cases with deterministic, fixed-seed
  synthetic data (`_data.py`):
  - `bench_catdap1` — 100/1k/10k/100k rows × 10 categorical cols
  - `bench_catdap2` — 100/1k/10k rows × 5/10 mixed cols, `nvar=5` (subset-search
    bounded; `nvar=None` would search 2^cols)
  - `bench_pooling` — `optimal_binning` on 1k/10k/100k rows
  - `bench_discovery` — `discover_error_slices` on a synthetic 14-col
    Adult-Income-shaped frame, **hard-bounded** (`max_vars=2`, capped
    `max_candidates`, 5k-row subsample, `slow`-marked) to avoid the known OOM
    regime, and synthetic to avoid OpenML network-timing variance
- **`bench` dependency-group** (`pytest-benchmark`) — dev-only, not a user extra,
  not in `dev`; `py-cpuinfo`-only transitive deps so **no numpy/pandas cap** →
  `uv.lock` numpy/pandas resolution unchanged. Not shipped in the wheel.
- **`make bench`** — runs the suite with `-o addopts=""` (drops `--cov` so timing
  is undisturbed) and `-o python_files="bench_*.py"`. `benchmarks/` stays outside
  `testpaths`, so `make ci`/`make test` never collect it.
- **`docs/performance.md`** — baseline numbers (i9-14900K / Python 3.11) +
  methodology/caveats; added to mkdocs nav.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.

## Baseline (min, this machine — relative reference only)

| Function | Workload | Min |
|---|---|---:|
| `catdap1` | 100k rows × 10 cols | 2.79 s |
| `catdap2` | 10k rows × 10 cols, `nvar=5` | 4.30 s |
| `optimal_binning` | 100k rows | 0.055 s |
| `discover_error_slices` | 14 cols, 5k rows, `max_vars=2` | 6.98 s |

The #20 scenario (CATDAP-02 on a 14-col dataset) is well under the 30 s target
at these bounded params.

## Out of scope (deferred follow-up)

Nightly non-blocking benchmark CI, historical trend charts, and PR-delta
comments — see #29 decision (hosted-runner noise makes a per-PR 20% gate flaky;
the chosen strategy is a non-blocking nightly alert).

## Invariants / Failure paths

N/A — benchmarks are read-only measurement; no concurrency, state machine, or
resource ownership introduced.

## Test plan

- [x] `make ci` green (ruff + format + mypy strict + pytest `-m "not slow"`,
      966 passed, 89.17% cov) — `benchmarks/` NOT collected (test count unchanged)
- [x] `make bench` runs all 14 benchmarks green (catdap1/2/pooling/discovery)
- [x] `uv.lock` numpy/pandas pins unchanged after adding `bench` group
- [x] `ruff check`/`format --check` clean on `benchmarks/`

Part of #29 (Phase 1). Remaining CI/observability work (nightly, charts,
PR-delta) is tracked in #161.

author: claude
body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>[color] Select AMaZE demosaic on the refine/export path (Bayer ships bilinear today)</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Summary
> 
> AMaZE is implemented in the core but **never selected by the live editors or the default export** — so Bayer images ship through **bilinear**, the weakest demosaic (softest, most prone to false color and edge fringing). Make the **refine + export** render path select AMaZE on every platform, while keeping a fast demosaic for the interactive preview. This is a CPU-only quality change; no GPU work and no color-math change.
> 
> ## Current state (code-verified)
> 
> `raw-core/src/pipeline/develop/mod.rs` maps `RenderQuality` → demosaic:
> 
> - **Bayer:** `Preview → half_res`; `Full → bilinear` (or `hamilton_adams` only under the `high-quality-demosaic` feature, which platform builds do **not** set); `Amaze → amaze` (`:183-188`).
> - **X-Trans:** `Preview → xtrans_bilinear`; `Full | Amaze → markesteijn` (`:174-176`) — **already high quality.**
> 
> So the default-quality gap is **Bayer-specific**: X-Trans already gets Markesteijn at `Full`.
> 
> Key facts:
> 
> - **AMaZE is not behind a cargo feature** — `demosaic::amaze` is unconditionally compiled (`raw-core/src/demosaic/mod.rs:1,7`). Selecting it is a runtime `RenderQuality::Amaze` request; no build-flag or recompile gymnastics.
> - Consumers currently request `Full` (→ bilinear for Bayer): the web `raw-wasm` `render_bytes` path, the Apple FFI develop path, and the export path. Only `maple-cli` requests `Amaze`.
> - Net: the live editors and the default export demosaic Bayer with bilinear.
> 
> ## Why this matters
> 
> Demosaic reconstructs 2/3 of every pixel's color by interpolation. Bilinear's failure modes are *color* artifacts in detailed regions — false color / color moiré on fine repetitive texture, and magenta/green zipper fringing at high-contrast edges — introduced **early** (before the color matrix, saturation, and sharpening, all of which amplify them). It also costs ~half the effective resolution. AMaZE is direction-aware and exists specifically to suppress those artifacts. This directly serves the "trustworthy color" bar and should tighten the worst-case parity tails.
> 
> ## Proposal
> 
> 1. Select **AMaZE** (best demosaic) on the **refine + export** path on all platforms; keep `Preview` (half-res) for the interactive fast phase.
> 2. Ensure demosaic is a **once-per-image** cost (decoded / scene-linear develop cache), not a per-edit cost — so AMaZE runs at image open, never on the slider-tick path.
> 3. No cargo-feature change required.
> 
> ## Per-platform scope
> 
> - **Apple** (true two-phase): refine pass → AMaZE; fast phase → `Preview`/half-res. Clean win now.
> - **Export (all platforms) + CLI**: always AMaZE (CLI already does; wire export to request it).
> - **Web**: export → AMaZE now. The web **live** path currently re-develops the full image per debounced edit and has no fast phase, so adopt AMaZE on the web live path **together with** the develop-result cache / fast-phase work (see Related) — so demosaic is paid once per open rather than per edit, and the single-phase WASM render isn't made heavier in the meantime.
> 
> ## Non-goals
> 
> - **Not GPU work.** AMaZE stays on the CPU; this is independent of the wgpu/WGSL per-tick render migration (#925) and must not be coupled to it.
> - **Not porting AMaZE to GPU.**
> - **No color-math / calibration change** — same WB, DCP, working space; only the spatial reconstruction improves.
> - **X-Trans untouched** — already Markesteijn at `Full`.
> 
> ## Acceptance criteria
> 
> - Bayer **refine + export** select AMaZE on Apple, web export, and CLI; the interactive preview stays on a fast demosaic (`Preview`/half-res).
> - Demosaic confirmed to run **once per image** (cached), not on the slider-tick path; slider-tick budget unaffected.
> - Cold-open / refine cost measured on the 100MP Bayer fixture (test_0000) and documented.
> - **`test-fixtures/budgets.json` re-baselined in the same commit** (one-way ratchet); report the bilinear→AMaZE ΔE delta per fixture (expect p95 / max / per-hue to tighten on detailed scenes; mean dominated by the view-transform delta and largely unchanged).
> - Color parity harness (`test_color_pipeline.sh`) green.
> 
> ## Suggested first step (measure before flipping)
> 
> Render the reference fixtures at `RenderQuality::Amaze` vs `Full`, diff each vs the ACR reference and against each other (`compare_images.py`, CIEDE2000), at both the gate's downscaled size and full resolution. That quantifies the win per fixture and produces the budget re-baseline numbers.
> 
> ## Related
> 
> - zubair-io/Maple#925 — complementary, **not blocking**: that epic is the per-tick GPU render chain; demosaic stays CPU and is out of its scope.
> - zubair-io/Maple#846 / zubair-io/Maple#321 — web two-phase / fast-phase + develop caching; the web **live** AMaZE adoption pairs with these so demosaic runs once per open.
> </issue_description>
>

author: deepme987
body:
## What
Move the `spawn-helper` chmod from the build-time `afterPack` hook (#966) to a runtime `ensureSpawnHelperExecutable()` call at `terminal.ts` module load.

## Why
#966 was the wrong layer. After it merged we shipped 1.0.11 and the Terminal tab was still black; checking `/Applications/Comfy Desktop.app/.../prebuilds/darwin-arm64/spawn-helper` shows mode `0644`, identical to pre-fix. Confirmed the ToDesktop build pipeline doesn't actually apply our `afterPack.mjs` chmod — `7zip-bin/mac/arm64/7za` is *also* `0644` in the shipped dmg, and it only works at runtime because `src/main/lib/extract.ts:32` chmods it on every call.

This PR mirrors the `extract.ts` pattern for `spawn-helper`:

- Resolve `node-pty`'s package dir via `createRequire(__filename).resolve('node-pty/package.json')`
- Walk to `prebuilds/<plat>-<arch>/spawn-helper`
- Swap `app.asar` → `app.asar.unpacked`
- chmod 0755 — best-effort, wrapped in try/catch

Also chmod `build/Release/spawn-helper` for dev installs where `@electron/rebuild` has produced a local copy (node-pty's loader prefers `build/Release/` over `prebuilds/`).

#966 stays useful as belt-and-braces for any future pure-electron-builder dmg path; this commit is the actual fix for the shipped ToDesktop build.

## Test
- [ ] Tag + build 1.0.12 from this branch
- [ ] Verify spawn-helper in the new dmg is `-rwxr-xr-x` after launching (runtime chmod kicked in at module load)
- [ ] Open bottom-panel Terminal tab → real prompt

author: velantrian
body:
## Summary

Implements **RFC0073 — Neurogenesis Dynamic Growth**, the **last** of the four Hybrid Biological Memory modules (issue #7). Together with RFC0070 (Fractal), RFC0071 (Epigenetic) and RFC0072 (Immune), this completes **RFC0070–0073**. Modelled on adult hippocampal neurogenesis: young memory is highly plastic, matures into stable storage, and **pattern separation** keeps similar-but-distinct memories from collapsing — pillars of lifelong learning without catastrophic forgetting.

## `core/neurogenesis.py`

- **Plasticity & maturation** — `plasticity(fact)` is high when a fact is young (recently created) and matures linearly to a stable floor over twice the maturation window. Deterministic from `created_at`, dependency-free. Tunable via `VELANTRIM_NEURO_PLASTICITY` / `_MATURATION` / `_YOUNG`.
- **Pattern separation** — `separate()` links a new fact to canonical neighbours that are vectorally **close** (similarity ≥ threshold) but **not** contradictions, via a `SEPARATED_FROM` edge — distinct-but-similar memories stay distinct. Reuses the conflict candidates ingest already computes.
- **Growth & capacity** — `growth_report()` exposes AHN stats: young/mature counts, average plasticity, capacity ceiling/headroom (`VELANTRIM_NEURO_MAX_NODES`), `at_capacity`, and a pattern-separation score.
- **Lifelong capacity** — `prune_candidates()` lists mature, weak, **non-CORE-anchored** facts that could be reclaimed (advisory only; deletion stays with `erase_fact`, GDPR Art. 17 — CORE fractal anchors are never candidates).

## Integration

- `ingest.ingest`: optional pattern separation (`VELANTRIM_NEURO_SEPARATION`), mirroring auto-contradict — **off by default**, so existing behaviour and tests are unchanged. Adds `result['separated_from']` when it fires.
- `cli.py`: `neuro-report` / `neuro-prune-candidates`.

```bash
velantrim neuro-report
velantrim neuro-prune-candidates --max-confidence 0.2
```

## Tests & docs
- `tests/test_neurogenesis.py`: plasticity/maturation, env fallbacks, pattern separation (contradiction exclusion, threshold, ingest opt-in), growth report, capacity flag, prune filters incl. CORE-anchor protection, CLI round-trip. `core/neurogenesis.py` at **99%**.
- README (module table + usage), ROADMAP (RFC0073 done — issue #7 complete), TEST_REPORT & SECURITY refreshed.
- **459 passing**, 12 skipped, **99% coverage** (gate 95%).

author: kazukinakai
body:
## What

Make the mindbase MCP server's tools (`conversation_search`, `conversation_hybrid_search`, `memory_search`, `conversation_timeline`, …) discoverable through `airis-find` and routable when called.

## Why

mindbase was registered but **none of its tools surfaced via `airis-find`**, so they were effectively invisible to agents:

1. mindbase was absent from `TOOL_CATALOG` (the keyword index `airis-find` searches).
2. The mindbase entry in `mcp-config.json` had no `tools_index` (used to auto-enable COLD servers on first native tool call).
3. A latent `find()` bug: the TOOL_CATALOG keyword fallback only runs `if not matched_tools` and **skips tools already cached in `self._tools`**. Once a COLD server's `tools_index` is cached, its tools land in `self._tools`, but the primary search only substring-matches the full query against name/description — so a keyword query like `"search past conversations"` never matched `conversation_search`, and it fell through both paths.

## Changes

- **`tool_suggester.py`** — add a `"mindbase"` entry to `TOOL_CATALOG` with keywords for `conversation_*` / `memory_*` / `content_*` tools.
- **`dynamic_mcp.py`** — in `find()`, also match cached tools against their `TOOL_CATALOG` keywords (not just substring), so keyword queries surface cached COLD-server tools. General fix, not mindbase-specific.
- **`mcp-config.json.example`** — add `tools_index` to the mindbase server for auto-discovery/routing.

## Verification

Rebuilt the gateway image and confirmed end-to-end on a live gateway:

```
airis-find "search my past conversations history"
→ mindbase:conversation_search, mindbase:conversation_hybrid_search,
  mindbase:memory_search, mindbase:conversation_timeline, …
airis-schema conversation_search → full input schema returned
```

(Backing data: 191 Claude Code conversations populated in the mindbase DB; semantic search verified against the same embedding path — qwen3-embedding:0.6b, 1024-dim.)

body:
## Security fix (P0 — preview server hardening, part 3 / final)

Completes the preview-server remediation. Builds on **#13** (loopback bind) and **#14** (strict CORS + CSRF + validation + GitHub allow-list). Off clean `main` — standalone PR.

Closes the residual gap PR-1b intentionally left (loopback no-Origin tooling could still perform state changes) and hardens the **opt-in external-bind** path: even there, a LAN caller can neither obtain nor forge the token.

### Token threat model
- Server mints a **per-process** CSPRNG token.
- `GET /preview-token` returns it **only to loopback callers** (`Host` check) **and** CORS-restricted to the configurator origin. A LAN attacker reaches the server via its routable IP → `Host` isn't loopback → 403; a foreign browser page can't read the response → CORS. No Vite/file coupling, no startup race.
- State-changing endpoints (the 3 POSTs + token-backed `GET /api/github/user-repos`) require a valid `X-Preview-Token` (**401**) on top of the origin/CSRF check (**403**), via `authorizeStateChange()` (origin first → 403, then token → 401). Constant-time token comparison.

### Changes
**Server:** `serverAuth.js` (token mint, loopback-Host gate, constant-time check); `GET /preview-token`; token enforcement; `X-Preview-Token` allowed in CORS.
**SPA:** `previewToken.js` (fetch-once + cache + retry); token attached to every state-changing call (`configStore` save-local-config, `GitHubSaveUIManager` user-repos + save-config, `SvgPreviewRenderer` generate-preview, `ServerTest`).

> The `style:` commit is an **isolated, mechanical** prettier reformat of `configStore.js` (the SPA files predate the repo's `semi:false` config). Keeps the security diff reviewable. No `.svelte` reformat (no prettier-svelte plugin).

### Tests & acceptance
- `vitest run`: **476 pass** (new: serverAuth 10, authorizeStateChange 5, previewToken 3). `eslint .` clean.
- [x] Existing local configurator flow still works.
- [x] Foreign-origin requests can't read the token or perform state changes.
- [x] LAN callers on opt-in external bind can't obtain the token via `/preview-token`.
- [x] Missing/invalid token rejected (401); valid token happy path works.

### Manual verification (booted server)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /preview-token` from loopback (origin localhost:5173) | 200 + 64-char token |
| `GET /preview-token` with spoofed non-loopback `Host` | **403** |
| state change, allowed origin, **no** token | **401** |
| state change, allowed origin, **valid** token, bad body | 400 (auth passed → validation) |
| state change, **foreign** origin + token | **403** (origin checked first) |
| **End-to-end SPA flow:** fetch token (origin localhost:5173) → `POST /generate-preview` with token | **200 + `<svg>`** |

### Note for the PM
Per your direction, **PR-4 (CI verify gate) should come next** so normal merges stop requiring owner override (these PRs don't trigger the `build` check due to the `pull_request.paths` gap). I'll resequence: PR-4 → PR-2 (license) → PR-3 (workspaces) → PR-5 (reliability spine).

🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix Magick.NET SSRF/XXE via strict policymap

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: Magick.NET allows potentially unsafe remote/local fetch coders (HTTP, HTTPS, MVG, MSL, EPHEMERAL, URL) by default, leading to SSRF and XXE when processing user-provided images.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could supply a malicious image/payload that forces the server to make internal network requests (SSRF) or read sensitive files (XXE).
🔧 Fix: Initialized Magick.NET with a strict `policymap` inside the `ImageMagickTransformer` static constructor to explicitly disable these unsafe coders globally before any image processing.
✅ Verification: Ran `dotnet build` successfully. Reviewed file changes to ensure the policy is correctly applied in the static constructor. Added security journal entry.

body:
## Describe the changes in the pull request

1. **Current:** The GC repair callback receives `(&RSIndexResult, &IndexBlock)`. `numeric_range_tree`'s HLL accumulator-split logic relies on `std::ptr::eq(block, last_block_ptr)` to decide whether to fold a block's registers into the without-last-block or with-last-block HLL.
2. **Change:** Add a logical block index alongside the block reference, but wrap both in a `RepairContext<'a>` struct (marked `#[non_exhaustive]`) so future fields can ride along without breaking the callback signature. Switch `numeric_range_tree` from pointer equality to `ctx.block_idx == last_block_idx`.
3. **Outcome:** Decouples the repair callback from pointer identity of blocks. Required for the upcoming snapshot model where blocks are walked from an owned point-in-time view, not the live index. Behavior is identical on master.

#### Which additional issues this PR fixes
1. MOD-16141

#### Main objects this PR modified
1. `src/redisearch_rs/inverted_index/src/gc.rs` — new `RepairContext<'a>` struct
2. `src/redisearch_rs/inverted_index/src/index/index_block.rs` — `repair` passes `RepairContext` instead of `&IndexBlock`
3. `src/redisearch_rs/numeric_range_tree/src/tree/gc.rs` — switch HLL accumulator split to logical `block_idx`
4. `src/redisearch_rs/c_entrypoint/inverted_index_ffi/src/lib.rs` — FFI wrapper unpacks `ctx.block` for the C callback (FFI shape unchanged)

- [ ] This PR introduces API changes
- [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes

Tracking epic: [MOD-16139](https://redislabs.atlassian.net/browse/MOD-16139)

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches fork-GC repair and numeric-range-tree HLL accounting, but logic is equivalent to pointer comparison today and the public C callback is unchanged.

> **Overview**
> Introduces **`RepairContext`** for inverted-index GC repair callbacks so callers get the source block plus its **logical `block_idx`**, not only a block pointer. **`scan_gc`** / **`IndexBlock::repair`** now invoke repair as `(record, &RepairContext)`; **`block_idx`** is threaded through the block loop.

author: nadaverell
body:
## What & why

Radar's GitOps **detail page** parses Argo/Flux failures into a plain-English cause + a one-click remediation (e.g. "destination namespace doesn't exist → create `demo-broken-sync`"). But the cluster-wide **issues engine** — which feeds `/api/issues`, MCP (`issues`, `diagnose`), and AI context — only saw a single `gitops_sync_failed` category with no cause, and **never read `status.operationState.message`**, so a failed sync was invisible to every API/MCP consumer. The same failure had different truth depending on entry point.

This consolidates the two: **one shared parser** (`pkg/gitops/diagnose`, stdlib-only, imported by both engines), the issues engine as the canonical author of issue truth, and the detail page enriched with what the issues engine knows. `buildIssues` is intentionally **not** demoted — see "Not in this PR".

## Changes

**Issues engine → API / MCP (forward direction)**
- **`pkg/gitops/diagnose/` (new):** the Argo operation-error pattern table + condition/Flux action maps as vocabulary-neutral primitives. `insights` calls it via an adapter (behaviour-preserving — pinned by a cross-package constant test).
- **`detect_gitops`:** reads `operationState.message` → `OperationFailed` (critical) with parsed cause + remediation. A failed operation **outranks** a Degraded health rollup (the failed apply is the root cause; the degraded health is a downstream symptom) so the row keeps the honest `gitops_operation_failed` category. An empty operation message defers to a specific error condition. Adds stuck-drift-loop detection. **SyncError** conditions also get the parsed diagnosis.
- **Issue age** for failed operations/conditions comes from `operationState.finishedAt/startedAt` + condition `lastTransitionTime` — so "Started Nd ago" reflects the failure, not the Application's age.
- **Wire fields** (additive, `omitempty`): `cause` / `action` / `remediation_kind` / `remediation_target` / `operation_retry_count` / `stuck` on `issuesapi.Issue`, carried through grouping only when members agree, and **filterable via CEL/MCP** (`stuck && operation_retry_count >= 5`).
- **Categories:** `gitops_sync_failed` split into `render_failed` / `spec_invalid` / `operation_failed` / `out_of_sync` / `health_degraded` (fallback preserved).
- **MCP `diagnose`** accepts `application`/`kustomization`/`helmrelease`: reconciler status summary + parsed-cause related issues, no pod fan-out.
- **Parity guard:** the issues engine and the detail page (`insights.Build`) must surface the same parsed cause + remediation for a failed operation — both call `pkg/gitops/diagnose`, so the two authors can't drift on the diagnosis (catches precedence regressions).

**Issues engine → detail page (L4 bridge)**
- When Argo reports a managed resource as **Degraded/Missing**, the detail page now shows the concrete workload "why" (crashloop / oom / image-pull / unschedulable / pvc-pending) the issues engine already classified, instead of "open the resource drawer". Backed by a vocab-neutral `ResourceProblems` resolver method + a **compose-once-per-request** `RelatedIssuesFrom` (group-normalized so built-in workloads actually match).

**Issues page UX**
- Expanded rows **lead with the plain-English Cause**, then Next step, then "Stuck · retried N×", with the raw controller message demoted (matching the detail-page failure card).
- A **GitOps reconciler subject deep-links to its detail page** (via `gitOpsRouteForResource`) instead of the dead-end resource drawer; member resources still open the resource view.

## Notes

- **`issuesapi` is a stable wire contract consumed by Radar Cloud.** The new fields are additive-optional (safe); the new `gitops_*` category strings are additive enum values — fine for consumers with a default arm, worth a heads-up for any exhaustive switch.
- Verified live against `gitops-demo` (consistent cause + remediation across `/api/issues`, MCP, and the detail page) and against a real cluster's CNPG webhook failure. All package tests + `go vet` + `tsc` pass; CI + Cursor Bugbot green.

### Not in this PR (deliberate)
- **P3.3 (demote `buildIssues`)** — deferred for a **structural** reason, not wire-thinness: the issues engine groups by K8s ownerRef, not Argo ownership, so `RelatedIssues(application)` can't gather an Application's managed-resource issues — only `buildIssues`' `status.resources[]` walk does. Full demotion would *move* that orchestration, not remove it. The parity guard locks the diagnosis against drift meanwhile.
- **`*Warning` conditions** and **manual-drift** — advisory; detail-page-only by choice (would make the live Issues stream chatty).
- **Lifecycle / finalizer-stuck** in the issues engine — broken-not-advisory, but deferred for audit overlap (its own decision).
- The broader Argo-parity gaps tracked in #601 (sync windows, wave gating, SSA/Helm drift, Argo API).

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches issue classification, additive API/MCP wire fields, and GitOps detection precedence; broad test coverage and parity guards limit drift, but consumers with exhaustive category switches need awareness of new `gitops_*` values.
> 
> **Overview**
> Unifies GitOps failure diagnosis so the **issues API/MCP** and the **GitOps detail page** surface the same plain-English cause, next steps, and structured fixes (e.g. create-namespace).

> **Shared parsing:** New `pkg/gitops/diagnose` holds Argo operation-error parsing and Flux/condition action maps; `detect_gitops` and `pkg/gitops/insights` both consume it (insights via an adapter), with a parity test for failed-operation diagnosis.

Those fields flow through compose/grouping (diagnosis only when members agree) and **CEL/MCP filters**.

author: aminsato
body:
## Summary

Akash (AKT) transactions were being rejected by the network for an insufficient fee. Akash's chain-registry gas price (0.025 uakt/gas) on a ~300k-gas transaction computes only **7500 uakt (0.0075 AKT)**, which is below the minimum the network's validators accept. `CosmosFeeService` hardcoded that 7500 uakt for Akash, so the wallet overrode any user-supplied fee back down to 0.0075 AKT.

This floors the Akash default fee to **25000 uakt (0.025 AKT)** — the minimum the network accepts — by pulling Akash out of the shared 7500-uakt branch into its own branch, following the existing `OSMOSIS_MIN_FEE_UOSMO` pattern.

## Suggested solution

This matches the fix suggested directly on the issue:

> I think for this one the minimum gas fee forced by the wallet just needs to be increased to 0.025 AKT. we tried forcing it through our own ui but the wallet still overrode it to 0.0075.

— https://github.com/vultisig/vultisig-android/issues/4307#issuecomment-4332383790

It also mirrors the equivalent fix on vultisig-windows (`keplrMinInjectedFee.Akash = 25_000n`, PR vultisig/vultisig-windows#4025).

## Changes

- `CosmosFeeService.kt` — add `AKASH_MIN_FEE_UAKT = 25_000L` and a dedicated `Chain.Akash` fee branch (0.025 AKT). Other Cosmos chains are unchanged.
- `CosmosFeeServiceTest.kt` — add a test asserting the Akash default fee floors to 25000 uakt.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :data:testDebugUnitTest --tests "*.CosmosFeeServiceTest"` passes (incl. the new Akash floor test and the unchanged 7500-uakt assertions for GaiaChain/QBTC).
- [x] ktfmt formatting applied.
- Manual: send a small AKT amount and confirm the verify screen shows a **0.025 AKT** fee and the tx broadcasts and confirms on-chain (mintscan shows 25000 uakt fee).

## Notes / scope

This is a focused fix for the fee floor, equivalent to the vultisig-windows PR. It corrects the fee for all Akash transactions but does not add a native Akash *staking* UI (Android has none for Akash yet) — that would be a separate, larger feature.

Closes #4307

author: 64johnlee
body:
## Summary

Addresses two related usability issues:

- **Closes #189** — Adds an `instructions` string to the `McpServer` initialization in `mcp-server.js`. MCP clients that support the [2025-06-18 spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/schema#initializeresult-instructions) will now receive a brief description of the server's capabilities and a heads-up about deployment duration on first connection.

- **Closes #134** — Adds a step 3 under the Node.js setup guide in `README.md` explaining how to configure a longer MCP client timeout. Cloud Run deployments trigger a Cloud Build that can take several minutes; the default 60-second timeout in some clients (notably Gemini CLI) causes premature disconnects. The README now clarifies that the build continues on GCP even after a disconnect, and shows the Gemini CLI `timeout` config with a 5-minute value.

## Changes

**`mcp-server.js`** — Added `instructions` field to `McpServer` options:
```js
instructions:
  'Use this server to deploy and manage applications on Google Cloud Run. ' +
  'Available tools: deploy source code or file contents to Cloud Run, list services, ' +
  'get service details, and retrieve service logs. ' +
  'Note: deployments trigger a Cloud Build and can take several minutes to complete.',
```

**`README.md`** — Added optional step 3 under "Using Node.js":
> Cloud Run deployments trigger a Cloud Build, which can take several minutes to complete. If your MCP client disconnects with a timeout error before the build finishes, increase the client timeout. The build continues running on GCP even after a client disconnect.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `npm run test:local` — existing tests should pass unchanged (no logic modified)
- [ ] Run `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node mcp-server.js` and verify the `instructions` field appears in the `InitializeResult` response

body: ## Bug and impact When a user leaves the dashboard and returns within the subscription registry grace window (~100ms), `clearUserListsSyncState` wipes in-memory sync state while the Firestore owned-list listener stays alive. PR #134 correctly gates dashboard pruning on `ownedListsHydrated`, but after state reset `ownedListsHydrated` never flipped back to `true` until a new Firestore snapshot arrived. **Impact:** Saved-list removals (and other prune-dependent dashboard updates) could fail to persist locally. Stale saved lists could linger on the dashboard indefinitely until an unrelated owned-list Firestore event occurred. ## Root cause `initUserListsSyncState` reseeded saved-list IDs from profile cache on resubscribe, but did not restore owned-list hydration. With the listener reused via grace-window refcounting, no new owned-list snapshot fired, leaving `ownedListsHydrated = false` and blocking all `syncCachedUserLists` prune operations. ## Fix On sync state initialization, hydrate `ownedLists` from `getCachedUserLists` when local dashboard cache exists (filtering out `isSavedList` rows). This restores `ownedListsHydrated` during grace-window resubscribe without reintroducing the original cache-wipe race (first load with empty cache still waits for Firestore). ## Validation - Added failing test: `prunes saved-list removals after sync state reset within subscription grace` - All 159 tests pass (`npm test -- --run`)

author: jandubois
body:
## Why

We are merging rancher-desktop-app into this repository (to become
rancher-desktop-2). The app will live at the repository root, so this PR moves
the daemon's code into `rdd/` first, clearing the root of the directories that
would otherwise collide with the app (`pkg/`, `bats/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`).

This is step one. The app import and the reconciliation of the root-anchored
files come later.

## What moved

Everything daemon-specific moved under `rdd/`: `cmd/ pkg/ config/ bats/ docs/
scripts/ go.mod go.sum Makefile macos-entitlements.plist .golangci.yml .ltag/
NOTICE README.md`. The module path is unchanged, so imports are untouched.

## What stays at the root, and why

- `.github/` and `.gitmodules` are anchored there by GitHub and git.
- `LICENSE` covers the whole repository.
- A root `Makefile` runs the repo-wide checks. Spelling covers the entire tree
  (its two driver scripts stay in the root `scripts/`); the spelling config and
  the check-spelling submodule stay under `.github/`.
- `ltag` stays scoped to `rdd/`. rancher-desktop-app checks license headers
  with its own tooling and carries no SPDX headers, so a repo-wide ltag would
  flag every app file. It widens to the whole repository later.

## Commits

1. `Move daemon code into the rdd/ subdirectory` — pure `git mv` (306 files at
   100% rename similarity), kept separate so open PRs rebase cleanly.
2. `Run spelling from a root Makefile; keep ltag scoped to rdd/`.
3. `Point CI workflows at the rdd/ subdirectory`.

## Verified locally

`build-rdd`, `test`, `lint-rdd` (0 issues), `lint-bats`, and `check-ltag` all
pass from `rdd/`; the spelling generator walks the whole tree from the root.
The BATS suite and end-to-end spelling run in CI.

## Note for reviewers with open PRs

You will need to rebase. Edits to moved files follow the rename, but new files
land at their old paths and need a manual `git mv`, and the `bats.yaml` ->
`rdd-bats.yaml` rename may surface.

author: 0kam
body:
## What

Fixes the bug where the species picker showed **no Japanese vernacular name (和名) anywhere** — not in the search dropdown, not in the annotation-set palette — even with UI locale = `ja`.

### Root cause (3 backend defects, empirically verified)
1. **Search** — GBIF search was locale-unaware and read only GBIF `/species/search`'s inline `vernacularNames`, which is near-empty (no `jpn` for common species). The ja-capable sources were never used; the iNaturalist `ja` fallback only fired on 0 GBIF results.
2. **Palette** — `_build_palette` returned `common_name=None` unconditionally.
3. **Materialize** — `from-gbif` persisted the common name always as `locale="en"`.

(The "DB has almost no ja rows" symptom was downstream of #2/#3, not the cause.)

## Changes

**Backend**
- Thread `locale` through gbif-search → `search_species_full`. For **non-en** locales, live-enrich the top-8 results' vernacular: **iNaturalist** (exact scientific-name match, *locale-verified* to reject English fallback) → **GBIF `/species/{key}/vernacularNames`** → English → scientific. Concurrency-capped (4), per-source timeout (700ms) + total budget (~1.5s) with graceful fallback, rate-limited, Redis-cached (14d hit / 1d miss). **English search makes zero extra external calls.** Locale normalized to primary subtag (`ja-JP`→`ja`).
- `_build_palette` resolves `common_name` via local `resolve_vernacular_names(locale)` — **no live external calls in the display path**.
- `from-gbif` accepts language-tagged `vernacular_names` and persists them under the correct locale: idempotent, source allow-listed, length-capped, never overwriting an existing name. The legacy English `common_name` is derived from the `en` entry (not the client's locale-resolved display name). ja-backfill task enqueued only when no ja row truly exists.

**Frontend**
- Pass `getLocale()` to GBIF/local search; fix `resolveGbifCommonName` precedence (locale entry wins over English `vernacular_name`); send `vernacular_names` on materialize; thread locale into the annotation-set detail query key.

## Design (decided with Codex)
Live-enrich at search + persist on materialize + **display resolves from local DB/cache only**. Source: iNat-primary + GBIF per-key fallback (iNat reliably covers e.g. ツバメ which GBIF lacks).

## Review
code-reviewer + Codex — both **GO-with-fixes**; all findings applied (iNat locale verification, end-to-end `source` typing, locale normalization, ja-backfill condition, rate-limiter on enrichment, persist hardening, and the legacy-en-common_name derivation found in Gate 3).

## Verification
- **Gate 1**: ruff + mypy clean; frontend `npm run check` 0 errors; paraglide lint clean.
- **Gate 2**: backend tests pass (+new unit/integration for enrichment, palette, materialize, iNat-fallback-reject, no-overwrite); frontend vitest 42/42.
- **Gate 3** (dev `/ja`): search "Passer montanus"/"Hirundo rustica" → dropdown shows 和名 (雀/スズメ/ツバメ), gbif-search sends `locale=ja`; add to palette → item shows "スズメ (Passer montanus saturatus)"; `/en` toggle shows English. Console 0 errors.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
- Seeding worker: relax `gbif_taxon_key IS NOT NULL` gate / run `resolve_gbif_batch` first so background ja-fetch covers key-less taxa.
- `services/vernacular.py` optional admin/refresh live fallback for display.

### Description
- Extended the core model by adding `import_source: str | None` and `cash_flow_type: Literal["inflow","outflow","transfer"] | None` to `Transaction` and added `stable_import_source` logic and `import_source_default` fallbacks for backward compatibility; updated `FlowType` to include `transfer` (`src/core/models.py`).
- Extended `Rule` with optional `import_source` and `applies_to_source` and changed `RuleEngine` ordering to prefer source-specific rules at equal priority, allow `transfer` rules to match either sign, and set `cash_flow_type` on rule classification (`src/core/rules.py`).

body:
## Problem

Trends bar charts render flat, square-cornered bars with a hover highlight that snaps in. This is a visual polish pass on the hog-charts bar chart.

## Changes

- New `fillStyle` option on quill-charts `BarsConfig` (`flat` | `gradient` | `gloss`), applied per-bar in `makeBarFill` (canvas-renderer). `gradient` is a diagonal light→dark sheen; `gloss` is a curved radial highlight.
- Trends bar charts (both the vertical time-series path and the horizontal breakdown path) now use `gloss` fill with a 4px corner radius.
- Hover highlight eases in over 180ms (`animateHover`) on the trends bar configs, instead of snapping.
- Extracted the hover-animation RAF loop out of `useChartDraw` into a new `useHoverAnimation` hook, with a shared `clearAndPrepare` helper in `clearCanvas.ts`. `useChartDraw` keeps the static-layer draw and delegates hover to the new hook.
- Added a `FillStyles` Storybook story comparing flat / gradient / gloss on a horizontal breakdown chart.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent — verification was per-file TypeScript checks on the changed quill-charts files (no type errors) and confirming the dev server + quill Storybook compiled. No automated tests were added. Visual verification of the gloss fill, rounded corners, and hover ease-in still needs a human (the quill Storybook `FillStyles` story is the easiest place to look).

## Publish to changelog?

## 🤖 Agent context

Authored with Claude Code (Opus 4.8). This was an iterative, design-driven session exploring how to make trends bars "more posthoggy."

Notable decisions:
- Tried a logo-style "facet" fill (three hard diagonal bands echoing the PostHog logo spikes) but it read as blocky color-blocks on thin bars, so it was removed in favor of the smoother `gradient` and curved `gloss`.
- Explored pastel colors, then confirmed the chart palette is the app-wide `--data-color-*` set (defined in `frontend/src/styles/base.scss`, not quill at runtime) — so a recolor would repaint every chart and belongs with design, not this branch. No palette changes were made.
- Attempted a hover fade-*out* on cursor-leave (in addition to the fade-in) but couldn't get it to fire reliably through the interaction/overlay layers, so it was reverted; only the fade-in ships. The `useHoverAnimation` extraction was kept as a standalone cleanup.

body:
## Describe the changes in the pull request

1. **Current:** `scan_gc` accepts `impl FnMut(&RSIndexResult<'index>, &RepairContext<'index>)` where `'index` is tied to `&self`. That signature lets the closure stash an `RSIndexResult<'index>` borrow and use it after the call — sound today because all callers walk synchronously, but not sound once `scan_gc` walks an owned snapshot whose blocks live only for the function body.
2. **Change:** Switch the closure bound to a higher-ranked trait bound (HRTB): `for<'snap> FnMut(&RSIndexResult<'snap>, &RepairContext<'snap>)`. Because the closure must work for any `'snap`, it can't persist a borrow with a specific lifetime. As a side-effect, `scan_gc` on `InvertedIndex`, `EntriesTrackingIndex`, and `FieldMaskTrackingIndex` no longer needs an `'index` lifetime parameter. Rename `IndexBlock::repair`'s `'index` to `'block` for clarity.
3. **Outcome:** Borrows from each repair callback invocation are statically scoped to that call, removing the soundness blocker for the snapshot-based reader in subsequent PRs. No behavior change.

#### Which additional issues this PR fixes
1. MOD-16142

#### Main objects this PR modified
1. `src/redisearch_rs/inverted_index/src/gc.rs` — HRTB on `scan_gc`, drop `'index` lifetime
2. `src/redisearch_rs/inverted_index/src/index/index_block.rs` — rename `'index` → `'block`
3. `src/redisearch_rs/numeric_range_tree/src/test_utils.rs` — closure types follow new bound

author: raz-mon
body:
## Describe the changes in the pull request

1. **Current:** `build.sh` wires `sccache` in as the C/C++ compiler launcher (`CMAKE_C/CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER`) whenever the `sccache` binary is present and executable. It never verifies that the sccache *server* can actually start. When the server fails to come up (e.g. the remote S3 cache is unreachable), every compile invocation errors out and the whole build dies with a cascade of `Error 2` failures across unrelated targets (hiredis, snowball, etc.).
2. **Change:** Before enabling the launcher, probe the server with `sccache --show-stats`. If it starts, use sccache as before; if it fails to start, print a warning and build **without** sccache. `--show-stats` is idempotent — it spawns the server if needed, connects to an already-running one otherwise, and fails only if the server cannot start.
3. **Outcome:** A transient sccache/remote-cache outage now degrades gracefully to a slower, uncached-but-successful build instead of failing the job. Because the fix lives in `build.sh`, it protects local builds as well as CI.

#### Main objects this PR modified
1. `build.sh` — `prepare_cmake_arguments()` sccache setup

#### Mark if applicable

- [ ] This PR introduces API changes
- [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes

#### Release Notes

- [ ] This PR requires release notes
- [x] This PR does not require release notes

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Build-script-only change that improves resilience when sccache is unavailable; no product runtime or API impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`build.sh`** no longer enables sccache solely because the binary exists. In `prepare_cmake_arguments()`, it runs **`sccache --show-stats`** first; only if that succeeds does it set **`CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER`** / **`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER`** as before.
> 
> If the server cannot start (e.g. remote cache unreachable), the script logs a **warning** plus the probe output, then **clears** the compiler launcher CMake variables so reconfigures in an existing build dir do not keep a broken sccache wired in. Builds continue **without** cache instead of failing every compile.

author: micode-ai
body:
## Problem

Two bugs in the static web build (https://ai-budget.pl), reported by a user:

1. **Login works but no accounts show.** Nothing else loads because without a selected account the `X-Account-Id` header is empty.
2. After a redirect the URL became malformed: `https://ai-budget.pl/ai-budget.pl/expenses` (domain duplicated in the path), then errored.

## Root causes

**1. Accounts not loading**
- `executeSql` was **missing entirely** from `apps/mobile/src/db/client.web.ts` (the web SQLite mock). Repositories import `executeSql` from `./client`, which Metro resolves to `client.web.ts` on web → the import was `undefined` and every repository call threw at runtime.
- `accountStore` inserts server accounts into SQLite then **reads them back** to build state. On web that read-back is a no-op mock, so the accounts the API returned were dropped.

**2. Doubled-domain deep-link path**
- The deep-link handler in `app/_layout.tsx` was written for the native custom scheme `budget://expense/voice`, where the first path segment lands in `URL.host`, so it builds `fullPath = /${host}${pathname}`.
- On web, `Linking.getInitialURL()` returns the full browser URL `https://ai-budget.pl/expenses`, whose `host` is the **domain** → it built `/ai-budget.pl/expenses` and `router.push`ed it → `https://ai-budget.pl/ai-budget.pl/expenses`.

## Changes

- **`client.web.ts`**: add the missing `executeSql` (+ `QueryResult` type) export as a no-op resolving to `[]`, so web repository calls stop throwing.
- **`accountStore.ts`**: in `initialize` and `loadAccountsFromServer`, fall back to the server account payload when the local SQLite read-back is empty (via a new `toAccountWithRole` normalizer). Native is unchanged — the fallback only triggers when the local read returns nothing.
- **`_layout.tsx`**: skip the deep-link effect on web (Expo Router already routes browser URLs natively), and distinguish `http(s)` URLs from custom-scheme URLs in the parser so native App Links / Universal Links can't hit the same host-as-segment corruption.

## Native (iOS/Android) impact

None.
- `client.web.ts` is web-only (`.web.ts`); native uses `client.native.ts`.
- `accountStore` fallback is skipped whenever the local DB returns rows (normal native path) — behavior is byte-for-byte identical.
- The deep-link parser's `else` branch reproduces the original logic exactly. Verified against the actual widget URIs (`budget://expense/voice`, `/receipt`, `/new`) → identical output. The new `http(s)` branch is unreachable on native today (no App Links registered for `ai-budget.pl`).

## Notes

- Deps aren't installed in the dev environment, so a full `typecheck` couldn't run here; changes are small and type-safe. Please confirm in CI.
- These fixes take effect on web only after a rebuild — the `web-deploy.yml` workflow runs on push to `development`.

body: ## Summary Fixes two mobile TOC drawer issues on all subpages (PCV, BridgeDP, Huawei, Huikon, marriage): 1. **Semi-transparent backdrop covered the drawer** — `.section` uses `content-visibility: auto`, which traps `position: fixed` descendants inside the section’s containing block. The overlay (appended to `body`) then painted above the drawer. 2. **Incorrect top/bottom offsets** — For the same reason, `top`/`bottom` were measured from the section instead of the viewport, so the drawer shifted when scrolling. ## Approach Aligned with the [Humanoid notebooks](https://imchong.github.io/Humanoid_Robot_Learning_Paper_Notebooks/) mobile TOC pattern: - Disable `content-visibility` containment on sections that host `.subpage-detail-layout` - Mobile z-index stack: header `1200`, overlay `1250`, drawer `1300`, FAB `1350` - Full-height drawer: `top: 0`, `bottom: calc(24px + 48px + 28px + safe-area)` - Fixed header + `main` top padding on subpages at `≤1200px` - `overflow-x: clip` on mobile to avoid horizontal scroll on long articles - Unified breakpoint to `1200px` in CSS and JS ## Verification - `npm run check` passes - Playwright mobile test on PCV page: drawer receives pointer events above overlay, `top: 0` before and after scroll ## Files changed - `css/style.css` — mobile TOC drawer layout and stacking fixes - `js/main.js` — matchMedia breakpoint `1200px`

author: cobriensr
body:
## Summary

**Once a Lottery Finder or Silent Boom alert appears, it never disappears for the rest of the trading day — absolutely.** Implements the spec in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-06-feed-never-vanish-design.md`.

## Why

The feeds did a straight **replace** every poll with no client-side pinning, so any server hiccup dropped already-visible rows. Investigation found three real vanish vectors: (1) heavy reignition/badge CTEs hitting `degradeOnTimeout(... [])` → "Hot Right Now" blanks for a poll (~258×/day historically); (2) live Q1/Q2 quintile-suppression flips removing a ticker's chains mid-session; (3) Silent Boom having no monotonic gate (safe only by frozen columns). A client-side absolute union neutralizes all three independent of the backend.

## Mechanism

- New `useStickyUnion<T>(items, { key, storageKey })` — upserts every item the server returns, **never deletes**, persists to `localStorage[storageKey]`, resets when `storageKey` (the date) changes. Render-loop-safe (content-aware guard).
- **Lottery** pins fires + the reignited ("Hot Right Now") rows, keyed by `optionChainId` (stable across reignites; the row `id` rotates and is correctly not used), day-scoped.
- **Silent Boom** pins alerts keyed by the composite **`optionChainId|bucketCt`** — required because SB is one row per spike bucket, so two buckets of the same chain are distinct alerts that must pin independently.
- Union active on the live view (`minute/bucket==null && page===0`); historical scrubs/pages show the raw point-in-time response; the union persists across the detour and resumes on return. Page>0 de-dupes already-pinned rows; per-ticker counts + totals are floored at the union so pinned rows are never under-counted.

## Tests

- `useStickyUnion`: 8 tests (pin, update, reset, persist/hydrate, malformed JSON, guards) — non-vacuous (sabotage-verified).
- Lottery + Silent Boom: never-vanish (omit-on-poll-2 keeps the row), update-in-place, date-reset, page-dedup, count-floor, SB same-chain-two-buckets — all confirmed to FAIL without the wiring.

author: hahwul
body:
## Problem

On the docs site, the footer (`.site-footer`) spans the full viewport width, but the sidebar (and TOC) are `position: fixed` and overlay it (`z-index: 150`). The footer's content is centered (`max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto`) across the full width with no offset for those fixed columns.

At awkwardly small window widths (roughly the range where the sidebar is still visible, ~769–1100px), the centered footer content — the copyright line and "Documentation built with Hwaro" — slides underneath the fixed sidebar and gets cut off.

## Fix

- **Reserve the fixed columns' space on the footer**, scoped to docs pages only via `.docs-layout ~ .site-footer`. The landing page has no `.docs-layout`, so it keeps the original full-width footer.
  - `padding-left` accounts for the sidebar (`--sidebar-w`).
  - `padding-right` accounts for the TOC (`--toc-w`) only above 1100px, where the TOC is actually visible.
  - The offset is reset back to `2rem` at the mobile breakpoint (≤768px) where the sidebar slides off-screen.
- **Let the footer wrap when space is tight**, like the mobile layout: added `flex-wrap: wrap` + `gap` to `.footer-inner` and `flex-wrap: wrap` to `.footer-branding`, so the branding/links rows break onto new lines instead of overflowing.

CSS-only change; no template or content changes.

author: joselunasrt8-creator
body:
ensureSchema() previously executed CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, and
CREATE TRIGGER statements in a single sequential pass before calling
ensureRequiredSchemaColumns(). Against legacy live databases where a
table was created before a column was added by a later migration (e.g.
execution_registry.validated_object_hash, added in
migrations/0004_enforcement_lock.sql), the CREATE INDEX statement
referencing that column threw "no such column" before the repair pass
ever ran, surfacing as POST /session -> {status: NULL, reason:
missing_required_column}.

Split stmts into a CREATE TABLE phase and a post-table phase
(indexes/triggers), and run ensureRequiredSchemaColumns() between them
so legacy tables are backfilled with required columns before any index
or trigger that references those columns is created.

body:
## Summary

Ben flagged that prospects appearing in the Qualified Bookings drilldown were not appearing in the Cost Per Lead drilldown for the same window. Root cause: \`fetchLeads\` was filtering out every typeform whose \`ad_id\` didn't resolve via \`lib_ad_audience\`. So organic, direct, referral, or any not-yet-tracked-form lead became a "phantom" — visible as a booking but invisible as the lead it came from.

This PR drops the ad-attribution filter. Unmapped typeforms now appear with audience \`Untracked\` and a yellow \`untracked\` status pill, distinct from qualified ad-attributed leads. The audience filter chip still excludes them when a specific funnel is selected, so funnel-by-funnel views stay clean.

## Trade-off

Tile vs drilldown count divergence is now intentional — the drilldown is a superset of the Leads tile (which still reads \`leads_d\`, excluding marks + unmapped). This matches the Bookings drilldown shape established in #29.

## Known limit

This only helps when the source typeform was submitted **inside the same window** as the booking. If the lead came in 10 days ago and booked yesterday, a 7-day window will still miss them. That's a separate "show source leads from prior windows" feature — flagged but not in scope.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open \`/sales/marketing\` → Bookings drilldown → pick a known booking whose typeform you suspect was organic/untracked.
- [ ] Open Cost Per Lead drilldown for the same window → confirm that prospect now appears with audience \`Untracked\` + yellow status pill.
- [ ] Confirm the Leads TILE count is unchanged (still ad-attributed only).
- [ ] With an audience filter selected (e.g. only "Restoration"), confirm Untracked rows are excluded from the list.

author: rsafier
body:
## Problem

There's no stable, programmatic way to drive a Tellus player from outside the page. The built-in
autonomous agents (Johnny/Mira/Sol/Atlas) have a rich action vocabulary and an in-world dispatch path,
but it's all internal to `createTellusWorld()`. An external driver (a headless-browser agent runner, an
integration test, a bot) currently has to simulate mouse/keyboard over the WebGPU canvas — brittle — or
reach into minified internals. There's also no way to make such a driver appear as a chosen, stable
visitor; `visitorId` is always a fresh random UUID.

## Solution

Expose a small, stable agent-control API on `window`, attached inside `createTellusWorld()` so it closes
over the same in-world dispatch functions the built-in agents use — external and native agents then share
one action path and coexist as ordinary visitors.

- `window.tellusAgent.getState(radius?)` — position, terrain under you, distances to pond/mountain/shore,
  nearby objects, and the accepted verbs.
- `window.tellusAgent.getNearby(radius?)` — nearest generated objects (id/kind/prompt/distance/direction).
- `window.tellusAgent.sendAction(verb, args)` — verbs mirror the built-in agent vocabulary: `moveSelf`,
  `generate`, `sculptTerrain`, `moveAsset`, `rotateAsset`, `scaleAsset`, `moveAssetToWater` (reusing
  `generate()`, `sculptTerrainAt()`, `moveGenerated()`, `rotateGenerated()`, `scaleGenerated()`,
  `moveGeneratedToWater()`, `sendPresenceUpdate()`).

`tellusVisitorId()` now honors a host-pinned identity — `window.__hyadesIdentity.visitorId` or a
`?visitorId=` query param — before falling back to a fresh random id, so an embodied external agent can
join as a stable, distinct visitor.

The change is purely additive: no existing client/agent behavior changes. Object-literal property names
survive the production build (esbuild doesn't mangle keys/member access by default), and `tsc --noEmit`
is clean.

Example:

```js
window.tellusAgent.getState();                                  // perceive
window.tellusAgent.sendAction("generate", { prompt: "a stone bridge", near: "pond" });
window.tellusAgent.sendAction("moveSelf", { dx: 3, dz: -2 });
```

## Context

This is the game-side half of letting external AI agents play Tellus as embodied players; a companion
driver loads the client headless, pins an identity, and calls these hooks each turn.

body:
## Describe the changes in the pull request

1. **Current:** `InvertedIndex::blocks() -> &[IndexBlock]` is exposed directly and consumed by query iterators, GC, numeric tree scans, and FFI accessors. There's no abstraction for a point-in-time view of the index.
2. **Change:** Introduce a borrowed `InvertedIndexSnapshot<'a>` wrapper exposing `blocks()`, `last_block()`, `num_docs()`, etc. and a new `InvertedIndex::snapshot()` returning it. All current readers are migrated to consume the snapshot wrapper. Underlying storage remains `ThinVec<IndexBlock>` — semantics are identical.
3. **Outcome:** The next PR ([MOD-16144]) can swap the backing store to three regions and return an *owned* snapshot from `snapshot()` without touching any call site. This isolates the API change from the storage change.

#### Which additional issues this PR fixes
1. MOD-16143

#### Main objects this PR modified
1. `src/redisearch_rs/inverted_index/src/index/snapshot.rs` — new borrowed `InvertedIndexSnapshot<'a>`
2. `src/redisearch_rs/inverted_index/src/index/inverted_index.rs` — new `snapshot()` method
3. Migrated readers: query iterators, GC, numeric range tree, `inverted_index_ffi` accessors

#### Mark if applicable

- [x] This PR introduces API changes
- [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes

> API change is internal: `blocks()` callers switch to `snapshot().blocks()`. No public C/FFI signature changes.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches hot query/GC read paths and reader staleness detection; borrowed FFI snapshots require strict lifetime and no-mutation discipline until owned snapshots land.

> **Overview**
> Introduces a borrowed **`InvertedIndexSnapshot`** and **`InvertedIndex::snapshot()`** as the stable way to walk index blocks, ahead of a follow-up storage refactor that can swap in owned snapshots without changing call sites.

GC **`scan_gc`** and numeric-tree repair routing use snapshot block indices (not pointer identity on blocks).
> 
> **FFI/C headers** add **`InvertedIndex_Snapshot`**, **`InvertedIndexSnapshot_*`**, and document that the snapshot must not outlive the index and the index must not be mutated while a borrowed snapshot is alive.

author: caasiyatnilab-sketch
body:
This PR introduces two main performance optimizations to the portfolio website:

1.  **Native CSS Smooth Scrolling**: Replaced the custom JavaScript implementation of smooth scrolling with the native CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth` property. This offloads animation work to the browser's compositor thread, reducing main-thread load and removing unnecessary event listeners. It also restores default anchor behavior, allowing the URL hash to update properly.
2.  **Optimized Script Loading**: Moved the `script.js` tag to the `<head>` and added the `defer` attribute. This allows the script to be downloaded in parallel with HTML parsing without blocking the initial render, improving the time to interactive.

Additionally, I've added a media query to respect `prefers-reduced-motion` settings and reformatted the CSS for better maintainability.

body:
## Summary

The core of the desktop daemon-client refactor (Task #7 in `DESKTOP_REFACTOR_HANDOFF.md`). The Electron app no longer **embeds** the agent engine — it talks to the per-stage daemon over the Unix socket via `DaemonConnector` and owns only native/UI concerns. One runtime (the daemon) now owns the agents, so the desktop and CLI see the same live state and the single-writer guarantee on `dataDir` is real.

Builds on the pre-work in #197 (handshake `stage`/`apiBaseUrl`, `getDaemonPaths`/`resolveStage` exports, late-attach approval snapshot).

## Changes

- **New `DaemonConnection` (main):** connects to `getDaemonPaths(stage).socketPath`, verifies the RPC protocol version, forwards daemon push notifications to the renderer (and opens approval URLs via `shell.openExternal` on the daemon's behalf), and tracks connection state.
- **`main/index.ts`:** drops `AgentRuntimeManager`/`FileAgentConfigManager`/`JsonCronStore` + `EngineConfig` + the `before-quit` engine cleanup. It just connects on launch and disconnects on quit — the daemon owns the agent runtime and lifecycle.
- **`ipc-handler.ts`:** agent/env IPC methods delegate to the connector; native methods (theme/updates/dialog/`getVersion`) stay. Drops the redundant shell-env-on-add (the daemon does it) and the local `shell-env.ts` helper.
- **Connection UX:** new `getDaemonConnection`/`reconnectDaemon` IPC + a `daemon-connection-changed` event. The renderer shows a **"daemon not running" / "protocol mismatch"** gate with a Retry button, and only mounts the agent UI once attached.
- **`@newio/cli`:** `DaemonClient` gains an `onDisconnect` hook so the desktop notices when the daemon stops mid-session.
- Removes the dead `better-sqlite3` external (cron store gone).

## Scope / what's next

Single **build-time stage** for now (connects to the `__NEWIO_STAGE__` daemon socket — same model as today, just as a thin client). The remaining handoff follow-ups will be separate PRs:
- **(Q2)** build-flag-gated dev/integ/prod **env selector** (stage → socket; relaunch on switch).
- **(Q1)** desktop-local **create-account** register flow in the main process.

> **Dev note:** `pnpm dev` now requires a daemon running for the target stage (e.g. `newio daemon run`/`start`). With none running, the app shows the "daemon not running" gate.

## Renderer impact

Minimal by design — the agent event channels are unchanged, so the agent store and panels are untouched. The only new renderer surface is the connection gate.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] JSDoc added for new public APIs
- [x] `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` passes
- [ ] No breaking changes (desktop now **requires** a running daemon; documented above)
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated (n/a — redirects to website)

## Test results

- Build / typecheck / lint / format: ✅
- Tests: ✅ 706 passing (added 5 `DaemonConnection` tests covering connect/handshake/mismatch/disconnect + notification forwarding)

## High-conflict files

`@newio/cli` (`client.ts`) and the connector main/shared IPC contracts.

author: propensive
body:
Two refinements to the crypto permit and cipher APIs: year-based permit levels as an alternative to the named NIST statuses, and initialization vectors that are now always supplied explicitly at the encryption site rather than resolved from a contextual given.

The `crypto` permit package gains year-based levels alongside the named ones, composed from the same fine-grained permits. `permitCryptoThrough<year>` permits every algorithm NIST disallowed on or before that year, so a later year is strictly more permissive:

```scala
import crypto.permitCryptoThrough2030   // DES, MD5, RC2, Blowfish, RSA-1024, 3DES, DSA, SHA-1
```

`permitCryptoThrough2014` covers DES, MD5, RC2, Blowfish and sub-2048-bit RSA/DSA; `…2024` adds Triple-DES and DSA signatures; `…2030` adds SHA-1.

Initialization vectors are now explicit. Instead of an implicit `InitializationVector` given (with a `random` default), the IV strategy is passed at the call site:

```scala
data.encrypt(InitializationVector.random)        // a fresh random IV
data.encrypt(InitializationVector.fixed(bytes))  // deterministic
data.encrypt(InitializationVector.zero)
```

`random`/`fixed`/`zero` are plain values (no givens), and modes or ciphers that don't use an IV (ECB, RSA) ignore the argument. This makes IV selection visible and removes the implicit-resolution machinery (and its contextual-given edge cases) entirely.

body:
Batch 5 (final) of the third-review backlog. Closes #241, #242, #244.

## #241 - Insights 500 on a malformed timezone cookie (low)
A bad percent-escape in the `codex-tz` cookie made `decodeURIComponent` throw and 500 the insights page. The decode is wrapped in try/catch and falls back to UTC.

## #242 - Marker autosave stored unclamped anchors (low)
The scene autosave persisted client-supplied `anchorStart`/`anchorEnd` verbatim, so a stale or crafted client could store out-of-range or inverted ranges (garbage TODO slices, highlights past the end). `updateMarkerAnchors` now clamps anchors to the body length the way `createMarker` does; the autosave and rename-sweep callers pass the new body length.

## #244 - word_count diverges JS vs SQL on Unicode whitespace (low)
`scenes.word_count` is computed in JS (`/\s+/`, Unicode-aware) but insights recomputed it in SQL with POSIX `\s` (ASCII only), so prose using NBSP and similar spaces drifted between the dashboard total and the insights chart. `WORDS_SQL` now normalises the Unicode spaces JS treats as whitespace and counts non-whitespace runs, matching the JS counter (and dropping the trim/empty-element edge too).

## Tests
- `markers.test.ts`: out-of-range anchors are clamped to the body on save.
- `insights.test.ts`: `WORDS_SQL` equals the JS `wordCount` across ASCII and Unicode whitespace samples (NBSP, ideographic, thin space).

| `lib/data/quran_repository.dart` | `open()` sekarang copy `assets/quran.db` ke app docs dir pada first launch; fallback ke programmatic seed kalau asset missing |
| `pubspec.yaml` | + `path_provider: ^2.1.4` (untuk `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`); `assets/quran.db` ditambahkan ke asset bundle |
| `.gitignore` | Section baru: exclude `quran-uthmani.xml` (raw input) + `**/assets/quran.db` (build artefact) dari VCS |
| `README.md` | Credits section: attribution Tanzil Project (CC BY 3.0) |

## Build pipeline

```
data_pipeline/normalizer.py    # 6/6 parity tests pass
data_pipeline/build_quran_db.py quran-uthmani.xml -o quran.db
→ quran.db: 8.7 MB, 114 surahs, 6236 ayahs, 81812 words
```

## Testing

- ✅ Normalizer parity (Python ↔ Dart): 6/6 pass via `python -X utf8 normalizer.py`
- ✅ DB sanity check: surah/ayah/word counts match canonical
- ✅ Sample Al-Fatihah:1 — Uthmani text retains harakat, simple text loose-keyed correctly
- ✅ `git check-ignore` confirms quran.db + xml excluded from VCS
- ⚠️ `flutter analyze` deferred to CI (Flutter SDK not available locally); will be enforced via GitHub Actions in subsequent PR

## Known limitation

No DB migration logic: once asset is copied to docs dir on first launch, subsequent app updates with refreshed `assets/quran.db` will not replace the existing on-device DB (`File(path).exists()` short-circuits). Acceptable for current scope (single-version mushaf). Future tooling should compare an asset version stamp before overwriting.

## Folder migration note

Old `QuranRepository.open()` used `getDatabasesPath()` (sqflite default, typically `/data/data/<pkg>/databases/`); new patch uses `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` (`app_flutter/` or `Documents/`). Pre-patch users will have an orphan seeded DB ~50KB in the old location — harmless, gets cleaned up on app uninstall.

author: debuggingfuture
body:
## Summary

`ci-triage-pr` can now triage **caller-supplied observability signals** alongside the GitHub Actions / Cloudflare Pages failures it reads itself. An Action-mode dispatcher that owns its own scheduling (per § Schedule-ownership, consumers keep their timers in their own repos) collects errors from systems the dispatcher's read capabilities don't reach — an APM/tracing SaaS, Workers runtime exception logs, health probes — and passes them in the dispatch body:

```json
{ "firedAt": 1765000000000,
  "signals": [
    { "source": "workers-observability:my-api",
      "title": "Unhandled exception in fetch handler",
      "detail": "TypeError: … — 12 occurrences over 24h",
      "url": "https://dash.example.com/…", "count": 12 } ] }
```

## Insight

- **Signals count for the green-day check.** Previously a day with zero CI/deploy failures short-circuited before the model call; a runtime-errors-only day would never file a triage. The guard now requires *all three* surfaces empty.
- The run never checks out a repo — its dispatch `github.sha` is dedup/check-run metadata only, so consumers can dispatch it daily with plain `GITHUB_SHA`.

## Rationale

- Caller-collected signals (vs. new read capabilities per SaaS) keep the dispatcher credential-free for third-party observability systems and keep consumer-specific query logic out of the public registry — same posture as the writeback design (#112).
- Caps (50 signals × 2 KB detail ≈ 100 KB worst case) are enforced as Schema refinements, so an oversized dispatch fails as a clean `400 invalid_inputs` with the parse tree at the dispatch gate, well under the CF Workflows params ceiling.

## Key changes

- [ ] `runs/ci-triage-pr.ts` — `Signal` schema + optional `signals` input (defaults `[]`), green-day guard, user-body + report ("Raw signals") + PR-body rendering, `signalsCount` output
- [ ] `runs/ci-triage-pr.test.ts` — signals-only day opens PR + consults model; combined rendering; green-day with empty signals; dispatch-gate decode tests (default, >50 items, over-long detail)

Schedule mode unchanged (cron supplies `signals: []`).

author: kazukinakai
body:
## What
2.4.3 (self-signed) won't launch — dyld kills it: the **hardened runtime's library validation** only loads frameworks whose Team ID matches the main process. A self-signed identity has **no Team ID**, so the main app can't load the bundled (also Team-ID-less) `Sparkle.framework` → `"different Team IDs"`, no Gatekeeper prompt.

## Fix
`package.sh` applies `--options runtime` (hardened runtime) **only to Apple-issued certs** (Developer ID / Apple Development — which carry a Team ID and are what we'd notarize). Self-signed builds sign without it. Verified locally: re-signing 2.4.3 without the hardened runtime → app launches.
