author: felipefuhr
body:
## Summary

Adds `general-claude-judge.yml` — a reusable workflow that uses `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`
to act as a judge over Code Scanning (CodeQL, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks) and SonarCloud findings on a PR.

**Flow:**
1. Caller passes `pr_number`, `head_ref`, `base_ref`
2. Workflow fetches Code Scanning alerts via GitHub API + optionally SonarCloud issues
3. Claude classifies each finding: TRUE_POSITIVE / FALSE_POSITIVE / PRE_EXISTING / NEEDS_INVESTIGATION
4. Posts a single summary table comment on the PR
5. For each TRUE_POSITIVE: creates a `claude/fix-pr-N-slug` branch, makes a minimal fix, opens a draft fix PR targeting the feature branch (not main/develop)

**Triggers (in caller workflows):** label `claude-review` applied to PR, or `@claude` comment.

**Not wired to ci.yml self-test** — requires live PR context. YAML syntax covered by `general-actionlint.yml`. Exception documented in workflow header and AGENTS.md.

## Type of change
- [x] `feat` — new capability or behaviour
- [x] `ci` / `docs` — tooling, workflows, or documentation only

## Test plan
- [ ] No test needed: workflow requires live PR context; actionlint validates YAML via existing self-test
- [ ] Caller PRs open in ffreis-rust-shared and ffreis-go-shared — merge this first, then pin SHA in callers

## Risks and follow-ups
- `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` uses version tag, not SHA — Renovate will pin after merge
- `--allowedTools` flag format may need adjustment after first real invocation (could be `--allowed-tools`)
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret must be added to each caller repo before the workflow can run
- Caller `@main` references must be updated to this PR's merge commit SHA

## What

One-time cleanup of working-tree state left by buggy `relay recurring --all` debug sweeps. The **recurrence fix is #314**; this PR just clears the existing mess (kept out of #314 deliberately).

author: jaenster
body:
Replaces the trust-all MVP with Battle.net's Old Logon System.

- `xsha1.zig` — Blizzard's broken SHA-1 (little-endian I/O, no message-expansion rotate) + the clientToken/serverToken double-hash helper.
- `CREATEACCOUNT2` stores the account's password hash (rejects duplicates); `LOGONRESPONSE2` verifies the double-hash. Unknown accounts auto-register password-less on first login (pvpgn-style), so the existing flows keep working and a password is only enforced once set.
- Accounts persist via the store facade (durable backend; `accounts/<name>` = `has_password ++ pwhash`).

Harness gains the matching xsha1 + `create_account_real_auth` (create / dup-reject / good-login / bad-login-reject) and a fresh data dir per run for isolation. `zig build e2e`: 6 pass, 1 skip (delete_char).

Note: the broken-SHA-1 is internally consistent (server + harness share it); exact real-client bit-compat should be confirmed against a capture later.

## Summary

Adds end-to-end email verification for new signups and surfaces verification state inside the running app.

This PR also rolls up three commits that had not yet reached `develop` (the merge of #7 `feature/auth-features`, the sign-up back-navigation fix + live validators, and a CLAUDE.md branching update), since the branch was based on top of them.

### Email verification (this feature)

**Backend (`detectoo_api`)**

- New `EmailVerificationToken` model + migration; `is_email_verified` column on `User`.

FastCRUD's `create()` only commits the user, so the freshly-added token was being rolled back when the request session closed — every link would have read "invalid or expired." Now the token is durably stored regardless of caller.

**App (`detectoo_app`)**

# fix(validate,eval): image-path traversal containment (E-VAL-012) + slide source-span threading (SEC-001, diag-span) **Epic:** Wave 4 Follow-Up Validation Hardening **Mode:** fix / security hardening **Branch:** `fix/pra-validation-hardening` → `develop` **Convergence:** CONVERGED — 3 commits; fmt + pedantic clippy (unwrap_used denied) + rustdoc -D warnings all green ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-562%2F562_target_suite-brightgreen) ![Workspace](https://img.shields.io/badge/workspace-3428%2F3429-brightgreen) ![Clippy](https://img.shields.io/badge/clippy-pedantic_clean-brightgreen) ![Security](https://img.shields.io/badge/security-CWE--22_contained-blue) --- ## Summary Two Wave-4 follow-up findings resolved in this PR: - **SEC-001 (CWE-22, MED)** — New `ImagePathValidator` (Validator surface #5) in `slideforge-validate` rejects `ImageSpec.path` values that escape the source root: `..` traversal segments (segment-exact, not substring), absolute paths (`/` or `\`), and Windows drive letters. Emits new error code `E-VAL-012` (severity: error, exit 2 in strict mode). Allocated in error-taxonomy v2.19; traces to BC-1.16.001 EC-012. Registered in `slideforge/src/registry.rs` as Surface 5. Pre-emptive containment: no image disk I/O exists yet, so this guards future image loading before it lands. - **diag-span** — The evaluator's `eval_slide_node` hardcoded `SourceSpan::default()`, causing validation diagnostics to render `file:'' line:0 col:0`. Now threads the real slide span (`spanned_slide.span()`) into `Slide.source_span` via the byte-offset bridge; miette resolves line:col from the byte offset at render time. --- ## Architecture Changes ```mermaid graph TD A["slideforge-validate

Future image-loading code would have been exposed to path traversal if this gap was not closed before disk I/O shipped. **What ships:** - `crates/slideforge-validate/src/image_path.rs` — new file, 713 lines - `ImagePathValidator` struct implementing `Validator` trait - `E_VAL_012 = "E-VAL-012"` public constant - Three detection classes, applied in priority order: 1. Windows drive letter prefix (`[A-Za-z]:`) 2. Absolute path (`/` or `\` prefix) 3. Traversal segment — path split on `/` and `\`, any component equal to exactly `".."`; a segment like `"..images"` is NOT a traversal segment - Errors accumulate (no short-circuit) — all violations in a deck are reported - Each violation carries the `ImageSpec`'s own `source_span` for diagnostic location - Registered in `slideforge/src/registry.rs` via `register_validator(Box::new(ImagePathValidator))` ### diag-span — Slide Source-Span Threading **Category:** Diagnostics / Developer Experience **Severity:** MED (validation diagnostics were misleading/useless without location) **What was wrong:** `eval_slide_node` called `SourceSpan::default()`, so all validation diagnostics that cited a slide location rendered as `file:'' line:0 col:0`. **What ships:** - `eval_slide_node` now calls `spanned_slide.span()` and routes through `span_to_source_span()` byte-offset bridge - `Slide.source_span` carries a real byte-offset derived from the parse span - miette resolves line:col from the byte offset at diagnostic render time - Full `SourceMap` line:col remains a separately-documented deferred story (tracked separately); this PR closes the `default()` regression --- ## Test Evidence | Suite | New Tests | Status | |-------|-----------|--------| | `slideforge-validate` `ImagePathValidator` — reject cases (traversal, absolute, drive-letter) | 7 | PASS | | `slideforge-validate` `ImagePathValidator` — accept cases (safe relative paths) | 2 | PASS | | `slideforge-validate` `ImagePathValidator` — message format + span equality + accumulation | 2 | PASS | | `slideforge-eval` diag-span — non-default byte-offset assertions | 4 | PASS | | **Target suite total** | **15 new** | **562/562** | **Workspace:** 3428/3429. body:
This pull request introduces a user-visible task history feature, including soft-deletion (hiding) of tasks, and a new sidebar UI for managing task threads. It adds backend support for soft-hiding tasks, new API endpoints for listing and hiding user tasks, and updates frontend components to use and display this data. The changes also include an improved event feed for replaying recent activity and several supporting schema and utility updates.

**Backend: Task soft-hiding and user task APIs**
- Added a new `hidden_at` field to the `Task` model and database schema to support soft-deletion (hiding) of tasks from a user's history. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5786fa7fcb70006475e15e5e601552b85e77c80cb39082624eae5c45b15930e1R1-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c2fccb8144f70b58a148cc0e82ab3093d5005781106a987dee81e0ef39f9131bR91-R93)
- Implemented repository functions for listing tasks (excluding hidden), hiding tasks for a user, and fetching task details, along with subtask utilities. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c46a984d720ab914887ce2e3841757cac8cc29c0f23d8ea919172572841316b6R346-R359) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c46a984d720ab914887ce2e3841757cac8cc29c0f23d8ea919172572841316b6R401-R449)
- Added API endpoints to list a user's tasks and to hide (soft-delete) a task, returning structured task and subtask details. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-36d307d286a0bbe1266bd3dffb13ef84014283e3e08f30c79283c8c45b5e85ffL13-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-36d307d286a0bbe1266bd3dffb13ef84014283e3e08f30c79283c8c45b5e85ffR258-L267)
- Mark tasks as complete when all subtasks are processed.

**Backend: Feed improvements**
- Added a new `read_recent` function to fetch the most recent feed events for replay in the UI.
- Updated the SSE `/feed` endpoint to use the new `read_recent` function for initial backlog.

**Frontend: Task history sidebar and thread management**
- Introduced a new `TaskHistorySidebar` component that lists all user tasks (including pending and live), allows selection, and supports hiding tasks from history. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e9ef8f98209663a18d21bae05d6c09e5e8a88d203958f43058b23ca4d2d22feaR1-R167) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4d60a06834d6ba7404a0de306134b3edd19bfd779691d58d45800c731845c309R7) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4d60a06834d6ba7404a0de306134b3edd19bfd779691d58d45800c731845c309R24-R30)
- Refactored `TaskThread` to use the merged task list, synchronize selection with the sidebar, and update UI/scrolling logic accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-080b2443e72b544879024eacad0ce6503e972f2e11deb519d17ce97f170ea84fL7-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-080b2443e72b544879024eacad0ce6503e972f2e11deb519d17ce97f170ea84fL19-R88) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-080b2443e72b544879024eacad0ce6503e972f2e11deb519d17ce97f170ea84fL56-R100)
- Updated `TaskComposer` to hydrate tasks after posting a new one, ensuring the sidebar and thread stay in sync. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e5d69de35a6c9b5a6b2dd3df220257b693f0fac3c3d79b38ae8739c3af2a1f12L15-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e5d69de35a6c9b5a6b2dd3df220257b693f0fac3c3d79b38ae8739c3af2a1f12R51)

**Schema and utility updates**
- Added new Pydantic models for `TaskDetail`, `SubtaskDetail`, and `TaskListResponse` to standardize API responses.

These changes collectively enable users to view, manage, and hide their task history, improving usability and persistence of their interactions with the agent network.

author: ratoker-jpg
body:
## This is NOT the final placement fix

This is a **calibration/debug aid only**. It allows Denis to see the projected ground cell, selection ring center, and hull anchor markers side-by-side, then adjust the hull offset live until the Wasp hull sprite is correctly centered.

## Problem

Manual QA shows the generated Wasp hull sprite is visually shifted upward / not centered inside the selection ring / tile. The direction is now correct (PR #241), but the position needs calibration.

### Fixup v2 — Input processing

Denis reported that pressing calibration keys (U/I/K/J/L/O/P) triggered upgrade abilities instead of calibration. Root cause: upgrade hotkeys were processed before placement calibration. Fix: Alt+U activation chord + placement key consumption before upgrades.

### Fixup v3 — On-screen buttons + ModularTankDebugOverlay-style markers

Denis reported that keyboard-only calibration is not enough for GitHub Pages preview. The overlay was also visually unclear. Fix: Added on-screen calibration button panel + ModularTankDebugOverlay visual language.

## Solution

Added a devtools/Arena-only placement calibration overlay that shows **ModularTankDebugOverlay-style markers**:
- **Green diamond** — tile footprint diamond (projected ground-plane)
- **Gold crosshair + circle** — logical tile anchor (where the game thinks the vehicle tile center is)
- **Cyan circle + X pattern** — hull sprite origin marker (where the hull PNG origin is placed)
- **White line** — connecting line from hull origin to turret origin
- **Red crosshair + circle** — turret sprite/mount origin marker
- **Compact debug text panel** — tile coords, world position, scale/origin, current offset, hull→turret delta

**On-screen button panel** (bottom-right, fixed on screen):
- Row 1: UP / DOWN / LEFT / RIGHT (1px step)
- Row 2: UP x5 / DOWN x5 / LEFT x5 / RIGHT x5 (5px step)
- Row 3: RESET / PRINT VALUES
- Buttons are large enough for mouse/touch (68–110px wide, 42px tall)
- Button clicks do NOT leak into gameplay (no unit movement, no camera pan, no upgrades)

## Controls (Arena/devtools only, Wasp selected)

### Keyboard

| Hotkey | Action |
|--------|--------|
| **Alt + U** | Toggle placement calibration mode on/off |
| I | Move hull up 1px (only while active) |
| K | Move hull down 1px (only while active) |
| J | Move hull left 1px (only while active) |
| L | Move hull right 1px (only while active) |
| Shift + I/K/J/L | Move hull 5px (only while active) |
| R or 0 | Reset offset to (0, 0) (only while active) |
| P | Print placement values to console (only while active) |
| O | Toggle overlay visibility (only while active) |

**Key design**: Alt+U uses an Alt chord to avoid conflict with the U upgrade hotkey (mobility_boost). When placement calibration is active, I/K/J/L/O/P/R keys are consumed with `preventDefault`+`stopPropagation` before upgrade hotkey processing, so upgrades do NOT trigger and camera does NOT move.

### On-screen buttons

Visible when placement calibration is active. Click any button to adjust offset — same as keyboard controls. Button clicks are suppressed from reaching gameplay input handlers.

## Console API

```js
window.WASP_PLACE.up()       // adjust up 1px
window.WASP_PLACE.down()     // adjust down 1px
window.WASP_PLACE.left()     // adjust left 1px
window.WASP_PLACE.right()    // adjust right 1px
window.WASP_PLACE.up5()      // adjust up 5px
window.WASP_PLACE.down5()    // adjust down 5px
window.WASP_PLACE.left5()    // adjust left 5px
window.WASP_PLACE.right5()   // adjust right 5px
window.WASP_PLACE.reset()    // reset offset to (0,0)
window.WASP_PLACE.print()    // print placement values
window.WASP_PLACE.overlay()  // toggle overlay
window.WASP_PLACE.state()    // print current state
window.WASP_PLACE.set(x, y)  // set offset directly
```

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/phaser/debug/WaspHullPlacementCalibrator.ts` | Placement calibration state module, updated docs for Alt+U + on-screen buttons |
| `src/phaser/debug/WaspPlacementCalibrationPanel.ts` | **NEW** On-screen button panel (10 buttons: UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT, UP x5/DOWN x5/LEFT x5/RIGHT x5, RESET, PRINT VALUES) |
| `src/phaser/render/BlockoutVehicleRenderer.ts` | Apply debug offset to hull sprite position; draw ModularTankDebugOverlay-style markers; manage on-screen button panel lifecycle |
| `src/phaser/input/BlockoutVehicleInputController.ts` | Alt+U toggle + I/K/J/L/O/P/R hotkeys; guard pointer events when placement calibration active (button click leak prevention) |
| `src/__tests__/waspHullPlacementCalibrator.test.ts` | 22 tests for placement calibrator including Alt+U + screen buttons reference |
| `src/__tests__/waspPlacementCalibrationPanel.test.ts` | **NEW** 16 tests for panel lifecycle and button action integration |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| typecheck | PASS |
| tests (4077 total) | PASS |
| build | PASS |
| qa:smoke (standard + devtools) | PASS |

## Confirmations

- [x] No PNG changes
- [x] No direction remap changes
- [x] No turret changes
- [x] No movement/pathfinding changes
- [x] No production/economy/save-load changes
- [x] No bot/AI changes
- [x] No other hulls affected
- [x] Debug offset affects visual sprite position only
- [x] Selection ring / movement / pathfinding unchanged
- [x] On-screen buttons call same placement functions as keyboard
- [x] Button clicks do not leak into gameplay
- [x] ModularTankDebugOverlay-style visual markers preserved

body:
## 前景放大（Foreground scale）— 让主体整体变大去盖住过渡带

按你的反馈重做：**不是把边缘外扩（外扩带会露出一圈羽化的填充色），而是把整个前景主体按比例整体放大**，支点取主体质心。放大后的剪影在相机移动时**物理地盖住身后那条去遮挡过渡带**，而不是露出补全色。

### 改动
- **着色器**：前景几何在 warp 之前绕 `fgCenter`（主体质心 uv）按 `fgScale` 放大；纹理仍按原 `uv0` 采样 → 人物是「被放大」而非平移。背景层 / 中间层 `fgScale=1`（恒等），所以只有主体变大。同时恢复**干净硬阈值 matte**（去掉 fgExtend 外扩带 → 边缘零光晕）。
- **MeshUniforms**：`fgExtend` → `fgScale`(偏移 36) + 新增 `fgCenter` float2(偏移 48)，stride 56。Swift / Metal 字节偏移已逐字段核对一致。
- **烘焙**：干净锐利主体 matte；羽化带仍用「最近主体像素」颜色，避免放大时把背景色拉出一圈边。计算主体质心(uv)挂在 `Photo3DScene.fgCenter`。
- **UI**：「前景外扩」滑块 → 「前景放大」(1.0–1.25)，默认 1.05。

### 怎么测
1. 选一张人像 → 进编辑器，拖动「3D 强度」和「背景视差」拉大幅度。
2. 拖「前景放大」：0% = 原尺寸；往上拖主体整体变大，身后露出的填充带逐步被盖住。
3. 对比 `main`（外扩带方案）：放大方案在边缘不再有一圈半透明填充色。

### 注意
- 默认 1.05（轻微）。如果觉得人物「浮」起来或头/脚出框，把滑块拉回 0% 即为原尺寸。
- 构建已通过（Debug / iOS Simulator）。**先不要合并，明天 review。**

author: adam-s
body:
closes #144

# Description

**What this adds:** A regression test for manually grading an instance question that has **no submission** — the path that broke in #8801 and currently has no coverage.

<!-- No before/after screenshots: this PR is test-only and changes no production code or any
     user-facing rendered surface. The regression-catch proof below is the evidence. -->

**Upstream issue:** [`PrairieLearn/PrairieLearn#8805`](https://github.com/PrairieLearn/PrairieLearn/issues/8805) ("Add test for manually grading without submission")

**Context (what is being covered):** When an instance question has no submission, `manualGrading.sql`'s `select_submission_for_score_update` (`LEFT JOIN submissions`) returns a row with `submission_id = NULL`. `manualGrading.updateInstanceQuestionScore` (`apps/prairielearn/src/lib/manualGrading.ts:532`) handles this: it skips the grading-job insert and the submission update (both gated on `current_submission.submission_id`, `manualGrading.ts:687-722`) but still updates the instance question's points/score (`manualGrading.ts:725-748`). The realistic way to reach this with no submission is the instructor **assessment-instance page**: the manual-grading page 404s without a submission, so points are edited via `edit_question_points`, which calls `updateInstanceQuestionScore({ submission_id: null, … })` (`apps/prairielearn/src/pages/instructorAssessmentInstance/instructorAssessmentInstance.ts:170-188`). This is exactly what the bug-fix comment in `components/EditQuestionPointsScore.tsx:75-77` describes.

**The change (test added):**

```ts
// New describe block in apps/prairielearn/src/tests/instructorAssessment.test.ts:
//   - pick an instance question with no submission (HAVING count(submissions) = 0)
//   - assert pre-state: 0 submissions, status 'unanswered', last_grader NULL
//   - POST edit_question_points { points: 4 } from the assessment-instance page
//   - assert: points=4, manual_points=4, score_perc ≈ 4/max*100, last_grader set,
//             requires_manual_grading=false, status still 'unanswered',
//             and STILL 0 submissions and 0 grading jobs
// Plus a new instructorAssessment.test.sql sidecar with the supporting queries.
```

**Why this is correct coverage:**
- It drives the **real route** (`edit_question_points`) end to end, hitting the exact null-`submission_id` branch the #8801 fix protects — not a mock.
- The seed needs no extra fixtures: `helperExam.startExam` already creates instance questions for all exam questions, and the test only submits to two of them, so an unanswered instance question is available for free.
- The assertions pin both the positive outcome (instance-question points recorded) and the invariants that distinguish the no-submission path (no submission created, no grading job created, status stays `unanswered`).

**Regression-catch proof (this is a coverage test, so there is no production change to make red-on-base; instead the test bites when the #8801 fix is reverted) — VERIFIED in a live container:**
- Reverted `apps/prairielearn/src/lib/manualGrading.types.ts` line 61 from `submission_id: IdSchema.nullable()` to `submission_id: IdSchema`.
- `select_submission_for_score_update` returns `submission_id = NULL` for the unanswered question → `SubmissionForScoreUpdateSchema.parse` throws → the new test failed with:
  - `should accept a manual points edit with no submission` → **`AssertionError: expected 500 to equal 200`** (the `edit_question_points` POST returned 500 instead of 200).
  - `should record the points on the instance question` → **`AssertionError: expected +0 to equal 4`** (the score was never recorded because the route threw).
  - All other 190 tests in the file still passed (they all have submissions), so the test bites the regression precisely and nowhere else.
- Restoring the line returned the file to **192/192 passing**. (The toggle is only for proof; it is not part of this PR.)

**Regression check (blast radius):**
- **Production code changed:** none. This PR adds one test file (`instructorAssessment.test.ts` additions) and one SQL sidecar (`instructorAssessment.test.sql`).
- **Unchanged behavior:** the existing sections of `instructorAssessment.test.ts` (running point/score totals in sections 8-16) are untouched; the new `describe` is appended last and only reuses its own `locals` fields. Setting total points/score_perc earlier in the file does not stamp `last_grader` on instance questions (it goes through `update_assessment_instance_score`, which writes only `assessment_instances`/`assessment_score_logs`), so the pre-state assertion is stable.
- **Determinism:** the unanswered question is selected by a deterministic `ORDER BY q.qid LIMIT 1` query; assertions key on values fixed by the POST input and the documented seed defaults (`auto_points`/`manual_points` start at 0; `status` defaults to `unanswered`).
- **No SQL/schema production change** (the only SQL added is a test sidecar of read-only queries) → query performance audit N/A. **No user-facing rendered surface changes** → before/after screenshots N/A.

# Testing

**Coverage added:** `apps/prairielearn/src/tests/instructorAssessment.test.ts` — new `describe('17. manually grade an instance question with no submission')` (+ `instructorAssessment.test.sql`).

**Verified in a live PrairieLearn container (`vitest run apps/prairielearn/src/tests/instructorAssessment.test.ts`):**
- **With the #8801 fix in place (master):** `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 192 passed (192)` — the whole file is green, including all 8 new no-submission assertions.
- **With the #8801 fix reverted:** `Tests 2 failed | 190 passed (192)` — only the two no-submission scoring assertions turn red (500, points=0); the rest stay green.
- **Fix restored:** back to `192 passed (192)`.

Run it: `yarn workspace @prairielearn/prairielearn test src/tests/instructorAssessment.test.ts` (or the repo's standard vitest invocation for a single test file).

**Neighbors:** the rest of `instructorAssessment.test.ts` still passes (all 184 pre-existing tests green alongside the 8 new ones); this file owns its `helperServer.before/after` and shares no global state with other suites.

**Manual verification:** as an instructor (student data editor), open an assessment instance that contains a question the student never answered, click the edit-points control on that question's row, set the points, and confirm the points/score are recorded while the question shows no submission.

- [x] I have disclosed the level of AI assistance used: **majority of implementation** — gap analysis, test design, and drafting done with Claude Code via the PrairieLearn debug harness; reviewed by adam-s.

body:
## Summary

Wraps the release flow's final manual step (`git tag v<version> && git push origin v<version>`) into one gated command, per the owner request to reduce toil — while preserving the hard rule that **release is a human decision and ship never publishes**.

`roll release ship`:
- **Gate** (pure `planShip` in core): on main · clean tree · synced with origin · tag doesn't already exist · `consistency check` green. Any failure aborts with the reason — nothing tagged.
- **Confirm** (skippable with `--yes`; `--dry-run` previews), then tags `v<version>` and pushes → triggers release.yml.
- **STOPS there**: never runs `npm publish`, never touches 2FA. The owner publishes separately. The autonomous loop never calls it.

Read-only `roll release` now ends by pointing at `ship` as its step-4 automation.

## Test plan
- [x] core planShip: 7 tests (tag = v<current>, each blocker, accumulation)
- [x] cli: 11 tests (tag+push happy path, **never-publishes**, dry-run, --yes, decline-aborts, every blocker, missing version)
- [x] live: `--help`, `--dry-run` correctly blocked on a feature branch + dirty tree, `roll release` guidance line
- [x] `roll test` green

This PR updates [beautifulsoup4](https://pypi.org/project/beautifulsoup4) from **4.7.1** to **4.15.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.11.1
   ```
   This release was done to ensure that the unit tests are packaged along
with the released source. There are no functionality changes in this
release, but there are a few other packaging changes:

* The Japanese and Korean translations of the documentation are included.
* The changelog is now packaged as CHANGELOG, and the license file is
  packaged as LICENSE. NEWS.txt and COPYING.txt are still present,
  but may be removed in the future.
* TODO.txt is no longer packaged, since a TODO is not relevant for released
  code.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.11.0
   ```
   * Ported unit tests to use pytest.

* Added special string classes, RubyParenthesisString and RubyTextString,
  to make it possible to treat ruby text specially in get_text() calls.
  [bug=1941980]

* It's now possible to customize the way output is indented by
  providing a value for the 'indent' argument to the Formatter
  constructor. The 'indent' argument works very similarly to the
  argument of the same name in the Python standard library's
  json.dump() function. [bug=1955497]

* If the charset-normalizer Python module
  (https://pypi.org/project/charset-normalizer/) is installed, Beautiful
  Soup will use it to detect the character sets of incoming documents.
  This is also the module used by newer versions of the Requests library.
  For the sake of backwards compatibility, chardet and cchardet both take
  precedence if installed. [bug=1955346]

* Added a workaround for an lxml bug
  (https://bugs.launchpad.net/lxml/+bug/1948551) that causes
  problems when parsing a Unicode string beginning with BYTE ORDER MARK.
  [bug=1947768]

* Issue a warning when an HTML parser is used to parse a document that
  looks like XML but not XHTML. [bug=1939121]

* Do a better job of keeping track of namespaces as an XML document is
  parsed, so that CSS selectors that use namespaces will do the right
  thing more often. [bug=1946243]

* Some time ago, the misleadingly named "text" argument to find-type
  methods was renamed to the more accurate "string." But this supposed
  "renaming" didn't make it into important places like the method
  signatures or the docstrings. That's corrected in this
  version. "text" still works, but will give a DeprecationWarning.
  [bug=1947038]

* Fixed a crash when pickling a BeautifulSoup object that has no
  tree builder. [bug=1934003]

* Fixed a crash when overriding multi_valued_attributes and using the
  html5lib parser. [bug=1948488]

* Standardized the wording of the MarkupResemblesLocatorWarning
  warnings to omit untrusted input and make the warnings less
  judgmental about what you ought to be doing. [bug=1955450]

* Removed support for the iconv_codec library, which doesn't seem
  to exist anymore and was never put up on PyPI. (The closest
  replacement on PyPI, iconv_codecs, is GPL-licensed, so we can't use
  it--it's also quite old.)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.10.0
   ```
   * This is the first release of Beautiful Soup to only support Python
  3. I dropped Python 2 support to maintain support for newer versions
  (58 and up) of setuptools. See:
  https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/2769 [bug=1942919]

* The behavior of methods like .get_text() and .strings now differs
  depending on the type of tag. The change is visible with HTML tags
  like <script>, <style>, and <template>. Starting in 4.9.0, methods
  like get_text() returned no results on such tags, because the
  contents of those tags are not considered 'text' within the document
  as a whole.

  But a user who calls script.get_text() is working from a different
  definition of 'text' than a user who calls div.get_text()--otherwise
  there would be no need to call script.get_text() at all. In 4.10.0,
  the contents of (e.g.) a <script> tag are considered 'text' during a
  get_text() call on the tag itself, but not considered 'text' during
  a get_text() call on the tag's parent.

  Because of this change, calling get_text() on each child of a tag
  may now return a different result than calling get_text() on the tag
  itself. That's because different tags now have different
  understandings of what counts as 'text'. [bug=1906226] [bug=1868861]

* NavigableString and its subclasses now implement the get_text()
  method, as well as the properties .strings and
  .stripped_strings. These methods will either return the string
  itself, or nothing, so the only reason to use this is when iterating
  over a list of mixed Tag and NavigableString objects. [bug=1904309]

* The 'html5' formatter now treats attributes whose values are the
  empty string as HTML boolean attributes. Previously (and in other
  formatters), an attribute value must be set as None to be treated as
  a boolean attribute. In a future release, I plan to also give this
  behavior to the 'html' formatter. Patch by Isaac Muse. [bug=1915424]

* The 'replace_with()' method now takes a variable number of arguments,
  and can be used to replace a single element with a sequence of elements.
  Patch by Bill Chandos. [rev=605]

* Corrected output when the namespace prefix associated with a
  namespaced attribute is the empty string, as opposed to
  None. [bug=1915583]

* Performance improvement when processing tags that speeds up overall
  tree construction by 2%. Patch by Morotti. [bug=1899358]

* Corrected the use of special string container classes in cases when a
  single tag may contain strings with different containers; such as
  the <template> tag, which may contain both TemplateString objects
  and Comment objects. [bug=1913406]

  found in the HTML5 spec in much the same way that the html5lib
  tree builder does. Note that the lxml HTML tree builder doesn't handle
  named entities this way. [bug=1924908]

* Added a second way to pass specify encodings to UnicodeDammit and
  EncodingDetector, based on the order of precedence defined in the
  HTML5 spec, starting at:
  https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-with-a-known-character-encoding

  Encodings in 'known_definite_encodings' are tried first, then
  byte-order-mark sniffing is run, then encodings in 'user_encodings'
  are tried. The old argument, 'override_encodings', is now a

  This changes the default behavior of the html.parser and lxml tree
  builders, in a way that may slightly improve encoding
  detection but will probably have no effect. [bug=1889014]

* Improve the warning issued when a directory name (as opposed to
  the name of a regular file) is passed as markup into the BeautifulSoup
  constructor. [bug=1913628]

author: hearn1
body:
## Problem

With the `#249` fix merged, the release pipeline gets one step further but now fails the readiness phase at the graceful-shutdown call:

```
[Smoke] Packaged overlay HTML loaded.
urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: FORBIDDEN   # POST /api/control/shutdown
```

The local-API CSRF guard added in #228/#229 (`_enforce_local_api_token` in `web/server.py`) requires the `X-Bazaar-Coach-Token` header on all state-changing methods when the app registers a per-process token — which the real packaged app does (`set_api_token` at startup). `smoke_test_portable.py` sends the shutdown POST with no token, so it 403s and the release aborts.

This blocks cutting `0.2.0-alpha.12` (the smoke test also runs in CI on the tag, so the fix must be on `main` before tagging).

## Fix

The overlay HTML carries the token as `window.BAZAAR_COACH_API_TOKEN` (injected before `</head>` by `_serve_html_with_token`). The smoke test now:

1. Reads the **full** `/overlay` body (previously only the first 2 KB, which missed the late `</head>` injection).
2. Extracts the token via regex.
3. Sends it as `X-Bazaar-Coach-Token` on the shutdown POST.
4. Tolerates token-disabled builds (no token found → POST without the header).

No product code changes.

## Testing

Ran the updated script against the packaged exe:

```
[Smoke] Packaged overlay HTML loaded.
[Smoke] Portable package smoke test passed.
```

body:
Part of #396 (Slice 4 — Messaging orphan recovery).

## Summary

Messaging retry recovery can now distinguish a live owner from a dead one when Coordination is available. Retry pickup stamps claimed rows with the current node identity, compares stored owners against live membership during the distributed-lock pass, and accelerates rows owned by dead nodes back to the retry floor instead of waiting for the original lease to expire.

The provider contract now carries owner-aware reclaim methods across the in-memory, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server stores. The shared storage conformance harness injects mutable membership and proves each provider stamps owners, reclaims dead-owner rows, preserves live/restarted incarnations, leaves terminal/null-owner rows untouched, and keeps reclaim idempotent. PostgreSQL and SQL Server also assert the Owner column width and filtered/partial owner-index shape.

When Coordination is not configured, messaging keeps the existing locked-until behavior and emits EventId 85 so operators can see that recovery is using the fallback floor-only mode.

## Verification

- `make test-project TEST_PROJECT=tests/Headless.Messaging.Core.Tests.Unit/Headless.Messaging.Core.Tests.Unit.csproj TEST_FILTER='--filter-class "*RetryProcessorDistributedLockTests" --filter-class "*BootstrapperTests" --filter-class "*SetupMessagingCoordinationTests" --filter-class "*MediumMessageTests"'` passed 36/36.
- `make test-project TEST_PROJECT=tests/Headless.Messaging.InMemoryStorage.Tests.Unit/Headless.Messaging.InMemoryStorage.Tests.Unit.csproj TEST_FILTER='--filter-class "*InMemoryDataStorageTests"'` passed 41/41.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- Log search: watch for EventId 85 / `MessagingRecoveryUsingLockedUntilFloorOnly`; expected only on deployments that intentionally run without a Coordination provider.
- Healthy signal: retry backlog drains without waiting for the full `LockedUntil` lease after a node/process crash when Coordination is enabled.
- Failure signal: sustained growth in failed/retry rows with non-null `Owner` and future `LockedUntil`, or repeated EventId 85 on a deployment expected to use Coordination.
- Database validation: confirm `Owner` columns and owner indexes exist on `published`/`received` (`idx_*_Owner_not_null` for PostgreSQL, `IX_*_Owner_NotNull` for SQL Server).
- Window/owner: observe the first deployment window plus one retry-lease interval; owning team is the messaging/coordination rollout owner.
- Mitigation: disable Coordination wiring to fall back to `LockedUntil`-floor-only recovery, or roll back the messaging storage package if owner stamping/reclaim causes unexpected retry behavior.

author: katomm
body:
Hardens the DRep metadata hosting endpoint surfaced by the security audit. Previously POST /api/drep/metadata accepted a drep id and profile from any unauthenticated request, letting anyone overwrite another DRep's hosted document or fill storage with junk (no deposit needed).

- Hosting now requires proof of control of the DRep key: the client signs a fresh challenge with the DRep key (CIP-8, the same signature the login flow uses) and the server requires the drep id derived from that verified key to equal the submitted one. The derived id is used for storage and the returned URL, so a client claim is never trusted.
- Reuses the existing verifier, nonce, and identity derivation; the handler is extracted (handleDrepMetadata) and tested with a real preprod DRep fixture.
- Proof-of-control alone cannot bound storage (an attacker can generate unlimited keys), so the DRep sync now garbage-collects hosted metadata older than a 14 day grace period whose drep id is neither currently registered nor referenced by a current on-chain anchor hash. Real DReps are never affected.
- The GC is skipped when an enumeration returns zero DReps, so a transient empty drep_list can never wipe every hosted document.
- The registration UI signs the challenge with the DRep key before hosting; rate limiting on the endpoint is unchanged.
- 591 tests pass.

author: tcoratger
body:
## Summary

PR 10 from the `packages/testing/` audit — fork choice authoring ergonomics, in two parts. Net **−245 lines**.

### 1. Dedup the selective-validation models

`StoreChecks` drove its scalar, label-root, and pool target-slot checks through three parallel `if "field" in fields:` ladders (~75 lines); `AttestationCheck` repeated a fourth as a field-name `if`-chain; `StateExpectation` already had the clean accessor-table pattern. A shared **`SelectiveCheck`** base now iterates only the fields a test set against a subclass accessor table, and each repetitive group collapses to one table-driven loop:

- `_SCALAR_ACCESSORS` (9 fields), `_LABEL_ROOT_ACCESSORS` (4), `_POOL_TARGET_SLOT_ACCESSORS` (3) on `StoreChecks`
- a module-level slot-accessor table for `AttestationCheck`
- `StateExpectation` and `StoreChecks` both inherit the base

Genuinely bespoke checks (lexicographic head, reorg depth, block-body structure, `filled_block_root_label`) stay explicit — they aren't one-line lookups. `store_checks.py` drops 632 → 584; the duplication is gone without flattening the complex checks. No behavior change (error-message field labels now read as the field name, e.g. `head_slot` rather than `head.slot` — surfaced only on failure, never in vectors).

### 2. Fluent `ForkChoiceScenario` builder

A linear chain with attestations read as ~120 lines of nested `BlockStep(block=BlockSpec(...), checks=StoreChecks(...))`. The builder expresses the same step list through chained calls:

```python
ForkChoiceScenario()
  .block(1, label="block_1").expect(head_slot=Slot(1))
  .tick_to_unix_time(10)
  .attest(by=[1, 2], slot=2, target_label="block_2", target_slot=2)
  .block(3, label="block_3").expect(head_slot=Slot(3), block_attestation_count=1)
  .steps()
```

- `.expect(**fields)` attaches a `StoreChecks` to the preceding step — real field names, no alias layer that could drift.
- Two tick methods (`.tick(interval)` / `.tick_to_unix_time(time)`) name the targets separately, hiding `TickStep`'s mutual-exclusivity foot-gun.
- `.chain(slots)` appends a labeled block per slot.
- The builder emits **exactly** the frozen steps the explicit form does (verified by JSON-equality against the original before rewriting). The explicit `steps=[...]` form stays fully supported; the builder is opt-in.

`test_produce_block_includes_pending_attestations` is rewritten through it as the worked example. The other three block-production tests keep the explicit form, where heavy per-step overrides read more clearly.

### 3. Drop wrapper noise

`validator_indices=[ValidatorIndex(0), ValidatorIndex(1), ...]` → `[0, 1, 2]` across the fork choice tests. The spec types already coerce plain ints to `ValidatorIndex` at construction (verified identical), so the wrappers were pure ceremony. Scoped to validator-index lists in `fc/`; `Slot(...)` is left as domain-meaningful.

## Test plan

- `just check` passes (lint, format, ty, codespell, mdformat, lock)
- Builder/explicit step equality proven via JSON comparison
- Single-test fill smoke on the builder-converted test passes

author: ryoctrl
body:
## Problem

"並列ダウンロード数" looked like it did nothing — everything downloaded serially.

The politeness throttle (#28) gated **file downloads** as well as metadata, spacing every request *start* `MIN_GAP_MS` (300 ms) apart per service. So even with N download workers, downloads started ~1 every 300 ms → effectively serial for typical file sizes, regardless of the concurrency setting.

## Fix

File downloads are already bounded by the user's **concurrency** setting (the engine's worker pool), which *is* the load limit — a min-gap on top is redundant and defeats the setting. Drop `awaitPoliteSlot` from `downloadToFile`. Metadata enumeration (`requestFor`: creator/post listing, post detail) keeps the throttle, since bursty listing is what it was meant to tame.

Now N files download genuinely in parallel (browsers do ~6/host anyway).

## Scope note

Concurrency applies to a post's files; posts are still processed one at a time, so a post with M images runs `min(M, concurrency)` in parallel. For these image-heavy sites that's clearly parallel now. True cross-post parallelism (N files in flight spanning posts) would be a larger engine refactor — happy to do it as a follow-up if wanted.

## Docs

`docs/spec/security-and-legal.md` updated to describe the split: concurrency-bounded downloads vs. min-gap-throttled metadata.

## Test

`typecheck` / `lint` / `build` green; `npm test` green (89). The `throttle` unit tests are unchanged (they cover `awaitPoliteSlot`, still used by metadata).

## What this does — #987 slice (b): the decider runs AS A COACH
The autonomous decider (`LlmCoach`, the `claude -p` per-decision call the `feed_daemon`

workers it would answer substantive questions with no architectural grounding. Now it loads

The OMPT tests currently use an incrementing ID for the host_op_id. However, this value is not incremented for `submit_emi` callbacks, and uses a global integer that is incremented on callback invocation. This can lead to race conditions when e.g., `target nowait` is used.

author: anishkanase-scaler
body:
## Submission

- Roll Number: **10075**
- Name: **Nase Anishka**
- Lab: **Lab 6 — B-Tree Index (C++17)**

## What's inside `10075-Nase-Anishka/Lab6/`

- `main.cpp` — templated `BTreeIndex<Key, Value>` (key → value, the value standing in for a row pointer). Supports insert (with in-place update on a repeated key), search, in-order traversal, an indented + a BFS structure printer, and a `validate()` that checks every B-tree invariant and throws if one is broken.
- `CMakeLists.txt` — C++17 with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`
- `run_output.txt` — captured stdout from a real run
- `.gitignore`
- `README.md`

## Design notes

- **Minimum degree `t`**: each node holds `t-1..2t-1` keys and up to `2t` children.
- **Proactive top-down split**: a full child is split *before* descending, so insert is a single root-to-leaf pass; the median is promoted and the tree only grows taller by splitting the root — which is what keeps all leaves at the same depth.
- **Parallel `keys[]` / `vals[]`** per node (instead of a vector of structs), mirroring how a page separates the sort key from the payload.
- **`validate()`** carries a `(low, high)` window down the recursion and asserts key counts, strict sortedness, separator ordering, child-count `= keys+1`, and equal leaf depth.

## Demonstrated (see `run_output.txt`)

- `t=3` build with the two splits printed live (medians 40 then 60 promoted) → 12 keys in a height-1 tree.
- Traced searches showing the path walked and node-access count (hit and miss both cost `height+1`).
- Ascending `1..20` into a `t=2` (2-3-4) tree stays at height 3 — vs a height-19 stick for a plain BST — with every leaf on the same level.
- Upsert: re-inserting an existing key updates the value and leaves `size` unchanged.

## Build & run

```bash
cd 10075-Nase-Anishka/Lab6
cmake -B build -S .
cmake --build build
./build/btree_index
```

author: kadyapam
body:
## Summary

Fixes a template-resolution gap surfaced by [noetl/ai-meta#65](https://github.com/noetl/ai-meta/issues/65) kind-val: single-tool python steps producing a flat user dict were reachable via `{{ step.field }}` (flat-field path) but NOT via `{{ step.data }}` / `{{ step.data.field }}` (the wrapped path that canonical v10 fixtures use interchangeably).

## Root cause

`WorkflowState::build_context` (in `src/engine/state.rs`) inserts the extracted user_data directly at `<step_name>` in the template context — without a self-referencing `.data` key.

The task_sequence flatten path (`flatten_task_sequence_data`) coincidentally populates `.data` from a labeled sub-task's `data` field, so multi-step playbooks tend to work. But single-tool steps (e.g. `tool: python` with a `result = {...}` return) skip task_sequence wrapping entirely — so `<step>.data` resolves to None.

Surfaced concretely in kind execution `322087210360770560` from #65 kind-val: the `verify` step's assertion `assert run_from_file_data == expected_data` failed because `{{ run_from_file.data }}` rendered as `None` even though `run_from_file` had completed successfully with `data = {status: 'success', messages: [...], total_greetings: 3, script_source: 'file'}`.

## Fix

In `build_context`, after inserting the extracted user_data at `<step_name>`, also inject a `data` key on the user_data dict that re-references the same data — so both `{{ step.field }}` (existing) and `{{ step.data.field }}` (new) resolve to the same value.

Don't clobber an existing `.data` field — the task_sequence flatten path may have already populated it from a labeled sub-task. Preserved by the `!map.contains_key("data")` guard.

```rust
let with_data = match &user_data {
    serde_json::Value::Object(map) if !map.contains_key("data") => {
        let mut m = map.clone();
        m.insert("data".to_string(), user_data.clone());
        serde_json::Value::Object(m)
    }
    _ => user_data,
};
context.insert(name.clone(), with_data);
```

## Tests

Added two unit tests:

- `test_build_context_exposes_step_data_accessor_for_flat_user_dict` — reproduces the live #65 envelope (kind execution 322087210360770560); asserts BOTH flat (`step.status`, `step.total_greetings`) AND `.data`-prefixed (`step.data.status`, `step.data.total_greetings`, `step.data.messages`) paths resolve.
- `test_build_context_data_accessor_does_not_clobber_existing_data_field` — pins task_sequence flatten back-compat: a labeled-sub-task `data` field stays addressable as `<step>.<label>.data.x` AND as `<step>.data.x`, with the #66 fix not overwriting the flattened path.

Results:
- `cargo test --lib engine::state` → 19/0/0 (was 17, +2 new).
- `cargo test --lib` → 566/0/0.
- `cargo build --release --bin noetl-control-plane` → clean.

## Test plan

- [x] Local: `cargo test --lib`, `cargo build --release --bin noetl-control-plane` — all green.
- [ ] Kind validation (after merge + image build): re-run `tests/k65/python_file_loader` from #65 kind-val and verify the `verify` step's `{{ run_from_file.data }}` reference now resolves to the producer's dict.

Closes noetl/ai-meta#66

author: binjospookie
body:
## What

For a `Task` target, `debug` built its `output` spot as:

```ts
shape(
  { status: optional(target.status), result: optional(target.result), error: optional(target.error) },
  (x) => x,
)
```

This drops the trailing `(x) => x`, using the single-arg `shape(ctx)` overload instead.

## Why

The identity `fn` is dead weight:

- **Runtime** — every field is wrapped in `optional()`, so each leaf resolves to a value or `undefined`, never `Missing$`. The assembled object is therefore never `Missing$`, and `safe(identity)` just returns it unchanged. The output is byte-identical with or without the `fn`; the only effect was one extra `safe()`-wrapped identity step pushed onto the spot's compute pipeline per debug run.
- **Types** — the single-arg overload `shape<T>(ctx): Spot<T>` infers the same `Spot<{ status, result, error }>`. The identity adds no type information.

The trailing `(x) => x` predates the single-arg `shape` overload — leftover plumbing from when a `fn` was required.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter ./packages/app-coda test` — 142 passed, no type errors (debug snapshot tests confirm output is unchanged)
- `pnpm --filter ./packages/app-coda build` — clean, declarations emit unchanged

## Linter fixes (eslint-plugin)

Hardened `task-options-order` and `wire-options-order` while on this branch. Both rules matched call sites with a `:has(ObjectExpression.arguments)` filter and assumed the argument was always an object literal — which was unsound. Defects fixed:

- **Crash on wrapped arguments** — `createTask(factory({...}))` (and `createWire(buildWire({...}))`) made the rule operate on a non-object node; `task` threw calling `.some()` on it. Both rules now bail unless the argument is an object literal (`config.type !== ObjectExpression`).
- **Autofix dropped code** — the task autofix rebuilt the config from a fixed schema and silently dropped shorthand `run`/`enabled`, dropped unknown top-level keys, and emitted invalid syntax for getters. It now relocates the real property nodes, so shorthand, spreads, and unknown props survive verbatim.
- **Non-converging autofix** — when a nested key would have to move across a spread, the rule now reports without attaching a fix instead of applying one that can't converge.

Verification: `pnpm --filter ./packages/eslint-plugin test` — 38 passed; build (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsdown`), `knip`, and `oxlint` clean.

author: alibassam
body:
Closes #626.

## Summary

`cpuset_cpus` / `cpuset_mems` on `container.create()`, `container.run()` and `pod.create()` only accepted `List[int]`, so users couldn't pass the range/mixed cpuset strings the Docker CLI actually supports (`"0-3"`, `"0,2"`, `"0-3,7"`). This PR widens the accepted types and adds a small `format_cpuset` helper that passes strings through unchanged and joins integer iterables.

`container.update()` was already typed `Optional[str]` on master but its docstring still claimed it required a list — that's corrected too.

## Design note

Issue #626 suggested making this **string-only** (a backwards-incompatible change). I went with `Union[List[int], str, None]` instead to keep existing list-based callers working. Happy to drop `List[int]` and make it string-only with a deprecation if you'd prefer — let me know and I'll push a follow-up commit.

## Changes

- New `format_cpuset()` util in `python_on_whales/utils.py`
- `container.create()`, `container.run()`: widened `cpuset_cpus` / `cpuset_mems` to `Union[List[int], str, None]`, switched call-sites to `format_cpuset`
- `pod.create()`: widened `cpuset_cpus` to `Union[Iterable[int], str, None]`
- `container.update()`: docstring corrected (signature was already `Optional[str]`)
- Unit tests for `format_cpuset` covering None / list / empty / string / generator

## Summary

`toSentenceCase` and `capitalizeOnlyFirstLetter` both reimplemented the `str.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + str.slice(1)…` pattern. This extracts a shared private `upperFirst` helper and:

Note: the two functions intentionally keep their differing semantics (`toSentenceCase` preserves tail casing and only touches a leading ASCII word char; `capitalizeOnlyFirstLetter` lowercases the tail). No behavior change.

## What

Adds the `services/ontology-service` Go module and establishes Cubicle's graph contract using Meta/TAO-style vocabulary:

- `Object`, `ObjectRef`, and open `ObjectType` values for typed ontology entities.
- `Association`, `AssociationType`, and evidence-bearing association metadata for graph relationships.

This PR is the base of the ontology-service stack, so it needs to define the vocabulary every later PR uses. The service should expose and organize graph code around objects and associations from the start, including the later Ent codegen and query layers.

The base domain package now models the graph as objects and associations with explicit bounded expansion parameters like `LimitPerObject` and `AssociationTypes`. The ontology registry owns Cubicle's first product terms, while keeping the DTOs generic enough for Jira, GitHub, docs, Slack, and future connectors.

author: kaufd
body:
## Problem

Closes [DRA-176](https://linear.app/draftszone/issue/DRA-176). After saving/changing the Arena ID in profile settings, the value in the nav user menu (`UserMenu`) did not update until a full page reload.

## Root cause

- `UserMenu` reads `user.profileMetadata.arenaId` from `useAuth()` → `AuthProvider`, which fetches `/api/auth/session` **once on mount** and holds `user` in client state with no way to re-fetch (by design the only refresh was a full reload, cf. `GoogleOneTap onSuccess={() => window.location.reload()}`).
- `ArenaIdForm` updated only its own local state on success.
- The `updateArenaId` server action's `revalidatePath(profile)` invalidates the profile page server render — not the client `AuthProvider` state that feeds the menu.

## Fix (Option A)

- `AuthProvider`: expose `refreshUser()` that re-fetches `/api/auth/session` and updates the in-memory user (best-effort; keeps the last-known user on failure). Stable `useCallback`, merged into a memoized context value.
- `ArenaIdForm`: call `refreshUser()` (fire-and-forget) after a successful save so the nav menu reflects the new Arena ID without a reload.

Same `refreshUser()` is reusable by other profile edits that should reflect in the menu.

## Tests

- New `arena-id-form.test.tsx`: `refreshUser` is called on a successful save and **not** called on a failed save.
- `bun run typecheck` clean · `bun run lint` 0 errors · full web suite **1781 passed** / 18 skipped (152 files).

## Notes

Pre-existing bug, unrelated to the Phase-27 double-OTP flip (found during post-flip prod verification of 0.3.1). No DB/security implications.

author: divybot
body:
On Windows, a trailing space (or dot) in a file path argument such as `deno info ".\foo.tsx "` was percent-encoded into the module specifier (`foo.tsx%20`). The low-level Windows filesystem APIs still open the file (Win32 trims trailing spaces and dots when opening files), but the trailing `%20` caused the media type to be misdetected — e.g. `TypeScript` instead of `TSX` — producing a confusing parse error on otherwise valid JSX/TSX files:

```
deno info ".\tsx.tsx "
error: The module's source code could not be parsed: Expected ';', got '!' at file:///C:/.../tsx.tsx%20:4:21
```

On Linux/macOS the same command fails cleanly with `module could not be found` (a trailing space is a significant, distinct file name), so the behavior was inconsistent across platforms.

## Fix

Normalize file path arguments the same way the Windows filesystem does, by stripping trailing spaces and dots from the final path component before building the specifier (`cli/util/path.rs::strip_windows_trailing_chars`, wired through a small `resolve_url_or_path_normalized` wrapper). URL arguments (anything with a URI scheme) are passed through unchanged. This is a no-op on non-Windows platforms, where trailing whitespace in a file name is significant.

After the fix, `deno info ".\tsx.tsx "` reports `type: TSX` and resolves dependencies normally.

## Scope

The wrapper is wired into the commands that resolve a single argv path string directly through `resolve_url_or_path` — `run`/`serve`/`compile`/`info` plus `--preload`/`--require`. That is where the exact `%20` media-type symptom reproduces.

Other subcommands (`check`, `doc`, `test`, `bundle`, `cache`) resolve files through the file collector / glob expansion rather than `resolve_url_or_path`, so they don't hit the same code path. A fully uniform fix would live one layer deeper (in `deno_path_util`'s path→URL conversion), but that is an external crate; keeping the normalization in the CLI wrapper covers the reported case without reaching across repos. This can be broadened later if the same symptom is reported for the collector-based commands.

Two sibling direct call sites are intentionally left unnormalized, as neither is the reported symptom: `cli/tools/run/mod.rs` (the eszip `entrypoint#paths` run path, a special case) and `cli/tools/compile.rs`'s `resolve_compile_executable_output_path` (only infers the output binary name; the actual compile module still resolves through the normalized `args/mod.rs` path).

## Test

Added `tests/specs/info/jsx_trailing_space_windows` (gated with `"if": "windows"`, since the normalization is a no-op elsewhere), a `#[cfg(windows)]` unit test for `strip_windows_trailing_chars`, and a cross-platform unit test asserting URL arguments bypass normalization (locking in the scheme guard).

Closes #30585

Closes denoland/divybot#537

author: pat-lewczuk
body:
Fixes #2691

## Problem
Session and password-reset tokens are stored HMAC-SHA-256 hashed at rest, but three `AuthService` lookup paths fell back to querying with the RAW token when the hashed lookup missed. This made the on-disk `sessions.token` / `password_resets.token` column value itself a usable credential, defeating the point of hashing tokens at rest.

## Root Cause
`deleteSessionByToken`, `refreshFromSessionToken`, and `confirmPasswordReset` each retried with `{ token }` (the plaintext value) after the `{ token: hashedToken }` lookup returned nothing. The fallback existed purely as a transitional bridge for legacy plaintext rows, but no backfill/migration ever removed those rows, so the bridge remained a live attack surface: anyone who can read the token column (DB backup leak, replica snapshot, accidental log/dump, SQL injection in another module) could present the stored value directly to refresh a session or confirm a password reset.

## What Changed
- `packages/core/src/modules/auth/services/authService.ts`
  - `deleteSessionByToken` — deletes only by the hashed token; removed the raw-token retry.
  - `refreshFromSessionToken` — looks up the session only by the hashed token; removed the raw-token retry.
  - `confirmPasswordReset` — looks up the reset row only by the hashed token; removed the raw-token retry.

Tokens are still written hashed (`createSession`, `requestPasswordReset`); only the insecure read/delete fallbacks are removed. Public method signatures and return types are unchanged.

## Tests
- Updated/added regression tests in `authService.test.ts`:
  - `deleteSessionByToken` never issues a raw-token delete when the hashed lookup misses
  - `refreshFromSessionToken` looks up by the hashed token only and rejects a raw (legacy plaintext) session token
  - `confirmPasswordReset` looks up by the hashed token only and rejects a raw (legacy plaintext) reset token
- Verified red-before-fix: the five new assertions fail against the pre-fix code and pass after.
- `yarn workspace @open-mercato/core test src/modules/auth` → 337 passed
- `yarn build:packages`, `yarn generate`, `yarn typecheck` → all green

## Backward Compatibility
- No contract surface changes: method signatures, return types, API routes, event IDs, DI names, and ACL features are untouched.
- Behavioral note: any remaining legacy rows holding a plaintext token can no longer be resolved. Hashed tokens (issued since hashing was introduced) are unaffected; legacy sessions/resets simply require re-login / re-request, which is the intended security posture.

author: currenttide
body:
## R82 — mac-app Transfers shows "expires 0s from now" for every staged blob

**Surface:** mac-app/correctness. User-test minor (`user-testing/mac-app/mainwindow-transfers.png`).

### Root cause
`Format.timeAgo` (in RoostMac, not Linux-testable) is past-tense only: it clamps the
interval to `max(0, now - epoch)`, so any **future** timestamp collapses to `0s`. The
Transfers call site then string-swapped `" ago"` → `" from now"`, yielding
`"expires 0s from now"` for every staged blob with hours of TTL still remaining.

### Fix
- **New `RoostKit.RelativeTime`** — a pure, *signed* formatter (`signed`/`ago`) taking an
  injectable `now`, so the Linux harness pins both past (`"Xh ago"`) and future (`"in Xh"`)
  deterministically. Mirrors the R81 pattern: decision logic in RoostKit, the SwiftUI view a
  dumb renderer. No string-swap anywhere — real signed delta arithmetic.
- **TransfersView** migrated to `RelativeTime.signed(blob.expiresAt)` — the fragile
  ago→from-now swap is gone.
- **`Format.timeAgo` single-sourced** through `RelativeTime.ago` (epoch clamped to `now` so
  the past-only sites — last-seen, finished-at, updated-at — keep past-tense phrasing). The
  duplicated bucket logic is deleted. Only sub-second behavior changes: "0s ago" → "now"
  (intentional, consistent in both directions, documented in code).

### Other future-time call sites — audited
Schedule next-run already uses a separate, **already-correct** `ScheduleInterval.relative(to:now:)`
(renders `"in …"`/`"… ago"`). It is not a `Format.timeAgo` consumer and is not buggy, so it is
deliberately left as-is. A grep of `mac-app/Sources` confirms every remaining `Format.timeAgo`
call is on a semantically-past field; Transfers was the only future-time `timeAgo` site.

### Evidence (gate fully re-run)
- **A1 (failing test first):** the 14 new `RelativeTimeTests` were run against the reproduced
  pre-fix clamp logic → **15 failures**, future cases rendered `"0s from now"`. After the fix → green.
- **Linux RoostKit `swift test`** (`/tmp/swift-toolchain` 6.0.3): **82 passed** (68 base + 14 new).
- **`python -m pytest -q`: 853 passed** — server untouched (diff is `mac-app/` only).
- **Mac node** (mac-mini-m4, via `roost exec`): `swift build` → **Build complete, exit 0** (full
  RoostMac target incl. the migrated views compiles, arm64e-apple-macos14.0); `swift test` →
  **82 passed, exit 0**. (Per the item, a render screenshot is optional for a pure formatter fix —
  the unit tests + full-app build are the gate. R73 lesson satisfied: the app target compiles on macOS.)

### Judge
Independent judge on `claude-sonnet-4-6` (implementer: `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` — models differ).
Re-ran the gate itself (82 swift / 853 pytest / scope-checked mac-app-only). One round →
**approve**. Sole finding (a doc-comment overstatement re "byte-for-byte unchanged") addressed in
a comment-only follow-up; tests re-run green.

body:
## Resumen

`v2.9.1` — corrige un defecto de auditoría sistémico (pre-existente) que se hizo visible al desplegar `v2.9.0` (overhaul Session/Auth W1–W6) contra Postgres real, más la deuda de fixtures que `v2.9.0` introdujo.

## Bug raíz

`audit_entries_category_check` (migración 021) fijó el set de categorías permitidas, pero el vocabulario derivó de los call-sites de `IAuditService.RecordAsync`. El código emite `conversations`, `queues`, `reports`, `operational` y `license` — ninguna estaba en el constraint — así que **toda escritura de auditoría con esas categorías fallaba con `23514` en Postgres** (silenciosamente: el `try/catch` defensivo alrededor de cada `RecordAsync` deja pasar la operación pero pierde la fila de audit).

Los workers nuevos de `v2.9.0` (`AgentLivenessReaper` force-offline W3, `PendingPauseDrainWorker` W4, `WorkFailoverWorker` W5, `CallbackRescueWorker` W5b, supervisor reassign) ampliaron los emisores de `queues`/`conversations` y lo destaparon en un deploy real.

**Invisible en las 1311 Api.Tests** porque usan storage InMemory, que no tiene CHECK constraints.

## Cambios

- **Migración 034** — amplía `audit_entries_category_check` a la unión real de categorías (aditiva y segura: toda fila existente ya es válida).
- **Test TDD** (`CheckConstraint_ShouldAcceptDomainCategory_WhenWritten`) — bloquea las 16 categorías como aceptadas; los tests de rechazo de basura siguen vigentes. Fixture espeja la migración 034.
- **`AuditEntry.Category`** — doc actualizada con el vocabulario completo + nota de mantener-en-sync.

author: zyanklee
body:
## Kontext / Warum

Einige Features funktionieren nicht zuverlässig, weil die OS-Integrationen (systemd-logind über D-Bus, PAM-Curfew, `notify-send`) bisher **vollständig gemockt** wurden — die Tests blieben grün, während das reale Verhalten brach („grüne Tests, kaputte Realität"). Außerdem lief **keine CI** für Tests/Linter, und in einer frischen Umgebung waren nicht einmal die vorhandenen Tests lauffähig.

Dieser PR fügt eine **geschichtete Testpyramide** hinzu, die die kritischen Integrationen **real** und **headless** prüft — lauffähig im Claude Cloud Dev Environment und in CI. Nur das, was zwingend einen echten Desktop braucht, bleibt einer dokumentierten, extern auszuführenden E2E-Schicht vorbehalten.

## Was ist drin

| Layer | Marker | Inhalt | Wo |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** static | – | ruff / black / isort | überall + CI |
| **L1** unit | – | reine Logik (pro Paket); neue Tests für `guardian_agent`/`guardianctl`/`guardian_hub` | überall + CI |
| **L2** D-Bus-Contract | `dbus` | echter `dbus-daemon` + Mock-logind/Notifications in **dbus-next** → echter `SessionTracker.run()`, `Enforcer.notify_user`, Agent-Notify-Roundtrip | Cloud + CI |
| **L3** PAM-Curfew | `pam` | echtes `pam_time.so` via `pamtester`+`faketime`, Allow/Deny an Curfew-Grenzen | Cloud + CI (root) |
| **L3b** systemd-Units | `systemd_units` | Golden-Text generierter Units | *dokumentiert, noch nicht implementiert* |
| **L4** Desktop-E2E | `e2e` | echtes Login/SDDM/Termination je Distro | *dokumentiert, nur externe VM* |

**Warum dbus-next statt python-dbusmock:** Guardian abonniert logind-Signale über `manager.on_session_new(...)`, das dbus-next aus der **Introspection** baut. python-dbusmock fügt Methoden/Properties, aber **keine Signale** zur Introspection hinzu → `on_session_new` würde fehlen. Das dbus-next-Mock liefert korrekte Signal-Introspection, läuft in einem Interpreter (uv-venv) und braucht keine nativen Build-Deps. Das Mock-Session-Objekt exponiert bewusst die echten logind-Shapes (`User`-`(uid, path)`-Struct, `Desktop`-Property) — genau dort, wo die alten MagicMocks von der Realität abwichen.

## Verifikation (alles grün)

- **L1:** Daemon **262** · guardianctl **3** · guardian_agent **6** · guardian_hub **6 (+1 xfail)**
- **L2:** **9** · **L3:** **11** · **L0:** ruff/black/isort sauber
- → **297 Tests grün**, headless lauffähig

## Provisioning & CI

- `scripts/setup_testenv.sh` — idempotentes System-Dep-Setup (dbus, libnotify-bin, pamtester, libpam-modules, faketime) + `uv sync` + Capability-Smoke-Checks. Verdrahtet über einen **SessionStart-Hook** (`.claude/settings.json`), damit Web-Sessions sofort testfähig sind.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `lint` + `unit` (Matrix über 4 Pakete) + `dbus` + `pam` bei push/PR.
- `TESTING.md` — dokumentiert die Layer und die noch offenen L3b/L4.

## Nebenbei gefundene & behobene Zuverlässigkeits-Bugs

1. **`storage.py`:** Alembic-`script_location` war relativ zum Prozess-CWD → DB-Migrationen schlugen fehl, sobald der Daemon nicht aus `guardian_daemon/` gestartet wurde. Jetzt relativ zum Daemon-Verzeichnis aufgelöst.
2. **Packaging:** `guardian_agent`/`guardianctl`/`guardian_hub` hatten kein `[build-system]` (nicht als Paket installierbar) + verirrte äußere `__init__.py`, die das innere Paket überdeckten und `python -m guardianctl` brachen. Alle vier Pakete installieren jetzt sauber.

## Dokumentierter (noch offener) Befund

`tests/pam/test_curfew_enforcement.py::test_overnight_curfew_behaviour` pinnt einen latenten Bug: Über-Nacht-Fenster wie `22:00–06:00` werden als `Wk2200-0600` (start>end) erzeugt, was `pam_time` nicht als Mitternachts-Übergang interpretiert. Fix ist Folgearbeit.

## Hinweise

- Der Lint-Gate erforderte eine einmalige Formatierung einiger Bestandsdateien (alembic, `scripts/install_artifacts.py`, hub-Stubs) — **rein formatierend**, keine Logikänderung.
- **L4** (echte Desktop-E2E pro Distro: Nobara/Bazzite/CachyOS) kann prinzipbedingt nicht in Claude Cloud laufen und ist daher nur konzeptionell in `TESTING.md` beschrieben (inkl. Distro-Risiken wie Bazzite-Immutabilität und fehlendem authselect auf Arch).

## What

`/qa:plan` now ends with an **approval gate** that makes QA approval come *before* building, not after.

**Companion to** [mujtaba3B/dev#45](https://github.com/mujtaba3B/dev/pull/45) (claude-hooks), which adds three gates (build / PR / deploy) keyed to a per-branch approval stamp. This PR is the **writer** of that stamp.

## How

New **Step 6** in `qa/skills/qa-plan/SKILL.md`:
1. Present the Development + Production QA sections via `AskUserQuestion` (Approve / Revise / Skip).
2. On **Approve**, run `~/.claude/scripts/qa-plan-stamp.sh write` to record `<git-dir>/qa-plan-approved` for the branch (with an optional `--digest` of the plan text).
3. Only stamp on an explicit yes; revise loops back; detached HEAD / base-branch checkout refuses to stamp by design.

author: peterp
body:
## Problem

The CLI entry file had grown into a huge catch-all file. It mixed command dispatch, help text, asset downloads, session wiring, and many command implementations in one place. That made it hard to review changes and easy for dead-code or health problems to hide.

## Solution

This PR turns `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` into a small dispatcher. Command code now lives in focused modules under `packages/cli/src/commands/`, with shared helpers split into small files like `args.ts`, `base-assets.ts`, `errors.ts`, `session.ts`, and `help.ts`.

## Technical Summary

- Keeps `cli.ts` to dispatch and top-level error handling only. It is now 145 lines.
- Splits large command areas into domain modules for boot, restore, snapshot, fork, Node Level 5, registry, support, move, stop, exec, attach, and misc commands.
- Further splits the largest command modules so no changed CLI file is near the 1,000-line health guard limit.
- Moves shared target parsing, PTY handling, base asset setup, session handling, and CLI errors into reusable helpers.
- Updates convention tests so they check behavior in the new module locations instead of assuming everything lives in `cli.ts`.

author: jegs1984
body:
Port the Django/PostgreSQL money manager to a self-contained Android
application with a local SQLite database. No server or network required.

Stack:
- Jetpack Compose (Material3) for all UI
- Room 2.6 with six entities mirroring the Django models
- Hilt 2.51 for dependency injection
- Kotlin Flows + ViewModel for reactive state
- Apache POI 3.17 for XLS parsing (no LibreOffice on device)

Data layer:
- PeriodEntity, CategoryEntity, BudgetItemEntity, TransactionEntity,
  StagingTransactionEntity, StagingCCTransactionEntity
- BudgetItemDao includes a JOIN query that replicates the Django
  annotate(total_real, diff) used in DashboardView
- FinanceRepository.getDashboardStats() mirrors calculate_safe_to_spend()
- AppDatabase.SeedCallback inserts all 64 canonical categories from
  sql/categories.sql on first launch

Parsers:
- DatParser: pure Kotlin reimplementation of parse_scotiabank_statement()
  handles DDMMYYYY dates, cargos/abonos, BOM, CRLF, zero-padded CLP amounts
- XlsParser: reads Scotiabank CC estado de cuenta (.xls HSSF) via Apache POI,
  extracts card holder/number/statement date from header block,
  parses installment cuota fields and CLP period-thousands amounts

Screens (each with ViewModel):
- Dashboard: safe-to-spend, burn rate, income/expense summary cards,
  per-item capacity bars (green <80%, amber 80-100%, red >100%)
- Periods, Categories, BudgetItems, Transactions: full CRUD
- ImportDatScreen → StagingReviewScreen: file picker via SAF, category
  assignment per row, batch commit to ledger
- ImportCCScreen → StagingCCReviewScreen: same flow for CC statements,
  shows installment detail inline

APK packaging instructions in android/README.md

## Chista — Phase 2 (Kasm-parity P1) + Phase-3 differentiators

Follow-up to #6 (Phase 1, merged). Delivers **6 Phase-2 P1 epics + 2 Phase-3 differentiators**, all live on `chista.naiemi.com` and verified end-to-end via `qm guest exec` (curl / docker inspect). Full monorepo test suite stays green (**334/334**).

### Phase-2 P1 epics
- **C2** Bulk-CSV user import — `POST /users/import`: CSV parser (quoted fields), per-row `create()` (skip existing, per-row errors with line numbers), group assignment by name.
- **E4** File-mapping propagation — `dispatchProvision` binds org `CONTAINER` FileMappings (`sourcePath→destPath`, token-interpolated; home-profile rw else ro) into the session via `runConfig.volumes` (reuses the E1 agent binds).
- **E3** User-scoped storage — file-mapping propagation now honours `userId` (`{null}` ∪ session user); another user's mappings don't leak in.
- **G1** Config import/export — `GET/POST /config` (`SETTINGS_MANAGE`): versioned JSON of volume/file mappings + groups (+ roles inventory); idempotent import (skip existing by name); roles deliberately **not** imported (no privilege-grant via upload).
- **D4** Agent lifecycle / drain — new `Agent.drainRequested` persists across heartbeats (heartbeat keeps `DRAINING` while drained); `PATCH /agents/:id/drain {drain:false}` un-drains. Scheduler already places only on `ONLINE` agents. *(Fixes a latent bug: drain never stuck because the heartbeat hard-set `ONLINE`.)*
- **D5** Autoscale plan evaluator — `GET /pools/:id/autoscale/plan` computes desired capacity now (SCHEDULE slot by dayOfWeek+hour UTC, else base config) vs current pool members → `scale_up`/`down`/`none` + delta. Actual VM provisioning stays a pluggable step.

### Phase-3 differentiators (beyond Kasm)
- **FinOps / cost dashboard** — `GET /reporting/costs`: runtime cost by user + workspace over a lookback window (`cores·coreHourCost + GB·gbHourCost` per session-hour, running sessions accrue to now); rates overridable per request.
- **Public API + SDK contract** — a scoped Developer-API OpenAPI document (`/api/dev-docs(-json)`, **3 paths** vs the internal 155) so SDK codegen targets the stable, API-key public surface, not the control plane.
- **Policy-as-Code** — `POST /policy/evaluate`: a declarative org-policy document evaluated against live state → `{compliant, violations[]}` (rules: maxSystemAdmins, group idle-timeout required, workspace DLP required). Read-only GitOps gate.
- **KI-Copilot backend** — `POST /copilot/ask`: natural-language questions answered deterministically over live state (sessions / cost / agents / users), no hallucination; free-form LLM reasoning is a pluggable step (`CHISTA_COPILOT_*`).

### Schema (additive `prisma db push`)
`Agent.drainRequested`. (E1/E3/E4/G1/D5/FinOps/SDK: no schema change.)

### Hardening
Earlier in this branch: security unit tests (impersonate / ApiKeyGuard / Ed25519 license / RBAC roles+groups) + a vitest workspace-resolution fix that unblocked the whole suite → 334/334.

### Verification honesty
For the infra-bound surfaces the **platform layer** is verified; the live edge (real cloud creds, RDP/VNC host, VM-provider scaling) stays pluggable and is called out in `docs/ROADMAP-KASM-PARITY.md`.

author: andymai
body:
## What

PR5 — the **finale** of the brepjs-voxel performance & scale stack. Adds a persistent voxel field at the wasm boundary so operations chain in **one grid** (voxelize once → boolean/offset/shell → contour once), made geometrically correct by **Fast Sweeping reinitialization**.

This is what makes "union two solids, then offset the result by 2 mm, in one pass" both expressible *and* correct.

## Pieces

- **`reinit_sdf` (Fast Sweeping, Zhao 2005)** — restores the true-SDF property `|∇φ|=1` while **preserving the zero level set**. It freezes the near-surface band at its original banded distance (so every Surface-Nets crossing fraction is byte-stable → the contour doesn't move), then runs 8 Godunov upwind Eikonal sweeps that propagate true distance outward with the sign preserved. Fixed 8-sweep pass — no tolerance loop.
- **`VoxelField` wasm handle** (`#[wasm_bindgen]`, **additive** — the 8 existing exports stay byte-identical): constructor + `boolean`/`offset`/`shell`/`reinit`/`contour`, all mutating in place. `offset`/`shell` **auto-reinitialize when dirty**, so an iso-shift always rides a true SDF — that's what makes offset/shell-after-boolean correct without the caller remembering.
- **TS `VoxelFieldHandle`** — wraps the wasm field via `createKernelHandle` + a `.free()→.delete()` `Deletable` adapter + `Symbol.dispose`, so `using field = voxelField(...)` cleans up. `FinalizationRegistry` is unreliable, so disposal is **explicit and leak-tested**. Fluent + functional op-chain API with L3 shape conveniences.

## Why it's correct (the gates)

- **FSM preserves the surface**: contour before == after reinit (identical counts, < 0.5·spacing drift on cube + sphere).
- **`|∇φ|=1` restored** + **idempotent** (second reinit is a no-op, |Δφ| < 1e-4).
- **Value proof**: `offset-after-boolean` is correct **with** reinit and demonstrably **wrong without** (two overlapping spheres unioned then offset by d: with reinit the join moves ~d; without, it under-moves). Both branches in one test.
- **No leak**: live handles return to baseline after `using` scope exit and explicit dispose; double-dispose is a safe no-op; disposed-handle ops return `VOXEL_FIELD_DISPOSED`.

## Review fixes (one reviewer requested changes — all addressed)

- **P1 (silent wrong result)**: two fields sized to their own bboxes have different origins, and the combine path checked only dims — so a field-to-field boolean silently blended mismatched coordinate frames. Fixed both ways: `require_same_grid` now checks **origin + spacing** (`GeometryMismatch` → loud `JsError`, which actually caught two pre-existing tests exercising the broken path), and a co-registering `VoxelField::boolean_of` voxelizes both meshes onto one union-bbox grid (sharing `voxel_boolean`'s logic) → exposed as `voxelBooleanField` / `voxelBooleanFieldShapes`.
- **P2**: added runtime coverage for `fieldShell`/`fieldReinit`/`voxelFieldFromShape`/intersection+difference ops; Rust handle-wiring tests; fixed the misleading `fieldBoolean` docstring.
- **P3**: `reinit_sdf` no-surface safety; `Symbol.dispose` on the `WasmVoxelField` interface.

## Notes

- Persistent fields are **dense-only** in v1 (boolean is dense-only; sparse op-chains are future).
- 78 cargo tests, 212 voxel/lattice vitest, public-api surface guard. wasm 88 → 119.5 KB (within the 200 KB budget).
