author: grindlemire
body:
## Summary

When a row ends in a wide (CJK/emoji) character, every differential update destroys that character on screen. Scrolling the markdown example with Chinese text drops the last character of each heading and paragraph, and it stays missing until something forces a full redraw. Initial render and resize are unaffected since they go through the full-redraw paths.

`Diff()` scans each row right to left for the rightmost content cell, skipping continuation cells. A trailing wide char stops the scan at its primary cell, which leaves the continuation column in the tail region, and the tail's single `EraseToEOL` starts on the glyph's second half:

```
row:  [测][ ][试][ ][标][ ][题][ ]
       0   1   2   3   4   5   6   7

lastContent = 6, tailStart = 7  =>  ESC[K at column 7
```

Terminals blank a multi-column glyph when any of its columns is erased, so the flush writes `题` and then immediately clips it. Worse, after `Swap()` the front buffer thinks the continuation cell is fine, so no later diff repaints the glyph. It stays broken until a full redraw.

The fix is when the rightmost primary has `Width == 2`, extend `lastContent` past the continuation cell so the tail erase starts after the glyph. The continuation cell can now be emitted as a regular `CellChange` when it changed, which is already a handled case. `ANSITerminal.Flush` skips continuation cells and receives them today for interior wide chars.

`TestBuffer_Diff_TrailingWideChar` covers the scroll case from the issue plus a few neighbors found while poking at this: a tail that clears while the wide char itself is unchanged (the erase used to wipe a glyph that never got rewritten), a freshly written trailing wide char (the back continuation never matches the front space, so a bogus erase went out on the first incremental paint of the row), a continuation cell sitting on the last buffer column, and an ASCII control case. All five fail without the fix, at the positions the trace predicts.

I also checked the two sibling scans that use the same idiom, `RenderFull` and `bufferRowToANSI`. Both only trim trailing output, and writing the primary rune covers both columns, so neither needs the extension.

Fixes #79

author: williamzujkowski
body:
## What
Closes #3177. Wires the previously hardcoded no-op policy gate handler
(`plan-compiler.createGateHandler`) to the canonical `evaluatePipelinePolicy`
evaluator, so policy gates actually enforce at the pipeline stage boundary.

## Approach (ratified by 7/7 higher_order vote)
- New `GatePolicyEnforcement` bundle on `PlanCompileOptions` (engine + pipelineState
  snapshot + optional eventBus + mode). Threaded through `PipelineRunner.compile`.
- `enforceGatePolicy` calls the existing `evaluatePipelinePolicy`; gate nodes report
  `passed`/`warned` or throw on block.
- Did NOT unify the three policy APIs (that's #3194, out of scope).

## Conditions met
1. **WARN by default, block opt-in.** Gate-enforcement mode resolves via new
   `getGateEnforcementMode()` which defaults to `warn` (NOT the V2 umbrella's `block`).
   Block is opt-in via `NEXUS_POLICY_GATE_MODE=block` or an explicit `mode`. Test (f)
   proves a stage with no trust metadata does not throw under the default.
2. **Typed error.** New exported `PolicyBlockedError` carries `gateId` + `violations`;
   thrown only when mode resolves to `block` AND verdict `!allowed`.
3. **Overrides continueOnFailure.** Executor flags the failed node `policyBlocked`
   (terminal `permission` category, non-retryable); `PipelineRunner.toResult` halts
   even in continue-mode. Test (g) pins this.
4. **Escalate→HITL: verified.** The graph executor's `Interrupt` mechanism is a
   pause-for-input primitive with no approval→re-evaluation return path, so wiring
   `escalate→interrupt` would be a dead branch. Per the vote, `escalate` is treated as
   `block` (fail-closed). Follow-up filed: #3697.

## Tests (TDD, red→green; 100 pass in the touched suites)
plan-compiler.test.ts: (a) throw-to-halt executor contract, (b) block+untrusted →
PolicyBlockedError + halt + carries gate id/violations, (c) block+trusted → passes,
(d) warn → continues + event emitted, (e) off → evaluator not called, (f) default mode
+ missing trust → no throw. pipeline-runner.test.ts: (g) block overrides continueOnFailure,
plus back-compat (no enforcement → no-op pass).

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint --no-cache` 0 errors.

author: chrisdco
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the circuit-centric UI redesign and the #27 interactive value-editing feature. The headline fix: **value edits never actually reached SPICE** — overrides were keyed by array index while the backend matches the SPICE device name, so every R/V edit was silently dropped. This makes the feature work end-to-end and tidies up the surrounding UI.

## What changed

**Value editing (the bug).** Overrides were sent as array indices (`"106"`) but `spice.py` matches the SPICE name (`R107`). The component name the UI already holds *is* the SPICE name, so the `name→index` conversion is removed and values pass straight through. Verified: editing `R2` `1k→10k` on an HDC divider moves node N2 `2.5V → 4.55V`, and battery (`V`) edits scale the map proportionally. At the DC operating point only R and V move voltages (caps open / inductors short), so C/L rows are tagged **no DC** so a no-op edit isn't mistaken for a bug.

**UI polish on the layers redesign.**
- Parameter controls unified into one consistent control (label + typeable numeric box + slim slider) rather than a squeezed, drag-only slider.
- Sidebar reduced to two roomy tabs — **Params** and **Values** (a focused R/C/L/V editor; non-editable components collapsed under a disclosure).
- **Join check** is back as its own view (View bar → Analysis), reusing the existing image overlay + per-net stepper + metrics. The unified Source/Threshold/Detected/Voltage views and the netlist stay on the single best strategy (`graph_rescue`); the Join view sandboxes any strategy independently.
- View bar moved from styled-jsx to global CSS — fixes the unstyled flash on every refresh (styled-jsx injects after hydration).
- Image grid is a modal that closes via X / Esc / click-outside, and its scroll-to-load now pages past the first 60 thumbnails on large datasets (HDC).

**OCR ("Read values").** The label loader searched a hardcoded path, so it found 0 labels on any other machine and the button silently did nothing. It now derives the labels dir from the image's own path (`.../images → .../labels`). The button also surfaces the real reason as a toast instead of failing silently. (Reading values still needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on the backend.)

Relates to #11 (analysis-panel integration + simulation context; mobile UX in that issue is still open).

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; backend route imports clean.
- End-to-end in the UI (HDC): R/V edits recolor the voltage map, the Join view renders overlay + metrics, the OCR toast reports the failure reason, and the view bar is styled on first paint.

As @ManyTheFish diagnosed, the `words` ranking rule is force-inserted before `typo`/`attribute`/`proximity`/`exactness` so its term-dropping still runs, but the newer `attributeRank` and `wordPosition` rules were missing from that guard in `get_ranking_rules_for_query_graph_search`. Placing either before `words` in the settings skipped word-dropping and silently returned fewer hits.

Fix: add `AttributeRank` and `WordPosition` to that match arm.

Added a regression test in `words_tms.rs` asserting that reordering the ranking rules changes only hit order, not hit count. It passes with the fix and fails without it (22 vs 12 hits on the existing test corpus).

## Summary

Follow-up to #50. Phase 1 hid the crew checklist whenever the user attached only a screenshot (no text) and showed a *"Crew picked once Jugaadu reads the image"* placeholder. The original concern was a bait-and-switch — letting users tick Resume Darzi for a screenshot that vision might decide was a *person*, where Resume can't run. ## Summary

- Adds bill payment APIs so users can record manual payments (installments) against issued bills, with automatic bill status updates (`issued` → `partially_paid` → `paid`).
- Introduces the `BillPayment` model with payment method, reference number, notes, and required proof-of-payment image upload via Spatie Media Library.
- Adds a `partially_paid` bill status and recomputes status (and `paid_at`) whenever payments are created or deleted.

## API endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/transactions/{transaction}/bill/payments` | Record a payment |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/transactions/{transaction}/bill/payments` | List payments for a bill |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/transactions/{transaction}/bill/payments/{payment}` | Remove a payment |

**Payment methods:** `bank_transfer`, `cash`, `gcash`

**Validation highlights:**
- Payment amount cannot exceed the bill's remaining balance
- Proof image is required (JPEG, PNG, WebP; max 10 MB)
- Payments are only allowed when the bill is `issued` or `partially_paid`

## Database / dependencies

- New `bill_payments` table
- Migration to add `partially_paid` to the bills status enum
- Spatie Media Library (`media` table migration + `composer` dependency)

## Test plan

- [ ] Run migrations: `php artisan migrate`
- [ ] Run feature tests: `php artisan test --filter=BillPayment`
- [ ] Record a partial payment on an issued bill → bill status becomes `partially_paid`
- [ ] Record a second payment covering the remainder → bill status becomes `paid` and `paid_at` is set
- [ ] Attempt payment exceeding balance → 422 validation error
- [ ] Attempt payment without proof image → 422 validation error
- [ ] Attempt payment on draft/cancelled bill → 422
- [ ] Delete a payment → bill status reverts correctly (`paid` → `partially_paid` or `issued`)
- [ ] Verify another user's transaction returns 404
- [ ] Verify unauthenticated requests return 401

## Summary

`--compile` currently crashes the Ideogram-4 trainer **late and confusingly**. `Ideogram4NetworkTrainer` doesn't override `compile_transformer`, so the base default (`trainer_base.py:1127` → `raise NotImplementedError`) fires only *after* `accelerator.prepare` (`:1763`) when `args.compile` is set — i.e. deep in setup, after the 8B model is already loaded and prepared.

This rejects `--compile` in `handle_model_specific_args` (the first setup phase, before any model load), matching the existing `--use_mask_loss` / `--gradient_checkpointing` / `--blocks_to_swap` fail-fast pattern. The user gets a clear, actionable message instead of `NotImplementedError`.

A real `compile_transformer` over `[transformer.layers]` (disabling Linear compile when `blocks_to_swap > 0`, per the Qwen pattern) can be added later alongside gradient checkpointing + block swap for native-1024 training — that's specced separately.

author: edwardricardo
body:
## What
The CI "Test Suite" job (`apps/api test:unit:coverage`) intermittently fails with `Worker exited unexpectedly` **while all 503 files / 7945 tests pass** — an OS-level SIGKILL (no V8 heap message) of a fork worker. With `pool:forks` + `maxWorkers:2`, two forks each load the full monorepo module graph and accumulate raw v8 coverage; their combined RSS intermittently trips the runner's OOM killer.

## Fix (Option G)
- `apps/api/vitest.config.ts`: `maxWorkers: 2 → 1` — removes one full base process, bounding peak RSS to one fork + the orchestrator (the primary fix).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144` (secondary heap-ceiling backstop) + Test Suite `timeout-minutes: 15 → 20` (absorb the ~2x serial slowdown).
- Coverage thresholds (55/55/45/55) unchanged.

## Verification
Root cause + fix derived from SDD (explore→propose→spec→design→tasks). Internet canon (vitest pool/coverage memory; OS-OOM vs V8-heap distinction). The local full-coverage repro is RAM-bound on the 9GB dev box (editor's tsserver alone uses 3.2G), so **CI is the runner-specific proof for a runner-specific OOM** — by design, per the explore ("CI green is the only 100% proof").

## Unblocks
PR #68 (CB-fallback PR1), whose only red was this same flake. Re-run its Test Suite after this merges.

author: zgrether
body:
**Bug:** an owner who had dismissed the setup guide saw the generic **"Set dates / Your trip, day by day"** empty-state CTA even though the trip was in **poll mode** — no way to manage windows or watch votes. The crew/member view correctly showed the live poll.

**Cause:** `ItineraryPanel`'s **owner** path never checked `poll_mode`. With the guide dismissed it fell through to `DismissedEmptyState`. `FreshTripGuide` *does* have a poll-takeover (renders `DatePollCard` with owner controls), but **dismissing the guide bypasses it**. Because `useGuideDismissed` is **per-device** (localStorage), the same owner saw the poll in one browser (guide not dismissed) and the dead CTA in another (dismissed) — which is exactly what happened here.

**Fix:** add an owner poll-takeover branch — `pollActive && !datesSet` → `FreshTripGuide` (its `DatePollCard` surface) — placed **before** the dismissal/empty-state branches, so a live poll always owns the home tab regardless of guide dismissal. Mirrors the member short-circuit.

`tsc` + `next lint` clean. (No data change — pure routing; verify by viewing a poll-mode trip as owner.)

author: jspinak
body:
## Make the runner drive `hoverClick` end-to-end

Implements `plans/2026-06-07-hoverclick-unify-sdk-action-dispatch.md` (vet-corrected). The SDK side of `hoverClick` was already complete (`@qontinui/ui-bridge` 0.17.0: `actionExecutor` + `inferActions`); the runner couldn't exercise it because (a) its pin was still `^0.15.0` and (b) a runner **frontend** per-element gate rejected the action. There was **no SDK dispatch gap** — the runner already routes `execute_action` straight to `actionExecutor.executeAction`.

### Changes
- **Pin bump** `@qontinui/ui-bridge` `^0.15.0 → ^0.17.0` + a runner **Rust** gate (`is_action_advertised` treats `hoverClick` as a click-variant) — the previously-pushed groundwork (`ece73357`), rebased in.
- **Frontend gate** (`useControlEvents.ts` `execute_action` pre-check): a hover-gated toolbar button (the `ZoneHoverActions` "Send to window" button) advertises an explicit `actions` list with `click` but not `hoverClick`, so the pre-check rejected it *before dispatch* (surfaced as `ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`). Now uses `isElementActionAllowed`, which exempts `hoverClick` wherever `click` is advertised — mirroring the Rust exemption so the two gates can't disagree.
- **`utils.ts`** `isElementActionAllowed(allowedActions, action)` + **5 regression tests** in `utils.test.ts`.

### Verification
**E2E on a temp runner** (built on SDK 0.17.0 + this branch): `POST /ui-bridge/control/element/button-send-terminal-to-a-window/action {"action":"hoverClick"}` → `success: true`, the **Send-to-window dropdown opens** ("New window" + windows), with **no `page/evaluate` workaround**. `tsc` + `eslint` clean; 18 `utils` tests pass (5 new); cargo build clean.

## 개요

세션 281 리포트 🟡 N+1 4곳을 childcare bulk prefetch 패턴(`env_childcare.py:45-50`) 답습으로 통일.
새벽 배치라 사용자 체감 0, 목적은 **Supabase pooler timeout 위험 감소**(루프 내 단일 SELECT 라운드트립 제거).
**17에이전트 적대검증 + 직접 교차검증**으로 v1(배치커밋) 정정.

## 변경

| 파일 | 변경 |
|---|---|
| `env_air.py` | `collect_air_quality`: 루프 내 `db.get(Infra)` → `infra_map` prefetch |
| `env_emergency.py` | `collect_emergency_data`: 동일 |
| `env_crime.py` | `collect_crime_stats` + `load_crime_stats` 2곳: 동일 |
| `test_env_collect.py` | 회귀 테스트 3건 추가 (`test_Infra_없으면_skip_자동생성_안함`) |

**동작 불변**: childcare 와 달리 air/emergency/crime 은 Infra 부재 시 skip(자동생성 안 함) 유지.
prefetch 전환 후에도 `infra_map.get(None)` → skip → silent failure 가드 failed 동작을 테스트로 가드.

## 적대검증으로 정정한 v1

- **배치커밋 폐기**: 리포트의 "40000+ 아파트"는 할루시네이션 — 실측 Apartment=Infra=**2001건**(prod).
  청크·배치커밋 불필요. 더 중요하게, `SessionLocal` 은 `expire_on_commit=True`(기본)라
  루프 중간 `db.commit()` 이 미처리 prefetch 객체를 expire → 다음 setattr 시 **재조회 SELECT 발생**
  (실측 확인) = N+1 self-defeating. childcare(답습 원천)도 배치커밋 없이 단일 commit → 제거.

## 범위 밖 (별도 판단)

- `service_price.py` batch throttle `on_rate_limit` 누락(리포트 🟡 5번째): NaverEstateAPI 내부
  429 재시도가 이미 backoff 하고, error dict 무차별 `on_rate_limit` 은 과도 감속 위험 → 본 PR 제외.
- 인덱스 추가 금지(combined_aggregate_index_void / freshness-do-not-optimize 답습).

body:
**Fixes the live 500 on pick-a-sample.** Found by checking the deployed app at rcca.hector-garza.com — infra was healthy (`/healthz` ok, pages render), but picking a sample 500'd.

## Root cause (from the Render traceback)
The kill landed **inside `client.messages.create` while receiving the response**, at `gunicorn/workers/base.py handle_abort → sys.exit(1)`. It's a **gunicorn worker timeout**, not an API error: the synchronous agent run (Phase 1 tool-use loop + Phase 2 structured emit, opus-4-8) takes longer than gunicorn's **default 30s** worker timeout, so the worker is aborted mid-request.

(Confirmed offline that the installed SDK `anthropic 0.107.1` accepts `output_config`/`thinking`/`tools`, so it was never a param/SDK-version issue.)

## Fix
Prod gunicorn now runs `--workers 1 --threads 8 --timeout 120`:
- **`--timeout 120`** — headroom for the agent run.
- **`--threads 8`** — the agent call is mostly I/O wait on the Anthropic API (GIL released), so threads keep the app responsive during a run, on a single memory-light worker (Render free tier).

Also wires the **live-demo link** into the README.

## Verify
- `gunicorn --check-config` loads the WSGI app with the new flags. ✓
- After this merges and Render auto-redeploys, I'll re-run the live flow (pick a sample → cited 8D → approve → export) and confirm the agent completes end-to-end.

body:
Plan 170 (host-lifecycle convergence + density) — the plan/ADR docs **and** Workstream A code, in one PR. Folds in #679 (docs-only), which can now be closed in favor of this.

> **Numbering:** the docs originally landed as Plan 169 in #679, but 169 was claimed by the agent-RPC transport plan that merged to `main` first (`check-spec-numbers` hard-fails on duplicate prefixes). Renumbered the host-lifecycle plan to **170**; ADR-074 is unique and unchanged.

## Docs (cherry-picked from #679, renumbered)

- `specs/plans/170-host-lifecycle-convergence-and-density.md` — WS-A marked done, `--repair` moved to a deferred-followups subsection.
- `specs/adrs/074-registry-source-of-truth-convergence.md` — registry is source of truth; converge at CLI entry, not a resident daemon; fail-open.
- One-line pointer in `specs/plans/140` distinguishing the trigger (170) from the snapshot-correctness gaps (140).

## Code — Workstream A (ADR-074)

- **`mvm::vm::reconcile`** — pure-logic-first convergence, mirroring `reaper::sweep`:
  - `classify()` tags each `VmRegistration` as `Live` / `DeadProcessLeftState` / `RecordNoState`, plus `OrphanStateNoRecord` for unrecorded state dirs. Intentionally-paused records are skipped.
  - `sweep()` applies idempotent actions via injected `RuntimeView`/`ReconcileActions` (no real backend/clock/fs). **Running twice is a no-op** (asserted).
  - `FsRuntimeView`/`FsReconcileActions` are the real adapter; liveness is `kill(pid,0)` on recorded supervisor pid files only — **cheap by construction** (no `pgrep`/`ps` spawn, no VM boot, no Nix), reusing the live-vs-orphan discrimination from the `env::apple_container` reaper.
  - `converge_at()` is the path-injectable load/save seam; `converge()` wraps the default registry, **fails open** (never returns `Err`), and emits a `RegistryReconcile` audit line per healed item (ADR-044), so `audit verify` still chains.
- **`mvmctl reconcile [--dry-run] [--json]`** — explicit, observable pass (sibling to `cache prune`).
- **Reconcile-on-entry wiring** — `Commands::touches_vm_state()` gates a cheap `converge()` before dispatch for `up`/`down`/`run`/`console`/`dev`/`pause`/`resume`/`snapshot`/`ls`; read-only/VM-agnostic verbs skip it; `reconcile` never double-runs. Opt out with `MVM_SKIP_RECONCILE=1`.
- **`mvmctl doctor`** — one-line `registry drift: N reconciled / clean` summary.

## Deferred (tracked in the plan's deferred-followups)

- `mvmctl reconcile --repair` builder-store self-heal (the degraded `…-source/flake.nix` loop) — heavier than the PID-liveness budget; its own slice.
- WS-B (idle reaper), WS-C (memory-pressure reaper), WS-D (wake-on-request completion).

## Tests / gates

TDD throughout. 31 reconcile unit tests (classify / sweep / idempotency / fail-open / Fs adapter / converge_at / converge end-to-end incl. audit), `reconcile_cli.rs`, `touches_vm_state` gate tests, doctor drift-summary test, audit-kind serde roundtrip, audit-posture coverage table.

Green locally: `check-spec-numbers`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (nightly), `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, lib tests + doctests for `mvm`/`mvm-core`/`mvm-cli`, `reconcile_cli`, `audit_total_coverage`, and `audit_emissions_live` (exercises the entry hook on real `up`/`pause`). `mvm-backend` excluded locally (macOS codesign SIGKILL — environmental).

### Motivation
- Reduce client-side lag caused by many custom particles by culling and throttling spawn rates and by making smoke updates cheaper. 
- Improve model rendering throughput by uploading per-group geometry to GPU VBOs while keeping the existing Tessellator path as a compatibility fallback.

### Description
- Added centralized particle spawn gating `canSpawnParticle(...)` that respects camera distance, `gameSettings.particleSetting`, and enforces a per-tick particle budget; integrated this into `spawnParticle(...)` and `spawnParticleExplode(...)` in `MCH_ParticlesUtil.java`.

author: khaliqgant
body:
## Problem

Slack `<integration-event>` notifications were emitting bare-channel-id paths with `Message: unavailable; targeted context read did not return content` — even on a current build that already includes the #154 suffixed-candidate fix.

**Root cause:** `readEventContextPreview()` was **SDK-read-only** (`client.readFile`). The bare→suffixed candidate translation (#154) was correct, but the Relayfile SDK read still missed the suffixed candidate under remote-consistency lag *while the bytes were already present on local disk*. #154 fixed candidate generation, **not the read source**. The symptom fires even on the bot's own outbound messages echoing back, and fully blocks any worktree with no mount.

## Fix

- **Local-disk fallback** in `readEventContextPreview()`, tried after SDK `readFile` candidates and before `event.expand('full')`. Scoped to **matched concrete mount roots only** (`concreteLocalMountRootsForIntegration` + `pathIsInsideMount`) — no broad `.integrations` scan, and it preserves the DM **"watched-but-not-mounted"** state (no concrete mount → no fallback).
- **Canonical path emission**: resolve the suffixed context path (from preview or matched mount alias) and use it for visible `Path:`, `data.path`, **and** `data.resource.path` — closes the structured-metadata-stays-bare gap so unmounted/downstream consumers also get the usable path.

## Tests

- New regression for the exact live failure shape: bare Slack event path + suffixed matched local mount + SDK read miss → local read succeeds; asserts preview content + suffixed visible & structured paths.
- `integration-event-bridge.test.ts`: **63/63 pass**.

## Review

Code-approved by the investigation team (diagnosed + verified against agreed constraints: concrete-mount-scoped fallback, suffixed path into all three fields, DM safety preserved).

## Not in scope (tracked separately)

- DM mount model (DMs need a Cloud/Relayfile DM resource model — `listenDms` is watch-only today)
- Live rebuild+restart verification — **deferred per operator** (would disrupt the active instance); the running app picks up this fix on its next natural restart.

author: zerolocker
body:
## What & why

Two coupled changes for the Living Art subscription:

### 1. Quarterly billing (fee reduction)
Charge **\$2.97 once every 3 months** instead of \$0.99/month. Stripe's 2.9% + \$0.33 is brutal on a sub-\$1 charge — batching to one transaction per quarter saves ~\$0.66/yr per subscriber with **zero change to the effective rate** (daily rate is identical).

The interval + amount live in the Stripe **Price** (`STRIPE_PRICE_ID`), not in code — so this PR adds the matching display data + guards:
- `PRICING` gains `billedAmount` (\$2.97), `billingPeriodMonths` (3), `billingNote` ("Billed quarterly"), and `freeItemCount` (100 — now a single source, replacing three hardcoded literals).
- `pricing-drift.test.ts` now asserts the Stripe Price is **\$2.97 / month / interval_count 3**, plus an offline invariant that `billedAmount == promoPrice × billingPeriodMonths`.
- `scripts/migrate-to-quarterly.mjs` — moves existing subscribers onto the new Price (active → immediate + prorated; trialing → at trial end; others skipped). **Dry-run by default.**
- `docs/stripe-webhooks.md` — batched-billing notes + a price-change/migration runbook.

### 2. Free-forward repositioning (copy)
Lead with the free tier (100 artworks, account required) and upsell **"the full gallery plus a new piece every day."** Applied consistently across:
- Site: hero, pricing section, CTA, footer, page metadata
- Shared `SubscriptionCard` (web account page + Electron app)
- Screensaver `UpsellOverlay.swift`
- Electron `UpsellBanner.tsx`

## ⚠️ Required ops steps (before/with deploy — not in this PR)
1. Create the **\$2.97 quarterly** Stripe Price (`unit_amount 297`, `interval=month`, `interval_count=3`) in **test and live**.
2. Repoint `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` (`.env.local` + Vercel) to the new Price and deploy.
3. Run `scripts/migrate-to-quarterly.mjs --apply` (test, then live) to move existing subscribers.

> The `pricing-drift` test **stays red until step 1–2 are done** — that coupling is intentional (it's the guard that stops displayed price from drifting from what Stripe charges). In CI it only runs if `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_PRICE_ID` secrets are set; otherwise it skips.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean (web, `packages/ui`, electron `typecheck:web`)
- Electron `UpsellBanner` test: updated to new copy, passing
- `pricing-drift` offline invariant: passing; the Stripe-connected assertion is red until the new Price exists (by design, see above)
- Site copy verified rendering in the browser preview

### **User description** **Resumen** Fix SSR del barrel @tryfusion-co/moon-solid para SolidStart. **Bug** El compilador de Solid emite delegateEvents(["eventName"]) a nivel de módulo por cada onClick={...}, onInput={...}, onKeyDown={...} u onPaste={...} en JSX. delegateEvents accede a document para registrar delegación global, por lo que se ejecuta apenas se importa el barrel — incluso en SSR, donde document no existe. Resultado: import { Button } from "@tryfusion-co/moon-solid" rompe SolidStart con "Client-only API called on the server side", aunque Button en sí mismo sea SSR-safe. **Fix** Migración de event handlers en el source (packages/src/components/): - onClick sobre elementos DOM (9 archivos: Dialog, Drawer, BottomSheet, TabList, SegmentedControl, Carousel, Pagination, Chip, Alert) → patrón ref + onMount + addEventListener. El compilador no emite delegateEvents para este patrón y el acceso a document queda confinado al cliente. - onInput / onKeyDown / onPaste (4 archivos: Checkbox, Switch, Select, Authenticator) → namespace on:input / on:keydown / on:paste. Attach directo vía addEventListener, sin delegación, sin hoist. author: brandon-coproduct
body:
**CI-efficiency audit fix #1 (top ROI).** The 4 Kani jobs in `kani-nightly.yml` cached `~/.kani` with key `hashFiles('.github/workflows/kani-nightly.yml')` — so *any* edit to the file (even a comment) invalidated the cache and re-downloaded the **~1 GB Kani toolchain** (~5–10 min/PR).

- **Cache key → pinned version:** `kani-toolchain-<os>-kani-0.67.0` instead of the workflow-file hash. Unrelated edits no longer bust it; an intentional Kani bump does.
- **Pin `kani-version: "0.67.0"`** on all 4 `kani-github-action` steps. The action defaulted to `latest`, which (a) silently changes what the verification gate checks (bad for a *proof* gate) and (b) makes a version-keyed cache meaningless. Pinning makes the proofs **reproducible**. Bump the version input + the cache-key suffix together when upgrading.

No behavior change today (`latest` == 0.67.0); first run on the new key is a one-time re-download, then warm. CI-config only.

author: bazf
body:
## Problem
The `test` pipeline failed on the `main` merge commit (after #4 merged):

```
src/lib/crypto.test.ts > crypto > returns null on the wrong password
AssertionError: expected '`>V' to be null
```

This is a **pre-existing flaky test**, unrelated to #4's changes. `decryptConfig` used raw AES-CBC, which has no key authentication — decrypting with the *wrong* password "succeeds" a small fraction of the time, returning plausible-looking junk instead of `null`. Because each encryption uses a random salt, the assertion passed on the PR branch and locally, then hit a bad salt on the merge commit.

Reproduced empirically: across 3,000 trials, **~0.7%** of wrong-password decryptions returned a non-null garbage string (e.g. `"*;:,!M"` — same shape as CI's `` `>V ``).

> The real app path (`resolveConfig`) was never affected — it's already guarded by `isValidConfig`. Only this direct crypto-layer assertion flaked.

## Fix
Seal a fixed integrity header (`GLX-OK`) inside the ciphertext, tagged with a `glx1:` envelope. A correct password reproduces the header on decryption, so a wrong password is now rejected **deterministically**.

**Backward-compatible:** the already-committed `ENCRYPTED_CONFIG` is untagged and can't be re-encrypted (no password), so it still decrypts via the legacy best-effort path — production is unaffected.

## Tests
- Strengthened the wrong-password test to loop across 50 random salts (locks in determinism).
- Added a regression test proving legacy (untagged) ciphertext still decrypts.

## Verification
- 75 unit tests pass; typecheck + lint clean.
- Looped crypto/config tests 20× (~1,000 wrong-password attempts): **0 failures** (old code would have produced ~7).
- `admin` + `locked` e2e pass (admin round-trip works with the new format; the committed config still gates).

author: nochallenge
body:
## What

`solid_bounding_box_volume(solid)` / `solid_bounding_box_volume_tol(solid, tol)` return the **AABB volume** `V_bbox = Δx·Δy·Δz` — the product of a solid's axis-aligned bounding-box extents. Re-exported from the crate root.

## Why

It's the occupancy volume used by spatial indices (octree / BVH node extents, broad-phase culling) and the denominator behind the fill ratio. A grep confirmed it was missing. It threads `solid_bounding_box`, and double-threads `solid_bounding_box_fill_ratio` (#297) + `solid_volume` via the exact identity `V_bbox = V / fill_ratio`.

## Test

`solid_bounding_box_volume_is_the_extent_product` (analytic):

- **box** `box_solid(2,4,6)` → `48` (and `= solid_volume`, since a box fills its AABB);
- **threads `solid_bounding_box`**: `V_bbox = Π extentᵢ` for box + sphere (rel tol `1e-9`);
- **double-threads `solid_bounding_box_fill_ratio` + `solid_volume`**: `V_bbox = V / fill_ratio` — exact even for the tessellated sphere since the volumes cancel (rel tol `1e-9`);
- **sphere** R=2 → `64` (the cube of side 2R, tessellation tol `1e-2`); the AABB volume bounds the solid volume.

Verified: `cargo test -p valenx-cad` (54 lib tests pass), `cargo clippy -p valenx-cad --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean). Backend-only (no UI change).

Research-grade; not production.

author: devitway
body:
## Problem

The ansible Galaxy proxy serves cached collection/version metadata for the full `metadata_ttl` window without checking upstream, then does an **unconditional full refetch** when stale. Unlike npm (#596), it never used the shared conditional-GET path — so it can neither cheaply revalidate nor capture upstream cache validators.

## Change

Route ansible's `proxy_json` through the existing shared `proxy_fetch_conditional` mechanism:

- On a stale read, send `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` from the stored validators sidecar.
- **304** → re-serve the cached body, bump its freshness (mtime), increment `PROXY_UPSTREAM_304_TOTAL{ansible}` + `PROXY_REVALIDATION_BYTES_SAVED_TOTAL{ansible}` — **no body downloaded**.
- **200** → cache the raw body **first**, then persist the fresh validators (body-before-sidecar ordering, so a sidecar never advertises freshness for an absent body).
- New `ansible.revalidate` config (default `true`) + `NORA_ANSIBLE_REVALIDATE`, mirroring npm. Fail-open: any error falls back to the existing serve-stale / full-fetch path.

## Upstream caveat

Self-hosted Galaxy NG / pulp_ansible does **not** emit HTTP validators on the versions-list endpoint — its `CollectionVersionViewSet.list()` uses a server-side value cache and returns a full `200`, never a `304`. So a 304 only occurs behind a validator-adding CDN such as galaxy.ansible.com; for self-hosted upstreams this degrades to a full fetch — **never worse than before** — and it future-proofs ansible for validator-capable upstreams.

## Test

`test_ansible_revalidation_304_serves_cache_no_body_download` drives the real handler: a wiremock that answers **only** when `If-None-Match` is present returns `304` (any full fetch would 404), and asserts the cached versions body is served with the 304 counter incremented.

`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --package nora-registry -- -D warnings`, and the full suite (lib 55 / bin 1328 / doctests) green locally.

body:
## Summary

When a collection folder catalog has a genre filter applied (for example, a "Movies" catalog filtered to **Romance**), tapping **View All** dropped the genre and loaded the entire unfiltered catalog. This PR carries the active genre through the View All navigation so the full-catalog screen stays filtered to the same genre that was shown in the folder row.

## Why

The folder row sections are built from `FolderTab`s, which already hold the selected `genre`. However:

- `FolderDetailRepository.getCatalogSectionsForRows()` mapped each `FolderTab` to a `HomeCatalogSection`, but `HomeCatalogSection` had no `genre` field, so the genre was silently dropped at that point.
- `onCatalogClick` (in `App.kt`) built a `CatalogRoute` from the section without setting `genre`, even though `CatalogRoute`/`CatalogScreen` already support a `genre` parameter that is forwarded all the way to `CatalogRepository.fetchCatalogPage(genre = ...)`.

Because the genre never reached `CatalogRoute`, `CatalogScreen` was opened with `genre = null` and requested the catalog unfiltered.

The fix preserves the existing genre value through that single broken link in the chain. No filtering logic is added or changed — it already existed end-to-end; it was just being lost during the folder → View All transition.

author: nightturtles
body:
## Problem

Signing in from the **native** app now correctly returns via the `cafelytic://auth-callback` deep link and establishes the session, but the page that launched the flow (the login modal or `login.html`) **hung on the logged-out view**. The user was actually signed in (navigating to any other page showed the logged-in state), yet the current page never re-rendered, so it looked stuck and needed a manual refresh.

## Cause

`handleDeepLink` in `src/lib/capacitor-bootstrap.ts` calls `exchangeCodeForSession` (or `setSession`) to establish the session, then navigates to `reset-password.html` for the **recovery** flow. For the **OAuth sign-in** flow it did nothing after the exchange. The launching page was rendered logged-out and has no reactive path for a deep-link-driven `SIGNED_IN` (notably `login.html`, which only checks the session on load), so it stayed on the logged-out view.

## Fix

After a successful **non-recovery** deep-link exchange, call `window.location.reload()`. The fresh load reads the now-persisted session and renders the logged-in state, the native analog of the web OAuth flow's full-page redirect to `login.html`. This is exactly the manual refresh that already worked, done automatically. Recovery deep links keep their existing navigation to `reset-password.html`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npx prettier --check`, and `npm run build` all pass.
- This path is native-only (`appUrlOpen` -> `handleDeepLink`) and cannot be exercised in a web preview; final verification is a device re-test of native Apple/Google sign-in: the page should land logged-in with no manual refresh.

## Summary

Stage 1 of replacing the numeric `level` with a deterministic, self-describing **delivery capability** model. This stage is **purely additive** — it introduces capabilities derived from the existing level and carries them on the event. No routing or authoring changes yet, so everything stays green.

The model: an event declares how it expects to be processed; that declaration resolves to explicit capabilities the rest of the system reads.

| level | backgrounded | durable | broker |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InProcess` | – | – | – |
| `Background` | ✓ | – | – |
| `Outbox` | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| `Broker` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

## Changes

- New `core/src/capabilities.ts`: `Capabilities { backgrounded, durable, broker }` + `capabilitiesFor(level)`.
- `build` resolves `capabilities` onto the envelope; `DispatchedEvent` carries them (optional, like the other envelope fields).
- Exported `capabilitiesFor` + `Capabilities` from the package entry; smoke proves capabilities resolve on a defined event through the entry.
- Extracted the `Level` enum into `core/src/level.ts` (re-exported from `event.ts`, so all existing imports are unchanged) to avoid a circular import — `capabilities` maps `Level` at module-eval while `event` builds with `capabilities`, so they can't import `Level` from each other.

## What's next (staged, each its own PR)

2. Delivery routes on `event.capabilities` instead of `event.level`.
3. `defineEvent` takes a `delivery` preset (`inline | background | durable | broker`) instead of `level`; migrate call sites.

## Token Grab DEX Paper Runner V1

Adds a paper-only runner that automates the existing DEX research loop for future unseen runs. This is **not** trading, does **not** touch live-harness, does **not** create real PLAN_ONLY trades, and uses no wallet/keys/swap/signing.

### Command
```
npm run token:dex-paper-runner --   --dex-config config/dex-ears.example.json   --signals-out data/token-grab/x-ears/presignals.dex.json   --runs-dir data/token-grab/dex-watch-runs   --minutes 10 --interval-seconds 60   --fake-bankroll 20 --position-size 1 --cycles 1 [--json]
```

### Per cycle
1. Pulls fresh DEX signals (same logic as `token:ears-dex`).
2. Saves signals to `--signals-out` (append).
3. Watches them for the window (same logic as `token:ears-dex-watch`).
4. Saves the watch run to `--runs-dir/run-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json`.
5. Runs candidate simulation (same logic as `token:dex-candidate-sim`).
6. Prints: cycle number, signals found, contracts watched, winners/losers/flat, candidate trades simulated, fake P/L, win rate, blocked count.

### Reuse
Pure orchestration — reuses `dexEars` (`buildDexEarsReport` + real fetchers), `dexWatch` (`runDexWatch`), `dexCandidateSim` (`buildDexCandidateSimReport`, which reuses `dexWatchCandidates` rules unchanged). No duplicated logic, no modified thresholds or candidate rules. Full dependency injection (endpointFetcher / watchFetchImpl / sleepImpl / nowFn / log) keeps it deterministically testable.

### Safety
Read-only / paper-only. No real trading, no `token:auto-paper`, no live-intent, no wallet/key/swap/signing, no `LIVE_EXECUTED`, no browser/scraping. Banner states PAPER ONLY / no live-harness gate changed / no PLAN_ONLY trade created; report carries `tradingExecuted: 0` / `noRealTradeSent: true`.

### Tests
`tests/tokenGrabDexPaperRunner.test.ts` — 11 tests: one paper cycle with mocked DEX signals/watch data, writes signals-out, saves watch report, simulates candidates + reports fake P/L, respects `--cycles`, report shape, and PAPER ONLY / NO REAL TRADE SENT / tradingExecuted: 0 / no trading-swap-signing terms. Full suite: 1276 passed.

### CLI smoke (real DEX Screener API, live 1-min window)
1 cycle → 3 signals found, 67 contracts watched, run saved to `run-20260607-222547.json`, 0 candidate trades (no +20% movers in window), fake P/L +$0.00, 23 blocked.

**E4.4** — CI/CD Integrations

Plan: `docs/e4.4-cicd-integrations-plan.md`
QA report: `docs/e4.4-qa-report.md`

## What's in this PR

**`infergen check --json`** — new flag that outputs a machine-parseable `CheckReport` JSON object to stdout:
```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "issue_count": 2,
  "new_untracked": [{"id": "evt_...", "name": "page_viewed"}],
  "unreviewed": [],
  "violations": [{"event_name": "pageViewed", "message": "...", "suggestion": "page_viewed"}]
}
```
Exit code unchanged (non-zero when issues found). Enables CI scripts to parse check results without screen-scraping.

**CI/CD recipe templates** — ready-to-paste configs in `docs/ci-recipes/`:
- `github-actions.yml` — complete workflow that runs `infergen check --json` and posts a formatted PR comment on every pull request
- `gitlab-ci.yml` — GitLab CI snippet with caching
- `circleci.yml` — CircleCI config with artifact storage

## QA Summary
**6/6 cases passed (100%) · GREEN**

| Feature | Result | Success Rate |
|---------|--------|-------------|
| `check --json` clean catalog → `ok: true` | PASS | 100% |
| `check --json` proposed event → `ok: false` + unreviewed array | PASS | 100% |
| `check --json` naming violation → violations array with suggestion | PASS | 100% |
| `check --json` new untracked → `new_untracked` array with id+name | PASS | 100% |
| `--json` and text mode coexist without regression | PASS | 100% |
| Full test suite GREEN (539 tests, 0 failures) | PASS | 100% |

author: ria8651
body:
Fixes #10570

# 👩🏻‍💻 What does this PR do?

The `LoaderRegistry` is built **once at server startup** and shared across every HTTP request (`server/server/src/lib.rs`). async-graphql's `DataLoader` coalesces concurrent `load_one` calls — including calls from *different* requests — into a single `load()` batch. So one `load()` slice can mix inputs from different stores, requisitions, periods and users.

Several loaders assumed a batch was homogeneous on a request-scoped field: they took `loader_inputs.first()` and applied that one value to the whole batch (or rejected mixed batches outright). Under concurrent multi-store load this either **errors** or **silently returns data keyed to the wrong store/requisition/period**.

This PR fixes the four affected loaders by grouping each batch by its request-scoped key(s) and querying per group, mirroring the pattern already used correctly in `clinician`/`name`/`master_list` loaders. Each fix adds a `#[tokio::test]` that drives a heterogeneous batch and asserts every input resolves to its own value.

## 🔍 Loader review — which loaders needed fixing

I audited every loader in `server/graphql/core/src/loader/` that keys on a request-scoped field (`store_id`, `requisition_id`, `period_id`, `customer_name_id`, …). Categories:
- **A — errors**: rejects a mixed batch with an error.
- **B — silently wrong**: applies `.first()`'s value to the whole batch, returning wrong/missing data with no error.
- **C — safe**: groups by all scoped keys (or keys results by a composite key), so mixed batches resolve correctly.

| Loader | Scoped field(s) | Before | Fixed here? |
|--------|-----------------|--------|-------------|
| `item_stats.rs` · `ItemsStatsForItemLoader` | `store_id` (+ payload) | **A** — returned `BadUserInput` "Cannot batch item stats across multiple stores" (the load-test symptom) | ✅ |
| `stock_line.rs` · `StockLineByItemAndStoreIdLoader` | `store_id` | **B** — `.first()` store; other stores' inputs resolved empty | ✅ |
| `available_volume_on_requisition.rs` | `requisition_id` | **B** — `.first()` requisition; other requisitions' inputs resolved empty | ✅ |
| `requisition_indicator_information.rs` | `store_id` + `period_id` | **B** — `.first()` store/period; other periods' inputs resolved empty | ✅ |
| `program_indicator_value.rs` · `IndicatorValueLoader` | `store_id` + `period_id` + `customer_name_id` | **B** (had a `TODO`) | ⏩ already fixed on `develop` (PR #11278), not in this RC base |
| `clinician.rs`, `name.rs`, `master_list.rs`, `program.rs`, `program_order_types.rs`, `item_store_join.rs` | `store_id` | **C** — already group by store / key compositely | — no change |
| `item_stock_on_hand.rs` | `store_id` | **C** — `equal_any(store_ids)`, keyed by `(store, item)` | — no change |
| `previous_encounter.rs` | per-input | **C** — queries each input individually | — no change |

## 💌 Any notes for the reviewer?

- **Behaviour change for `ItemsStatsForItemLoader`**: it previously returned a `BadUserInput` error for a multi-store batch; it now resolves all stores correctly. No more cross-store batching error.
- The grouping key for `item_stats` is `(store_id, payload)` where payload already covers `amc_lookback_months` + `period_end` — exactly the grouping the issue's example called for.
- `program_indicator_value` (the fifth loader from the same family) is intentionally **not** touched here: it was already corrected on `develop` and is out of scope for this `v2.16.05-RC` branch.
- Root cause not addressed here: the registry is still global, so a future loader could reintroduce this. A per-request `LoaderRegistry` would prevent the class of bug entirely — flagging as a possible follow-up rather than expanding this PR's scope.

# 🧪 Testing

Automated (run from `server/`):

- [ ] `cargo nextest run -p graphql_core loader::` → 5 pass, including the 4 new heterogeneous-batch tests:
  - `item_stats::tests::item_stats_loader_batches_across_stores`
  - `stock_line::tests::stock_line_by_item_and_store_loader_batches_across_stores`
  - `available_volume_on_requisition::tests::available_volume_loader_batches_across_requisitions`
  - `requisition_indicator_information::tests::requisition_indicator_info_loader_batches_across_periods`

Each test would fail on the old `.first()` code: the second store/requisition/period's input was absent (or the batch errored), so its `.unwrap()` would panic.

Manual (optional, reproduces the original report): drive concurrent `itemStockOnHand` queries against two different stores on a busy server and confirm no `Bad user input` responses.

# 📃 Documentation

- [x] **No documentation required**: internal performance/correctness fix, no user-facing behaviour change (besides removing an error that only occurred under concurrent multi-store load).

author: dbmaps
body:
### Motivation
- Provide an audit-only helper for V260 to evaluate whether Gridly should support direct in-app feedback submission without implementing it yet.
- Record findings about the existing email handoff workflow, Supabase readiness, privacy needs, and a minimal beta plan so the team can decide next steps.

### Description
- Added `gridlyBuildFeedbackSubmissionAudit()` to `js/app.js` and exposed it as `window.gridlyFeedbackSubmissionAudit?.()`; the helper inspects DOM hooks, existing helpers, Supabase availability, and returns the requested V260 audit shape including recommended data model, UX, and architecture options.
- Registered the helper with the existing audit registry via `exposeGridlyAuditHelper("gridlyFeedbackSubmissionAudit", ...)` so it appears with other audit helpers.
- Added `docs/audits/GRIDLY_V260_DIRECT_FEEDBACK_SUBMISSION_AUDIT.md` documenting quick summary, files reviewed, audit answers to the 10 questions, recommended architecture (Options A/B/C), minimal data model, UX, merge guidance, and exact testing steps.
- No Supabase schema/tables were created or modified and no direct feedback submission path was implemented; protected systems remain unchanged.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check js/app.js` to validate syntactic correctness; the check succeeded.
- Ran `git diff --check` to ensure no whitespace/format issues; the check succeeded.
- Changes were committed and a PR metadata payload was prepared; no runtime behavioral changes were implemented, and the audit function can be invoked in-browser via `window.gridlyFeedbackSubmissionAudit?.()` as documented.
